# EZD-348 · Fix: the EZD-120d B4 sign-out test passes in the CI gate run

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-348-1, AC-EZD-348-2
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** testing, ci
- **User-visible result:** nothing changes for Josh in the app; the phase 3 pull request's CI check stops failing on the offline sign-out test.
- Phase: 3 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Cause (section 2, E1-E4): B4 fails at spec line 200, `await page.goto('about:blank')`, with `Navigation to "about:blank" is interrupted by another navigation to "chrome-error://chromewebdata/"`. Line 199 (the `ezd_signed_out=1` cookie poll) had already passed. The browser carries out the app's `location.replace('/sign-in')` (`app/src/lib/auth/device-sign-out.ts` `signOutOnDevice`) with the network off, so that navigation fails and Chrome then loads its error page. The poll can pass as soon as the `/sign-in` request is sent, before the error page loads. On the CI runner the error page loaded after `page.goto('about:blank')` had started, which interrupted it. **This is a race in the test, not an app bug.** The fix: register a waiter for the error page before "Sign out anyway" is clicked, and wait for it before `about:blank`. B5 runs the same lines (219-227) and gets the same fix. Test file only; no app file changes.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts` (test-author) | change | none exported. Exactly these edits (line numbers on develop bc056236, before any edit): (a) line 5 `import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';` → `import type { Frame, Page } from '@playwright/test';`; (b) after line 115 (the closing `}` of `watchSignInCookies`), insert one blank line, then the block in Decided "Helper block"; (c) B4: directly after line 196 `await network.set(page, 'off');`, insert `const errorPage = offlineErrorPage(page);`; (d) B4: directly after line 199 (the `ezd_signed_out=1` poll), insert `await errorPage;`; (e) B5: directly after line 221 `await network.set(page, 'off');`, insert `const errorPage = offlineErrorPage(page);`; (f) B5: directly after line 224 (the `ezd_signed_out=1` poll), insert `await errorPage;`. Then run `pnpm exec prettier --write app/e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts`. Nothing else | the waiter in B2 (lines 155-157: `const saved = next.waitForResponse(…)` registered before the action, `await saved` after it); `page.on('framenavigated', (frame) => { if (frame === page.mainFrame()) … })` in `app/e2e/realtime.spec.ts` line 72 | `node scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-348 e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts` (5 passed) |
| 2 | none (builder) | none | none. The builder changes no file. In the worktree: merge develop in (L-053), `pnpm db:up`, `pnpm build`, then the step 1 command as its own Bash call, then `node scripts/gate.mjs .claude/worktrees/EZD-348 --full` three times one after another, and report each run's result plus its B4 line from the gate log (`✓ … EZD-120d B4 …`). A failure of any of these is a `PLAN-GAP` to the planner, with the Playwright error text. The builder changes nothing to make a run pass, and never re-runs a failed run hoping it passes | `vault/plans/EZD-338.md` Build step 2 | step 1 command; then the three `--full` gate runs (AC-EZD-348-1, -2) |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fix the app or the test | The test. The run failed at line 200, after line 199 passed. So the marker cookie was written under the http name `ezd_signed_out` and sent with `/sign-in`, which clears EZD-342's rename. The failing call is a browser navigation to `about:blank`, which reaches no server. EZD-346's origin check covers only state-changing `/api` requests, so it is cleared too | E1, E2; EZD-342 plan section 3 (http names unchanged); EZD-346 title (tickets.json) |
| How to wait | Wait for Playwright's `framenavigated` event on the main frame with `frame.url()` exactly `'chrome-error://chromewebdata/'`. Rejected: `waitForTimeout` (the ticket row: "a flaky wait is fixed, not re-run"); Playwright retries (config `retries` 0, ARCH Browser tests Config); opening a new page in place of `about:blank` (B5 calls `signInAs` afterwards, and the `signInAs` fixture is bound to the test's `page`, `app/test-harness/e2e/test.ts` lines 22-24) | E2 (the error page URL as Playwright reported it); ticket row Scope |
| When the waiter is registered | Directly after `network.set(page, 'off')` and before `signOut(page)`. No navigation happens between those two calls, and the error page can only follow the "Sign out anyway" click, so the waiter is in place before the page can load | spec lines 196-198, 221-223; `signOutOnDevice` (navigates only in its catch) |
| Order after the click | The cookie poll first (unchanged), then `await errorPage`, then `page.goto('about:blank')` (unchanged). The cookie poll stays the B4/B5 check that the marker was sent | EZD-120d plan section 4 B4 row; spec lines 199-200, 224-225 |
| Timeout on the waiter | No `timeout` option. The test timeout (60,000 ms, ARCH Browser tests Config) bounds it. If the error page never loads, B4 and B5 fail on the test timeout rather than racing | ARCH Browser tests (EZD-016a) Config |
| B5 | Gets the same edits (1e, 1f). It runs the same three lines, so it has the same race; it passed in run 42183681444 only by timing. Leaving a known gate-failing race in place goes against CLAUDE.md rule 17 | E3; CLAUDE.md rule 17 |
| Helper block (step 1b) | exactly these lines, nothing else: `// EZD-348: an offline sign-out's /sign-in navigation fails and Chrome then loads its error page. Wait for that page` / `// before navigating again, or the new page.goto is interrupted by it (CI run 42183681444). Register before the click.` / `const CHROME_ERROR_URL = 'chrome-error://chromewebdata/';` / `function offlineErrorPage(page: Page): Promise<Frame> {` / `  return page.waitForEvent('framenavigated', {` / `    predicate: (frame) => frame === page.mainFrame() && frame.url() === CHROME_ERROR_URL,` / `  });` / `}` (each `/` is a line break) | this plan; E2 |
| Test titles and describe | Unchanged. EZD-120d is phase 3, the same phase as EZD-348, so the ticket gate's `EZD_TEST_GREP` already runs B4 and B5. No test is added, so no new top-level `describe` (C9) | tickets.json `phase` for EZD-120d and EZD-348; ARCH Test scope (Q-0006) |
| Expected values in B4 and B5 | All unchanged (EZD-120d plan section 4 B4, B5 rows) | EZD-120d plan section 4 |
| Proof (AC-1, AC-2) | Three consecutive `node scripts/gate.mjs .claude/worktrees/EZD-348 --full` runs, each `GATE PASS` with B4 `✓`. `--full` runs the whole e2e suite with 4 workers, the load under which CI failed. After merge, the CI `gate` check on the phase PR is the Linux confirmation | AC-EZD-348-1, -2; `scripts/gate.mjs` line 60 (`--full`); ARCH Test scope (Q-0006) "What runs where" |
| Gate parts this touches (L-053) | `lint` and `typecheck` (one `.ts` spec file), `test:e2e` (B4, B5). No `build`, `test` (Vitest) or `perf` input changes | Build step 1 |

### Do not touch
`app/src/lib/auth/device-sign-out.ts`, `cookie-names.ts`, `app/src/proxy.ts` and every other app file (the app behaves as designed, E1); `app/test-harness/e2e/network.ts` and `test.ts` (EZD-016a harness, shared by every browser test); `app/playwright.config.ts` (`retries` stays 0); B1, B2, B3 and every line of `sign-out-outbox.spec.ts` that step 1 does not name; every other spec.

Ticket row (phase-01.md, EZD-348):
- Scope: Phase 3 PR CI `gate` check failed (run 42183681444): `test:e2e` fails on `app/e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts:185` `EZD-120d B4 Sign out anyway with the server unreachable leaves the marker, then the next request signs out`; typecheck, lint, test, build and perf passed and the log shows no other failing e2e test. The log carries no error text. Find the cause first (run the spec as the gate does, read the Playwright error), then fix the app or the test (a flaky wait is fixed, not re-run; the cookie rename of EZD-342 and the origin check of EZD-346 are the first suspects).
- Done when: `sign-out-outbox.spec.ts` B4 passes in three consecutive full e2e runs of the gate; the full gate is green.
- Depends on: EZD-120d, EZD-342 · Spec ref: rule 17; CI run 42183681444

### Done-when list (L-057)
1. Import line 5 adds `Frame` (1a). 2. Helper block inserted after `watchSignInCookies` (1b). 3. B4 waiter registered (1c). 4. B4 `await errorPage` (1d). 5. B5 waiter registered (1e). 6. B5 `await errorPage` (1f). 7. Prettier run. 8. ui-run 5 passed. 9. Three `--full` gate PASS runs reported. 10. No other file in the diff.

## 2. Sources
- E1: CI run 42183681444 artifact `gate-logs/gate.log`, downloaded with `gh run download 42183681444` (lines on that log). Line 11271: `✘ 204 [desktop] › e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts:185:7 › … B4 … (3.8s)`. Lines 11332-11344: `Error: page.goto: Navigation to "about:blank" is interrupted by another navigation to "chrome-error://chromewebdata/"`, `- navigating to "about:blank", waiting until "load"`, `> 200 |     await page.goto('about:blank');`. Line 11364: `259 passed (4.3m)`, 1 failed. `gate-failures.log` in the same artifact carries the same error line. So the error text does exist; the ticket row's "no error text" refers to the job's console output.
- E2: the URL `chrome-error://chromewebdata/` in E1 is the one Playwright gives the error page's main-frame navigation. The same URL is what `framenavigated` reports, because both come from the same commit event.
- E3: the same artifact, line 11288: B5 `✓` (11.6s). B5's lines 219-227 repeat B4's lines 193-202.
- E4: `app/src/lib/auth/device-sign-out.ts` `signOutOnDevice`: in its catch it writes the marker cookie, then calls `env.location.replace('/sign-in')`. `app/test-harness/e2e/network.ts` `set('on')` evaluates `navigator.onLine` on every page of the context.
- `app/e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts` at develop bc056236 (EZD-120d, 531c3720): lines 5, 101-115, 155-157, 185-250.
- EZD-120d plan section 3 (`signOutOnDevice`, the `[data-confirm]` dialog) and section 4 (B4, B5 rows; Q-0503, Q-0581). EZD-342 plan section 3 (http cookie names unchanged).
- Spec: `vault/spec/sections/03a-working-copy-and-saves.md` (Working copy and saves) is the ticket's spec file. This ticket changes no behaviour it describes (KNOWN-LIMITS 1: spec_files is best-effort; the Spec ref is rule 17 and the CI run).
- Decisions: none for this area. CLAUDE.md rules 16 and 17.
- Lessons applied: L-034, L-036, L-050, L-053, L-057, L-062; the EZD-343 ui-run proof rule; EZD-338 plan as the pattern for a test-only fix.
- Research: no retriever was dispatched and no research report covers this ticket.

Architecture: Browser tests (EZD-016a)

## 3. Interface contract
| Kind | Name or path | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| file | `app/e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts` | only test file changed; exports nothing (before and after) |
| constant (file-local) | `CHROME_ERROR_URL` | `'chrome-error://chromewebdata/'` (E1, E2) |
| function (file-local) | `offlineErrorPage(page: Page): Promise<Frame>` | resolves with the main frame when it loads the URL `CHROME_ERROR_URL` (`page.waitForEvent('framenavigated', { predicate })`). No timeout option. It rejects only on the test timeout or when the page closes, and that fails the test |
| test names | B4, B5 | titles and the `describe('EZD-120d sign-out with queued edits')` unchanged |
| harness used | `network.set`, `signInAs` | from `app/test-harness/e2e/test.ts`, unchanged (EZD-016a) |

## 4. Tests
Test count: 0 new, 2 edited (B4, B5), 5 in the file. B1-B3 unchanged. Each edited row keeps every EZD-120d expected value; the only new step is the wait.
| Test | AC | Type | Input | Expected value | Source of the expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B4 (edited: 1c, 1d) | AC-EZD-348-1, AC-EZD-348-2 | browser | As now (EZD-120d B4). The interleaving: the waiter from `offlineErrorPage` is set up after network off. "Sign out anyway" makes the app's `/sign-in` navigation fail offline. The test waits on `errorPage` until the main frame reports `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`, and only then calls `page.goto('about:blank')` | the cookie poll is true (`ezd_signed_out=1`); `errorPage` resolves; then URL `/sign-in`, no `sb-` cookie, no `ezd_signed_out` cookie, `queued` 1. Old code: failed with the interruption error in run 42183681444 (E1). New code: `goto` starts only after the error page has loaded, so the interruption cannot happen. The wrong fix it rejects: a waiter registered after the click, or none (that is the old code) | EZD-120d plan section 4 B4; E1, E2 |
| B5 (edited: 1e, 1f) | AC-EZD-348-2 | browser | As now (EZD-120d B5), with the same wait as B4 before `about:blank` | unchanged: `posts` 0 during B, `queued` 1, no dialog, then `posts` 1 with a 200 save | EZD-120d plan section 4 B5; E3 |
| Proof run | AC-EZD-348-1, AC-EZD-348-2 | browser (gate) | `node scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-348 e2e/sign-out-outbox.spec.ts`, then three consecutive `node scripts/gate.mjs .claude/worktrees/EZD-348 --full` runs | ui-run: `5 passed`. Each gate run: `GATE PASS`, and its log has B4 `✓` | AC-EZD-348-1, -2; Decided "Proof" |

No deterministic red-first run exists: the race depends on timing (E1, E3). The test-author confirms the edit compiles (`pnpm run typecheck`) and passes ui-run. The full runs are the proof.

## 5. Visual checklist
None (no screen changes).

## 6. Proposed wording
None.

## 7. Security review
security-review: no (one test file; no app, auth, permission, data or API code changes).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
Low: one test file gains about 12 lines, every edit is dictated in section 1, and the cause is shown by the CI log. Test-author Sonnet 5.5 / medium (Playwright event typing); builder Haiku 5.5 / high (runs commands only, changes no file).

## 9. Dependencies
EZD-120d (the spec file and `signOutOnDevice`), EZD-342 (marker cookie name; cleared as the cause, E1). Missing from the ticket row: EZD-016a (the `network` and `signInAs` fixtures in `app/test-harness/e2e/`; merged, phase 0). EZD-346 was named as a suspect only; it is cleared (Decided "Fix the app or the test") and is not a dependency.
Risks: a full gate run takes several minutes, and three are needed. If Chrome on CI ever skips the error page (a navigation aborted rather than failed), `offlineErrorPage` would wait until the test timeout. Any such failure goes back as a PLAN-GAP; it is never re-run until it passes.

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-349 · Fix: every 401 from requireApiSession carries Cache-Control: no-store

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-349-1, AC-EZD-349-2
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** auth, security, api
- **User-visible result:** none on screen; a "signed out" answer from any app route is never kept in a browser or proxy cache, so a stale "you're signed out" reply cannot be replayed after signing back in.
- Phase: 4 (row in `vault/tickets/phases/phase-02.md`) · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Data: none (no table, column, migration or RLS change).

### Build steps
Verify commands run from the worktree root. `VITEST` below means `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run` (architecture Tests; package name from `app/package.json`).
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/src/server/auth/session.ts` | change | unchanged: `requireApiSession(): Promise<Session \| Response>`. ## 1. What to build

Lane already in use | The script stops with `BLOCKED: <file> is held by a live process` and exit 2 when any of `ezdraft-gate-lane1.lock`, `ezdraft-gate-lane2.lock`, `ezdraft-lane1.lease`, `ezdraft-lane2.lease` in `<tmp>` holds a live pid. The builder then reports BLOCKED with that line; it never deletes a lock or lease. | docs/architecture.md Build lanes (EZD-172): gate lock, lease file, "Run a lane by hand outside a gate only with that lease file holding your shell's pid" |
| D6. Counted run | Lane 1 is brought up (`db:up`) before the first lane 2 gate starts, so run 1 begins as soon as that gate holds its lock. A run counts as a pass when vitest exits 0 and the lane 2 gate lock holds a live pid both before and after it. Exit 0 with the lock gone at the end is `not counted` and the loop tries again, at most 8 attempts. A non-zero exit is a failed run whatever the lock, and ends the loop. When the lock is gone before a run, the script starts a new lane 2 gate; it starts at most 3 in all, and needing a 4th ends the script with `BLOCKED: the lane 2 gate ended before the runs finished, 3 times` (exit 2). | Ticket Done-when; this plan |
| D7. Outcome | Exit 0 and `RESULT: 5 counted passes, 0 failed runs` → report PASS with the summary lines and every log path. Exit 2 (`BLOCKED`) or 3 (`TIMEOUT`) → report BLOCKED with that line and every `lane2-gate-<G>.log` summary line; no counted runs are claimed. Exit 0 with any failed run, or fewer than 5 counted passes after 8 attempts → report FAIL with the `Tests` line and the first assertion error of each failed run; make no edit; the orchestrator sends it to the planner as a plan gap (the fix depends on which assertion fails; F1-F2 show neither test counts fixture rows). | Ticket Scope ("Reproduce it first") |

Cause of the 2026-11-02 failure: pinned lists, not shared database state. T19 reads no database and T18's two lists are code; dd1e24c3 (EZD-110a) added the notification table and the notification_email job before EZD-292 (73a1e2a4) listed them, and the scoped gate skipped both tests (second D-016 row, EZD-350).` `<date>` is the run date from `summary.txt`. | F1-F3; vault/debt.md row format |
| D9. Lane 2 gate result | Recorded, not judged: the lane 2 gate's own `GATE PASS` or `GATE FAIL` line goes in the report. The ticket's gate is step 2. | CLAUDE.md rule 12; Ticket Done-when |
| D10. Postgres notice | The `schema "ezd_test" already exists, skipping` NOTICE vitest prints is expected and is not a failure (seen by the planner at F4). | F4 run output |
| D11. Clean-up | Every exit after the lease is written goes through `finish`: it stops lane 1 with `pnpm db:stop` once `db:up` was attempted, waits up to 2,700 s for the started lane 2 gates, then prints each gate log's `GATE` line and its `exit <code>`. The lane 2 gate is never killed; still running after 2,700 s gives `TIMEOUT: …` and exit 3, and that gate stops its own stack when it ends. The trap removes the lease on every exit. If the Bash timeout kills the script, the lease's pid is dead, which the next lane gate treats as free, and it stops the left lane 1 stack. | docs/architecture.md Build lanes (EZD-172): lane stacks stop at each gate's end (Q-0354 (a)); stale lane stacks and dead lease pids (Q-0367 (b)) |
| D12. A lane 1 stack already up | A running lane 1 stack with no live gate lock and no live lease is stale by the lane rules, and the next lane gate would stop it; the script's `db:up` reuses it and resets it. No extra check. | docs/architecture.md Build lanes (EZD-172), Stale lane stacks (Q-0367 (b)) |

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# EZD-351 five-run check (vault/plans/EZD-351.md). Scratch file, never committed.
set -u
WT=/Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/.claude/worktrees/EZD-351
T=$(node -p 'require("os").tmpdir()')
OUT="$T/ezd-351"; mkdir -p "$OUT"; : > "$OUT/summary.txt"
L1="$WT/.lanes/lane1"
say() { echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"; }
live() { p=$(tr -d '[:space:]' 2>/dev/null < "$1"); [[ "$p" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] && kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null; }
GATES=0; UP=0
finish() {
  code=$1; shift; say "$*"
  if [ $UP -eq 1 ]; then EZD_LANE=1 SUPABASE_WORKDIR="$L1" pnpm db:stop > "$OUT/lane1-db-stop.log" 2>&1; say "lane 1 stack stopped (exit $?)"; fi
  for s in $(seq 1 2700); do [ -z "$(jobs -rp)" ] && break; sleep 1; done
  if [ -n "$(jobs -rp)" ]; then say "TIMEOUT: lane 2 gate still running after 2700 s; it stops its own stack when it ends"; code=3; fi
  for g in "$OUT"/lane2-gate-*.log; do [ -f "$g" ] && say "$(basename "$g"): $(grep -E '^GATE (PASS|FAIL)' "$g" | tail -1) $(tail -1 "$g")"; done
  exit $code
}
for f in ezdraft-gate-lane1.lock ezdraft-gate-lane2.lock ezdraft-lane1.lease ezdraft-lane2.lease; do
  if live "$T/$f"; then say "BLOCKED: $f is held by a live process"; exit 2; fi
done
echo $$ > "$T/ezdraft-lane1.lease"
trap 'rm -f "$T/ezdraft-lane1.lease"' EXIT
start_gate() {
  if [ $GATES -ge 3 ]; then finish 2 "BLOCKED: the lane 2 gate ended before the runs finished, 3 times"; fi
  GATES=$((GATES+1))
  (cd "$WT" && EZD_LANE=2 node scripts/gate.mjs "$WT" > "$OUT/lane2-gate-$GATES.log" 2>&1; echo "exit $?" >> "$OUT/lane2-gate-$GATES.log") &
  say "lane 2 gate $GATES started"
  for i in $(seq 1 120); do live "$T/ezdraft-gate-lane2.lock" && return 0; sleep 1; done
  finish 2 "BLOCKED: lane 2 gate $GATES took no lock in 120 s"
}
cd "$WT"
UP=1
if ! EZD_LANE=1 SUPABASE_WORKDIR="$L1" pnpm db:up > "$OUT/lane1-db-up.log" 2>&1; then finish 2 "BLOCKED: lane 1 db:up failed"; fi
say "lane 1 values: $(EZD_LANE=1 SUPABASE_WORKDIR="$L1" node scripts/db/local.mjs lane)"
start_gate
PASSES=0; FAILS=0; N=0
while [ $PASSES -lt 5 ] && [ $FAILS -eq 0 ] && [ $N -lt 8 ]; do
  N=$((N+1))
  live "$T/ezdraft-gate-lane2.lock" || start_gate
  say "run $N start, lane 2 gate lock live"
  (cd app && EZD_LANE=1 SUPABASE_WORKDIR="$L1" pnpm exec vitest run src/server/db/rls.audit.test.ts src/server/jobs/handlers.test.ts -t 'T18 exemption and grant lists match the catalog|T19 every registered handler has a run-twice test' --reporter=verbose) > "$OUT/run-$N.log" 2>&1
  code=$?
  if live "$T/ezdraft-gate-lane2.lock"; then lock=live; else lock=gone; fi
  if [ $code -ne 0 ]; then FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); verdict=failed; elif [ $lock = live ]; then PASSES=$((PASSES+1)); verdict=counted; else verdict="not counted"; fi
  say "run $N exit $code, lane 2 gate lock $lock at end, $verdict;$(grep -E '^ +Tests ' "$OUT/run-$N.log" | tr -s ' ')"
done
finish 0 "RESULT: $PASSES counted passes, $FAILS failed runs"
```

# EZD-353 · Fix: captureTraffic does not block the page's loopback Realtime websocket

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-353-1, AC-EZD-353-2
- **Complexity:** low (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, realtime
- **User-visible result:** none in the app; the browser tests that record a page's traffic now see the Realtime connection and the bell's requests exactly as a normal page makes them, so debt D-085 closes.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

Cause (probe P1, section 2): `captureTraffic` fulfills every loopback request from Node (`route.fulfill`), the page's document included. A fulfilled document has no IP address, so Chromium 156 puts it in the public address space, and its Local Network Access check refuses the page's websocket to `127.0.0.1` (`net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_CHECKS`). Websockets are not routed by `context.route`, so the check runs. hub.ts then reconnects and fetches `/api/realtime/token` again (D-085). An unrouted `127.0.0.1` page is in the loopback space and is not checked. Fix: on Chromium, `captureTraffic` grants `local-network-access` to the context before it routes; P1 shows the socket then opens, both for a new page and for a page that existed before the grant.

Data: none.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/test-harness/e2e/traffic.ts` | change | none new; `captureTraffic(context: BrowserContext, opts?: TrafficOptions): Promise<Traffic>` unchanged. Add header text H1 after the existing header block (before the `import` lines). First statement of the `captureTraffic` body, before `const fetchLimit`: `if (context.browser()?.browserType().name() === 'chromium') { await context.grantPermissions(['local-network-access']); }` with the one-line comment `// EZD-353: see the header (Chromium Local Network Access).` above it. Nothing else in the file changes. | the file itself (EZD-163 header style) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run test-harness/e2e/traffic.test.ts`; `pnpm run typecheck`; `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app run lint` |
| 2 | `app/test-harness/e2e/README.md` | change | none. In `## Traffic checks`, insert sentence S1 directly before `Every other test and the app run unrouted.` | the paragraph itself | `grep -c "EZD-353" app/test-harness/e2e/README.md` prints `1` |
| 3 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | none. In `### Browser tests (EZD-016a)`, bullet **Traffic checks**: insert sentence S1 directly before `Every other test and the app run unrouted.` | the bullet itself | `grep -c "EZD-353" docs/architecture.md` prints `1` |
| 4 | regression runs (builder, after the test-author's files exist) | run | none | none | each as its own Bash call: `node scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-353 e2e/traffic.spec.ts`, then the same with `e2e/money-pages.spec.ts`, `e2e/gate-secret.spec.ts`, `e2e/projects.spec.ts`, `e2e/projects-header.spec.ts`, `e2e/harness.spec.ts`, `e2e/sign-in.spec.ts`; every one exits 0 |
| 5 | gate | run | none | none | `node scripts/gate.mjs .claude/worktrees/EZD-353` green |

H1 (traffic.ts header, exactly these five comment lines, nothing else):
```
// EZD-353 (vault/plans/EZD-353.md; debt D-085): a document fulfilled from Node has no IP address, so Chromium puts it in
// the public address space and its Local Network Access check refuses the page's loopback Realtime websocket
// (net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_CHECKS). On Chromium, captureTraffic first grants local-network-access to the
// context, which gives the routed page the loopback reach an unrouted 127.0.0.1 page has. WebKit has no such check and
// refuses the permission name, so it gets no grant.
```
S1 (README and architecture, exactly this sentence, nothing else): `On Chromium it first grants \`local-network-access\` to the context (EZD-353): a document fulfilled from Node has no IP address, so Chromium's Local Network Access check would refuse the page's loopback Realtime websocket; WebKit has no such check and refuses the permission name.`

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |

None (no user-visible text).

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. The change is a permission grant inside the test browser's context only; no app code, table, route, auth or money path changes. The net guard still refuses every non-loopback request (traffic.ts `isLoopback` fall-through).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
low: the cause is proven by probe, the fix is one guarded call in one harness file plus two doc sentences, and the risk is limited to the seven `captureTraffic` specs, which step 4 runs. Test-author: Sonnet; builder: Sonnet.

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-117a, EZD-117b (done): B1, B4 and their unrouted counts.
- Missing from the row: EZD-163 (done; author of traffic.ts and its contract) and EZD-110b (done; the bell, D16 counts). Both merged, so nothing waits.
- Regression set: the row names six specs; `projects-header.spec.ts` (B1 search, B9 no access) also calls `captureTraffic` and is added to step 4.
- Risks: a spec that relied on the routed page being refused local-network access would change; none does (step 4 runs all seven). The grant exists only in test contexts; production is served from a public origin to a public Supabase, where the check does not apply. A future Chromium that renames the permission would make `grantPermissions` throw, and U1/T1 and every `captureTraffic` spec would fail by name, not silently.

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-354 · Build system: the gate's checks run as the separate ezdraft macOS user, so code they run cannot reach Josh's keychain or files

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-354-1, AC-EZD-354-2, AC-EZD-354-3 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md` rows 578-580)
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** tooling, scripts, security, testing
- **User-visible result:** on Josh's Mac every check the gate runs (install, typecheck, lint, tests, build, browser tests, perf) runs as the `ezdraft` user from a copy outside Josh's home, so code in a ticket can no longer read Josh's files, keychain, ssh agent or Claude sessions; CI is unchanged.
- Phase: 1 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## Josh's steps
Only Josh can do these (account, sudo, Docker Desktop settings). Order: steps 1 and 2 before the build; step 3 after the orchestrator's row O1. Probe 2026-11-06: none is done yet (`ls -led /Users/josh` has only `group:everyone deny delete`; `/etc/sudoers.d` is empty).

1. **Close your home folder to ezdraft.** Both users are in group `staff` and `/Users/josh` is `drwxr-x---` josh:staff (`~/.claude` is `drwxr-xr-x`), so ezdraft can list and read most of it. In Terminal (no sudo; you own the folder):
   `chmod +a "user:ezdraft deny list,search,add_file,add_subdirectory,delete_child,readattr,readextattr,readsecurity" /Users/josh`
   Check: `ls -led /Users/josh` shows a `user:ezdraft deny list,add_file,search,…` line.
2. **Let the gate switch to ezdraft without a password, for one command only.** `sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/ezdraft-gate`, type exactly this line, save:
   `josh ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /bin/launchctl asuser 502 /usr/bin/sudo -n -u ezdraft -- /usr/bin/env *`
   Check: `sudo -n /bin/launchctl asuser 502 /usr/bin/sudo -n -u ezdraft -- /usr/bin/env -i /usr/bin/id -un` prints `ezdraft`. Then check it allows nothing else: `sudo -n /bin/launchctl asuser 502 /bin/sh -c id` must be refused (`sudo: a password is required`), and `sudo -n -l` shows no `NOPASSWD` line but this one.
3. **Limit what Docker containers can see** (after the orchestrator says row O1 is done). Docker Desktop → Settings (gear) → Resources → File sharing: remove `/Users`, `/Volumes`, `/private`, `/tmp`, `/var/folders`; add `/Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/.claude/worktrees` and `/Users/ezdraft/gate`; click Apply & restart. Why: the Docker VM mounts exactly the listed folders (probe 2026-11-06: a privileged container saw `/host_mnt/Users`, `/Volumes`, `/private`, `/tmp`, `/var/folders`), so today any container reads your whole home.

## 1. What to build

None

## 6. Proposed wording
None in the app. Console texts are fixed in section 3 (F-lines); the runbook holds Josh's steps verbatim.

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas: permissions (OS user boundary, sudoers rule, file ACLs), data access (Josh's home, keychain, Docker host mounts).
Unsandboxed steps (the gate is an excluded command, `scripts/unit-sandbox.json`; L-045, L-047):
| Command (as) | Sandbox-writable inputs it reads | Checked at the moment of use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| trusted-git `ls-files`, `read-tree`, `add`, `write-tree`, `commit-tree` (Josh) | worktree files, worktree git state | C8 before `add`; hooks and fsmonitor off (TRUSTED_CONFIG); temporary index (D3) |
| git `push` to `<L>/tree` with C7 (Josh sends, ezdraft receives) | worktree objects and refs | only `refs/gate/snapshot`, develop and `phase-*` tags sent (C11); the target path is only stat'ed |
| `userSpawn` commands: checks, `cat`, `id`, `test`, `mkdir`, `rm`, git (ezdraft) | run copy | run as ezdraft, which cannot read Josh's home (P5, L1) |
| canary write (Josh) | none | delete, then exclusive create (D2a) |
| relay CLI and `/bin/chmod +a` (Josh) | `/Users/Shared/ezdraft-gate` | C10 at P2; C15 refuses a non-socket at listen |
| relay forwarding to Josh's Docker engine (Josh) | every Docker API request ezdraft's code sends | none: a plain forwarder (Q-0614); Docker's file sharing (Josh's step 3, D18) bounds the host reach, as for every sandboxed unit (KNOWN-LIMITS unit sandbox hole (2)) |
| `copyBack` writes (Josh) | `<dir>/perf-results` | folder lstat, `O_NOFOLLOW` per file (C12) |
| `pgrep -x -u ezdraft loginwindow` (Josh) | ezdraft's process list | exit status only, absolute path; a spoof skips only F10 and WebKit then fails as before (D19) |
| ezdraft's GUI login session (ezdraft) | Josh types his password after leaving it | Josh's session is not reachable from it on the review's checks; runbook step 4 orders the key before the password; KNOWN-LIMITS states the rest |
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer yes · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a new OS security boundary with a root sudoers rule, a copy-and-sync path, a relay process and changes to the gate every ticket depends on; its proof needs the real machine (O2). Test-author: claude-opus-5-5. Builder: the orchestrator (Opus), section 1.

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-344 (gate-env; done), EZD-345 (trusted-git; done). Missing from the ticket row: EZD-172 (lanes, `scripts/db/lane.mjs`; done) and Josh's steps 1-3 (no ticket; they gate the build and O2).
- Build-system freeze (CLAUDE.md rule 18): Q-0611 (a) (`vault/questions/QUESTIONS-answered.md:355`): Josh's creating the ezdraft user for Q-0602 (a) is his yes (why and cost recorded there); ledger entry c86f68c8.
- Risks: every user-mode gate adds a snapshot, a push, a `pnpm install` and, on lane 0, one stack restart (D16), likely tens of seconds; after step 3 a stack started from the main checkout cannot mount its templates (stacks start from worktrees and run copies only); a Node or pnpm bump needs row O1 (b)/(c) again (F6 says so); until Josh's steps are done every local gate fails at F2, F4 or F5 (fails closed); tests that read Josh's home or `~/.claude` would fail as ezdraft and show in O2.

## 10. Open questions
- Q-0610 (answered-agent, `QUESTIONS-answered.md:354`): build with `launchctl asuser 502` as written; O1 (d)-(f) and O2 test it on the machine; if either fails, the builder stops and the orchestrator raises a new question ((a) a launchd daemon as ezdraft, its own ticket; (b) plain `sudo -u` only with a KNOWN-LIMITS line).
- Q-0611 (answered-agent, (a)): section 9.
- Q-0614 (answered-agent, security-reviewer 2026-11-06): Neither (a) nor (c). A symlinked bind or an exec into a container the relay did not create can hand ezdraft the raw engine, so no path-text check bounds it, and (c) checks a path ezdraft can write that Docker resolves later (CLAUDE.md rule 18). EZD-354 ships a plain forwarder (C15, C19, R1, R2); its Docker access is unchecked and bounded by Docker's file sharing (Josh's step 3, before O2), as every sandboxed unit's already is (KNOWN-LIMITS unit sandbox hole (2); scripts/unit-sandbox.json allowUnixSockets); that is a strict subset of today's reach. The policy relay moves to a follow-up ticket that depends on EZD-354 and needs Josh's yes per rule 18: it acts only on objects it labelled at create, resolved to their full ID; it binds only from a read-only folder Josh owns, written from the snapshot; gate stacks get their own project names; units reach Docker through the same relay.

None. The drawing list is data; EZD-207b draws it.

## 6. Proposed wording
None. `Room N` and `NAME · N SF` are decided (Q-0568; Q-0570; board S03).

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. Pure geometry and a schema shape; no route, table, permission or money. The schema change narrows what a save accepts (strict room fields).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor yes (outlines, areas, rounding) · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a new planar-face algorithm (joins, faces, face-line offsets, holes) that every room, area and takeoff ticket builds on, plus a schema migration and the shared font table (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
- Row: EZD-203, EZD-202, EZD-238 (all done; their merged code is the contract).
- Not in the row: none needed. Q-0592 (a): after this plan, EZD-221 is re-validated to add its reconcile test (U12).
- Dependents: EZD-205b (override clearing in `reconcileRooms`, `wallIds`), EZD-210a (calls `reconcileRooms`), EZD-221, EZD-236 (room data shape, version 3), EZD-207b (draws the label with both fonts), EZD-235 (caches `roomAreaSqFt`).
- Files: 14 source/doc + 5 new + 5 edited test files = 24 (about-20 guide); 21 tests. Not split again: the label and rooms parts share the schema bump, and each part pays the per-ticket overhead (Josh 2026-10-22).
- Risks: floating point at the half-SF boundary (axis-aligned intersections are exact; T5 checks 123); O(walls²) joins on the benchmark's 758 walls per floor until EZD-235.

## 10. Open questions
- Q-0612 ((answered-agent (a), 2026-11-06)): A wall or box of walls inside a room that does not divide it (a stub with a free end, a free-standing wall, a closed chase or closet box touching no wall of the room) is undecided: (a) the room's outline goes around it, so its footprint is not floor area and a free-standing one is cut out of the room as a hole, while a closed box is also its own room (recommended: it follows "outline on the inside finished face", Q-0559, and keeps takeoff areas true; no schema change, the hole is joined into the one boundary), (b) it is ignored and the room's area counts the floor under it (a box's floor then counts twice), (c) the room around a free-standing box is not detected until a wall joins the box to the room.
- Q-0613 ((answered-agent (a), 2026-11-06)): When a partition splits a room, which part keeps its id and name, and how are new rooms numbered: (a) the larger part keeps them, the other is a new room, and when a removed partition merges two rooms the larger stored room keeps its name and the other is deleted (recommended); (b) the part holding the old room's label point keeps them; (c) both parts become new rooms. Numbering: (a) one more than the highest `Room N` in the model, so a number is never reused (recommended), or (b) the lowest unused number.

# EZD-207a · Plan canvas: renderer, drawing, grid, pan and zoom

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-207-1, AC-EZD-207-4 (lines, arcs, fills, hatches), AC-EZD-207-6 (skeleton and failure clauses), AC-EZD-207-7 (Plan tab, no panels, disclaimer only), AC-EZD-207-8 (pan and zoom), AC-EZD-207-9 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:757-762`)

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canvas place | One `<canvas>` fills the whole frame behind header, cards and status bar (`backdrop` slot), so the grid runs behind the cards as on the board and later scenes draw into the same context; with it the frame drops its CSS grid, without it (loading, failed, no access, not found, `/dev` pages) the CSS grid stays. Input comes only from `PlanInputSurface` in the canvas region | board line 47; 11 rules 4, 6; ARCH-ES |
| Zoom scale | C3: 100% = 32 CSS px per foot (one board square = 1 ft at the board's 100%); limits 5% and 1600%; `clampPpi`: non-finite → `ZOOM_100_PPI`, else clamp | board lines 47, 169; Q-0568 (zoom limits) |
| View maths | `regionToModel = { x: v.x + p.x / v.ppi, y: v.y - p.y / v.ppi }`; `modelToRegion = { x: (p.x - v.x) * v.ppi, y: (v.y - p.y) * v.ppi }`; `panBy`: `{ x: v.x - dx / ppi, y: v.y + dy / ppi, ppi }`; `zoomAt`: `ppi' = clampPpi(ppi * factor)`, the model point under `p` stays under `p`; a non-finite or `<= 0` factor, or non-finite `dx`/`dy`, returns the same `view` object | S03 Canvas interactions ("Zoom toward cursor"); P207 |
| Wheel | `px = deltaY * (deltaMode 1 → 16, deltaMode 2 → 800, else 1)`; factor `= Math.exp(-px * (ctrlKey ? 0.01 : 0.002))`; a wheel at region point `p` gives `zoomAt(view, p, factor)`; a wheel with or without ctrl zooms (a trackpad pinch arrives as ctrl+wheel; a plain wheel or trackpad scroll is "Scroll"); `preventDefault()` on every wheel on the surface (listener `{ passive: false }`) | S03 ("Scroll / pinch: Zoom toward cursor"); P207 Scope (camera and input) |
| Pan | mouse or pen: right button (`button === 2`) drag, or left (`button === 0`) drag while Space is held; `panBy` by the pointer's movement since its last event. Touch: while exactly two touch pointers are down, each move pans by the change of their centroid and then `zoomAt(centroid, distance / previousDistance)` (ratio 1 when the previous distance is 0); a third touch is ignored. Middle button: nothing. Any `pointerType` other than `touch` is handled as mouse | S03 ("Space-drag, right-drag or two-finger drag: Pan"; "pinch") |
| Space | `keydown` with `key === ' '` on `keys` (the window) sets held unless `target` is a typing target (tag `INPUT`, `TEXTAREA`, `SELECT`, or `isContentEditable === true`); `keyup` `' '` and `blur` clear it; no `preventDefault` (a focused button still works) | S03; 11 rule 4 |
| Context menu | `contextmenu` on the surface: `preventDefault()`; the app's own menu comes with its later ticket | S03 Right-click row; Q-0500 |
| Pointer hand-off | A receiver set by `setPointerReceiver` gets: `down` for a mouse or pen press with `button === 0` that is not a pan, and for the first touch; `move` for every move of a mouse or pen pointer that is not panning (hover included) and of that delivered touch; `up` when a delivered pointer lifts; `cancel` on `pointercancel` of a delivered pointer and when a second touch starts while one touch is delivered; native `click` and `dblclick` with `button === 0` only when the last `pointerdown` on the surface was delivered. Pan gestures never reach it. `model` = `regionToModel(view, screen)`. No receiver: left input does nothing | P207 Scope (seams); P210 Ledger notes; S03 |
| Pointer capture | `surface.setPointerCapture?.(pointerId)` on every `pointerdown`, inside `try`/`catch` (ignore a throw) | 11 rule 4 (a drag continues over the cards) |
| Cursor | `getCursor()` is the last `pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`wheel` point of any pointer in region px (`clientX - rect.left`, `clientY - rect.top`), `null` before the first; kept after the pointer leaves | P209 C17, D-Pos |
| Region rect | The input reads `surface.getBoundingClientRect()` when created and on `pointerdown`, `pointerenter` and `wheel`, and keeps it for moves; the controller also takes it from `setRegionRect` | 11 rule 4 (no layout read per move) |
| View changes | No React state changes on any pointer, wheel or key event. `setView` (handle and input) ignores a view with a non-finite field, clamps `ppi`, and does nothing when `x`, `y` and `ppi` all equal the current ones; otherwise it stores it, sets the camera and grid, calls `invalidate()` once and then each camera listener once with the new view, in subscription order | 11 rule 4; P210 Ledger notes |
| Fit | `fitView`: `null` bounds (or any non-finite field) → `ppi = ZOOM_100_PPI` with model (0, 0) at the region centre. Else `bw = maxX - minX`, `bh = maxY - minY`, `aw = max(1, width - 2 * FIT_MARGIN_PX)`, `ah = max(1, height - 2 * FIT_MARGIN_PX)`, `ppi = clampPpi(min(bw > 0 ? aw / bw : Infinity, bh > 0 ? ah / bh : Infinity))`, `ZOOM_100_PPI` when both are 0; the bounds centre goes to the region centre | Q-0568 ("Fit on an empty model"); P207 (first view Fit) |
| First view | The controller fits once, the first time `setRegionRect` gives width and height above 0; after that edits and resizes never refit. `handle.fit()` fits again to the current list; it does nothing while the region has no size | P207 Scope (camera and input) |
| Grid | `gridStepIn(ppi)` = the first of `GRID_STEPS_IN` with `step * ppi >= GRID_MIN_PX`, else 1200; lines at model multiples of the step; colour `--ez-canvas-grid` on clear colour `--ez-canvas`; drawn by the grid shader below (no line buffer, so a pan or zoom rebuilds nothing) | Q-0568 ("plans decide grid meaning"); board line 47; 11 rule 4 |

Grid shader (`scene.ts`, `ShaderMaterial` on `PlaneGeometry(2, 2)`, `depthTest: false`, `depthWrite: false`). Vertex: `void main() { gl_Position = vec4(position.xy, 0.0, 1.0); }`. Fragment (uniforms set by `setGrid` and `setViewport`; `uColor` is `tokenRgb('--ez-canvas-grid')` written unconverted, because a `ShaderMaterial` adds no colour-space step):
```glsl
uniform vec2 uOrigin; uniform float uPpi; uniform float uStep; uniform float uDpr; uniform float uBufferHeight; uniform vec3 uColor;
void main() {
  vec2 css = vec2(gl_FragCoord.x, uBufferHeight - gl_FragCoord.y) / uDpr;
  vec2 m = vec2(uOrigin.x + css.x / uPpi, uOrigin.y - css.y / uPpi);
  float dx = (m.x / uStep - floor(m.x / uStep)) * uStep * uPpi;
  float dy = (ceil(m.y / uStep) - m.y / uStep) * uStep * uPpi;
  if (dx >= 1.0 && dy >= 1.0) discard;
  gl_FragColor = vec4(uColor, 1.0);
}
```
`uOrigin` = `regionToModel(view, { x: -offset.x, y: -offset.y })` (the model point at canvas px 0, 0). Nothing else.

security-review: no. The canvas reads the model P120c already loaded; no route, table, policy, permission or money field.
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a new WebGL renderer, merged buffers and input with no React render, which every later drawing ticket builds on (PROCESS.md section 4; Slice 4 Risks). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
- From the row: EZD-012 (a, b, c), EZD-202, EZD-238, EZD-017, EZD-020, EZD-120c, EZD-015 (a, b, c), EZD-016a, EZD-027 (all done).
- Missing from the row: EZD-205a (required `roomLabelPt` view member, room label `text` items; merged b1ce6b81), EZD-203 (`createWallData`, test data; done), EZD-024 (`captureBrowserError`; done), EZD-136 (status bar disclaimer, asserted in B7; done).
- Risks: three and R3F join the editor entry (B8 holds 500 KB; the perf check's `js-size:editor` still measures `/dev/shell` until EZD-207c). Each model edit rebuilds the whole drawing list on the CPU, uploading only changed batches; per-object caching is EZD-235's (11 rule 2). `dpr` 2 frame times: EZD-207c.

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-205b · Closure gap, absorb and keep out of square

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-205-2, AC-EZD-205-3, AC-EZD-205-4, AC-EZD-205-6 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:751-754`, stage-0)
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** geometry, data-model, api, security, testing
- **User-visible result:** none on screen yet; EZD-210 builds the gap box, pick mode and Keep out of square on these functions, and a kept room is logged as `room.closure_overridden` when it is saved.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned; re-validated 2026-11-06 against merged EZD-205a (b1ce6b81, fix 524ff885)

## 1. What to build
`G` = `packages/geometry/src`, `A` = `app/src`. P205a = `vault/plans/EZD-205a.md`, merged as b1ce6b81 (fix 524ff885); where the plan and the merged code differ, the code governs (section 3 "imports" row). Data: no table, migration, SQL or money field; no `schema_version` change (the room's `closureOverride` field is P205a's, version 3). One new `ObjectIssueCode`.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `G/rooms/test-utils/fixtures.ts` (test-author) | change | adds `openChain`, `applyChanged` (section 3); the header's "Nothing else is exported" sentence names them as EZD-205b's | `chain` in the same file (merged) | `pnpm run typecheck` |
| 2 | `G/rooms/closure.ts` | new | `GAP_LIMIT_IN`, `GapReport`, `ClosureReport`, `gapDisplayIn`, `findClosures` (section 3) | `G/walls/joins.ts` (pure, level filter, case-insensitive ids) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/rooms/closure.test.ts` |
| 3 | `G/rooms/absorb.ts` | new | `AbsorbResult`, `absorbGap` | `G/walls/move.ts` (result union, `changed` walls, never mutates) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/rooms/absorb.test.ts` |
| 4 | `G/rooms/sync.ts` | change | adds `nextRoomNumber`; `reconcileRooms` gains the gap rule (Decided "Reconcile with gaps"); signature unchanged | itself | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/rooms/sync.test.ts` |
| 5 | `G/rooms/override.ts` | new | `KeepOutOfSquareResult`, `keepOutOfSquare` | `G/rooms/sync.ts` (returns a `RoomReconcile`) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/rooms/override.test.ts` |
| 6 | `G/rooms/index.ts` | change | appends `export * from './closure'`, `'./absorb'`, `'./override'` after the three merged lines; the header comment gains "EZD-205b adds closure, absorb, override" | itself | `pnpm run typecheck` |
| 7 | `G/schema/index.ts` | change | `ObjectIssueCode` gains `'override_other_user'` | itself | `pnpm run typecheck` |
| 8 | `A/lib/events/registry.ts` | change | `EVENTS['room.closure_overridden'] = { kind: 'internal' }` after `'cleanup.deleted'`; `EventPayloads['room.closure_overridden']: { roomId: string; gapIn: number; userId: string }` | the `model.saved` rows | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/lib/events/registry.test.ts` |
| 9 | `A/server/model/model.ts` | change | `closureOverrideCheck`; `saveObjects` gains a required 4th parameter `appUserId: string`; `SaveResult` ok member gains `overridden` (section 3) | `loadModel` in the same file (session-client select, `if (error) throw error`) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/server/model/model.test.ts` |
| 10 | `A/app/api/projects/[id]/objects/route.ts` | change | none new; passes `p.session.appUserId`; emits (Decided "Emit") | the `model.saved` emit block in the same file | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run 'src/app/api/projects/[id]/objects/closure-event.test.ts'` |
| 11 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | `### Rooms (EZD-205a)`: add "`closure.ts` (`findClosures`: closed, gap up to 12", open, per wall chain), `absorb.ts` (`absorbGap`), `override.ts` (`keepOutOfSquare`); `reconcileRooms` keeps an override while its gap is unchanged (EZD-205b)". `### Events`: add "`room.closure_overridden` (`internal`, `{ roomId, gapIn, userId }`) is emitted by `POST /api/projects/[id]/objects` once per saved room whose closure override is new or changed against its stored row (EZD-205b)". `### Model working copy (EZD-120a)` Server and routes bullet: add "A room whose closure override is new or changed must name the saving user (`override_other_user`, 400 `invalid_object`); the stored rows are read for those rooms only (EZD-205b)". Nothing else | those sections | none (L-041) |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level and walls | `findClosures` keeps walls whose `data.level` equals `level` case-insensitively and whose length is over 1/64" (`wallLength`, `COMPARISON_TOLERANCE_IN`); joins from `findWallJoins` (`G/walls/joins.ts`) over those walls | P205a Decided "Reconcile scope"; P203 Degenerate walls |
| Wall ends | For each kept wall end: `corners` = its `corner` joins at that end; it is **free** when there are 0 corners and no `tee-into` at that end; **linked** when exactly 1 corner, no `tee-into`, and the partner end also has exactly 1 corner; else **branched**. `tee-on` and `cross` joins never change an end | 00e Wall chain, Join; Q-0598 (a) |
| Components | Walls connected through linked ends. A component with any branched end: no report. Every end linked and ≥ 3 walls: `closed`. Exactly two free ends: a chain (`gap` or `open`). Anything else: no report. Reports in the order of each component's first wall in the input array | Q-0570 (three or more walls); 03g |
| Walk order | Chain: start at the free end that is a wall's `start`; if both or neither free end is a `start`, start at the terminal wall whose id sorts first (lower-case); a one-wall chain starts at its `start`. Walk to the far end, follow the link, repeat. `wallIds` in walk order (ids as stored). Closed: start at the wall whose id sorts first (lower-case), leave by its `end` | P205a Decided `closureOverride` ("gap from the last wall end to the first wall start") |
| Gap | `P0` = first free point, `Pn` = last free point. `gap = P0 − Pn` (vector, inches, not rounded); `sizeIn = Math.hypot(gap.x, gap.y)` | Q-0569 (c) straight line; 03g (computed values not rounded) |
| Kind | `gap` when walls ≥ 3, `sizeIn <= GAP_LIMIT_IN` (12, exact compare, inclusive) and a gap boundary exists; otherwise `open`. Closed is decided by the corner join (`pointsEqual`, 1/64" inclusive), so a free-ended chain never misses by 1/64" or less | Q-0562; Q-0568; Q-0570; 09j Closure |
| Display | `gapDisplayIn(sizeIn) = Math.max(1, Math.floor(sizeIn * 16 + 0.5)) / 16` | Q-0568 (to 1/16"); Q-0570 (rounds to 0 → 1/16"); 03g halfway up |
| Gap boundary | Add one virtual wall `{ id: 'closure-gap', type: 'wall', data: { geometry: { start: Pn, end: P0 }, status: 'existing', level: <first chain wall's level>, attributes: { thickness: 0, thicknessSide: 'center', height: DEFAULT_WALL_HEIGHT_IN, topCutToCeiling: false, bearing: false, layers: [] } } }` to the level's walls and call P205a `findRoomOutlines`. `boundary` = the outline whose `wallIds` contain `'closure-gap'` with the smallest `outlineAreaSqIn`, ties to the first. None → kind `open`. Zero thickness puts both faces on the closing line (`wallFaceLines`, `G/walls/wall.ts`: `t = 0` gives both offsets 0); every other wall keeps its inside finished face. Checked 2026-11-06 on the merged `findRoomOutlines` (`G/rooms/outlines.ts`: vertices merge wall ends within 1/64", so the virtual wall joins the chain without a corner join; `wallIds` keeps `'closure-gap'`): CL1 rows 2, 3, 4, 8 give 17280 sq in, CL3 row 6 17220.125, angled 8640, CL5 (a) 17280, (d) 8370, SY1 (b) 18000 | 09j Keep out of square ("closes the outline across the gap"); Q-0559; P205a `findRoomOutlines` |
| Parallel | A chain wall is parallel to the gap when `abs(gap.x * uy − gap.y * ux) <= COMPARISON_TOLERANCE_IN`, with `(ux, uy)` the wall's unit direction (the end moves at most 1/64" off its line). `parallelWallIds` in walk order. Empty = a miss in both directions: only Keep out of square is offered. This decides the split's "both directions" for angled walls | Q-0568; Q-0569 (c); 09j Closure row 6; S02 Decisions |
| Absorb steps | (1) the `gap` report on the level of the wall `gapWallIds[0]` (case-insensitive) whose `wallIds` equal `gapWallIds` as a lower-case set, else `no_gap`; (2) `wallId` a wall in `objects`, else `wall_not_found`; (3) in the report's `wallIds`, else `not_in_chain`; (4) in `parallelWallIds`, else `across_gap`; (5) build the change; any changed wall with `wallLengthProblem` → `zero_length` / `too_long` with that wall's id (changed order); (6) every join `findWallJoins` gave a changed wall before must still be given after (same `kind`, ends, `otherId` case-insensitive), else `join_lost` with that wall's id. Refusals 1–4 carry the picked `wallId` | 09j Absorbing rows 3–5; Q-0570; P203 `wallLengthProblem` |
| Absorb change | Picked wall: its walk-later end moves by `gap`. Every chain wall after it in walk order moves both ends by `gap`. A wall outside the chain whose end has a `tee-on` join onto a moved (not the picked) wall moves that end by `gap` (09e stretch, as `moveWall` does for `tee-on`). `changed` = chain walls in walk order, then those walls in object order; data `{ ...w.data, geometry: { start, end } }` with fresh point objects | 09j Absorbing rows 1–2; 09e; P203 `moveWall` |
| Keep steps | (1) the `gap` report as Absorb step 1, else `no_gap`; (2) `closureOverrideSchema.safeParse({ who, when, gap: report.gap })`, else `invalid_override`; (3) the first stored room in object order on that level that pairs with `report.boundary` (`sameBoundary`, or `pointInRing(interiorPoint(b), s)` / the reverse, P205a step 2 test) → `update: [{ ...s, data: { ...s.data, geometry: { boundary: copy }, closureOverride } }]`; none → `create: [{ id: newId(), type: 'room', data: { geometry: { boundary: copy }, status: 'existing', level, attributes: { name: \`Room ${nextRoomNumber(objects)}\` }, closureOverride } }]`; `delete: []` | Q-0568; Q-0570; 09j Keep out of square; P205a Create |
| `nextRoomNumber` | Moves P205a's Create rule out of `reconcileRooms` unchanged: the largest integer in any room name, all levels, matching `/^Room ([1-9][0-9]*)$/`, or 0, plus 1. `reconcileRooms` calls it and adds 1 per further create | P205a Decided Create |
| Reconcile with gaps | Replaces P205a "Reconcile scope"'s override sentence; in merged `G/rooms/sync.ts` that is the step (2) guard `if (… closureOverride === null) updated.add(c.si)` and the step (4) guard `if (s.data.closureOverride === null) del.push(s.id)`, both removed. Outline list = `findRoomOutlines` outlines, then each `gap` report's boundary (report order). Merged steps (1) and (2) pair every stored room of the level over that list. Real outline with an overridden room, paired in step (1) or (2) → update: boundary, `closureOverride: null`. Gap outline with an override whose `gap` `pointsEqual` the report's → kept (update the boundary only when not `sameBoundary`). Gap outline with an override whose gap differs, or with no override → update: boundary, `closureOverride: null` (no update when already null and `sameBoundary`). Step (3) creates for real outlines only; a gap outline with no room makes none. Step (4) deletes every free stored room, overridden or not | AC-EZD-205-4; 09j Keep out of square ("the override clears", not the room); P202 stable ids; Q-0570 (gap box until resolved) |
| Override check | `closureOverrideCheck`: for each room in input order with a non-null override: stored = `stored.get(id.toLowerCase())` (`undefined` = no row). Unchanged = stored non-null and `who` equal lower-case, `when` equal as strings, `gap.x` and `gap.y` `===`. Changed or new with `who.toLowerCase() !== appUserId.toLowerCase()` → `invalid` `{ id, issue: 'override_other_user' }`; changed or new by the saving user → `overridden` `{ roomId: id, gapIn: Math.hypot(gap.x, gap.y) }`; unchanged → neither, whoever `who` is | split proposal (EZD-205b event scope); CLAUDE.md rule 18; S02 Events |
| saveObjects order | Parse (existing); any parse issue returns before the read. Then rooms with a non-null parsed `closureOverride`: none → no read. Else read in chunks of 100 ids: `client.from('model_object').select('object_id, type, schema_version, data, deleted').eq('project_id', projectId).in('object_id', chunk)`, the awaited call being `.in(...)`, chunks one after another in change order; `if (error) throw error` (route answers 500 `db_unavailable` through `reportRouteFailure`, nothing written). Map key = lower-case `object_id`; value `null` when `deleted` (so any override on a restored room is new), when `parseStoredObject` fails or when not a room; else its `closureOverride`. ## 5. Visual checklist
None (no screen changes).

## 6. Proposed wording
None. Refusals are reason codes (EZD-210 words the messages, 09j Absorbing row 3); the 400 reuses `error.invalid_input`.

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas: API, data access (the save route reads stored rows under the member's RLS before the rpc; it refuses an override whose `who` is not the saving user; an unbounded id list is read in chunks).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor yes (gap sizes, display rounding, absorb lengths, areas) · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: new chain and gap geometry with seven refusal paths, a reconcile rule change in a shared module, and a change to the shared save route that reads stored rows and refuses data (PROCESS.md section 4: data integrity, API). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
- Row: EZD-205a (`findRoomOutlines`, `outlineAreaSqIn`, `roomAreaSqFt`, `sameBoundary`, `pointInRing`, `interiorPoint`, `reconcileRooms`, `RoomObject`, `RoomReconcile`, `closureOverrideSchema`, `ClosureOverride`, fixtures; done, b1ce6b81, signatures re-validated in section 3), EZD-120a (route, `saveObjects`, conflict rule), EZD-022 (registry), EZD-102 (`requireApiPermission`), EZD-024 (`reportError`).
- Missing from the row: EZD-203 (`findWallJoins`, `wallFaceLines`, `wallLength`, `wallLengthProblem`, `moveWall`, `DEFAULT_WALL_HEIGHT_IN`; done), EZD-202 (`pointsEqual`, `parseStoredObject`, `ObjectIssueCode`; done). Both reach this ticket through EZD-205a.
- Dependents: EZD-210a (calls `findClosures`, `absorbGap`, `keepOutOfSquare`, `reconcileRooms`; formats `displayIn`), EZD-311, EZD-235.
- Risks: (1) closed 2026-11-06: the merged `findRoomOutlines` accepts the zero-thickness `layers: []` wall and gives the planned boundaries (Decided "Gap boundary"). (2) `findClosures` calls `findWallJoins` for every wall of a level (n²); with `findRoomOutlines` on each edit it may press the 50 ms typed-commit budget on the benchmark project (11 Performance); EZD-235 owns caching and EZD-236 measures. (3) A room whose gap changes keeps its id and name with no override and its label still shows while the gap box is up (Decided "Reconcile with gaps").

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-207b · Plan canvas: zoom stack, hover and text

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-207-2, AC-EZD-207-3, AC-EZD-207-4 (text items), AC-EZD-207-8 (Fit and hover), AC-EZD-207-10 (as its `showObject` seam) (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:763-767`, stage-0)
- **Complexity:** high
- **Areas:** ui, canvas, performance, testing
- **User-visible result:** the Plan tab has Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit to screen at its top right; the wall under the cursor turns blue; room labels such as `KITCHEN · 165 SF` show on the plan and grow and shrink with the zoom.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned; re-validated 2026-11-06 against EZD-207a 8a55e56a, EZD-205a b1ce6b81, EZD-205b 44cd595f

high: glyph-atlas text with two fonts in WebGL, and hover on the shared spatial index, both under the no-React-render rule and inside EZD-207a's controller (PROCESS.md section 4; Slice 4 Risks). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.

None.

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. Pure modules; no route, table, policy, permission or money field; the override's `who` is checked by P205b's save route.
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor yes (lengths, turns, areas, gap sizes) · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: two interaction state machines over geometry with many refusals, writing model data every later ticket reads, on four unmerged contracts (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
- Row: EZD-205a, EZD-205b, EZD-209, EZD-206, EZD-203, EZD-201, EZD-202, EZD-120b, EZD-012a. Missing from the row: EZD-010b (icon pipeline; done). All dependencies are done and merged on develop (EZD-205a b1ce6b81, EZD-205b 44cd595f, EZD-209 4deba37d); this plan was re-validated against them on 2026-11-06 (section 2).
- Q-0612 and Q-0613 are answered-agent (a) (`QUESTIONS-answered.md:356-357`; phase-auditor) ; EZD-205a, which implements them, is done: a wall or box inside a room that does not divide it is cut around; on a split the larger part keeps the id and name, the other is a new room numbered one past the highest `Room N`. W9 and M1 still assert areas and change order only: which id survives is EZD-205a's tested behaviour, not this ticket's.
- Moved from EZD-210b: the two rail icons and the E1 edit; EZD-210b keeps `ads_click`, `rotate_right`.
- For EZD-210b: P206 snaps angles to every multiple of 45°, so `angleDeg` can be 0, 135 or 180, which Q-0589 (a) does not draw ("90°" or "45°" only); EZD-210b's plan settles that look. Part b also sends `release` at the `press` point for a click under its drag threshold, passes `drawingWallIds` = `state.walls` ids, and runs Esc in order typed box → pick mode → tool.
- Performance: `toModelObjects` parses only rooms and the level's walls, once per committed edit, never per pointer move (11 rules 2, 4); typed commits must show within 50 ms (11 Performance).

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-355 · Build system: gate and unit Docker calls go through a policy relay that acts only on objects it created

## Split proposal
Why: after two tightening passes the whole plan is 49,992 characters (`outline.mjs --sizes`), touches 21 files and needs 26 tests, over all three limits (plan-ticket step 3; Josh 2026-10-22). It splits along the ticket's own seam: the gate's relay (AC-1, AC-2, AC-4) and the units' use of it (AC-3). Part a stands alone: until part b lands, units keep today's socket (KNOWN-LIMITS unit sandbox hole (2), unchanged), and the gate already removes their stack before it starts its own. The draft below these parts is kept for the part planners (each writes its own plan in its own unit); its row, contract and test IDs are named per part. Planner probe findings (section 2 of the draft) serve both parts.

### EZD-355a · Build system: the gate's Docker calls go through a policy relay that acts only on objects it created
- Scope: EZD-354's forwarder becomes the policy relay (route allow-list, HostConfig rules, a label at create, actions only on labelled objects by full ID, label-filtered lists and prunes, binds only to read-only copies of the email templates written from the snapshot under `/Users/Shared/ezdraft-gate/binds`); the gate (user mode) writes the copies, removes the lane's builder stack first, names its stacks `ezdraft-gate[-lane<n>]` through `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`, and stops its stack at the end on every lane; the lane scripts follow the name; probe P1; Josh's step J1; docs and KNOWN-LIMITS K1. Draft rows O0 (paths of rows 1-10), P1, 1-10 (row 2: C15 only), 13 (without D9), 14, 15 (K1 only), J1, O3; D1-D8, D10; C1-C15 (C13 without `clearForUnit`), C17-C20; tests T1-T17, T19, T22-T26 (23); S1-S4.
- Done when: A call through the relay on a container, volume, network or exec it did not create is refused (test). A bind source outside the relay's read-only folder, a symlink in it, Privileged or another host-access setting is refused (test). A gate stack has its own project name and the gate removes the lane's builder stack before it starts (test). The full local gate passes through the relay (full gate).
- ACs: AC-EZD-355-1 and AC-EZD-355-2 move here with the texts above; AC-EZD-355-4 moves here; one new AC for the third sentence (`gen_acs.mjs`).
- Depends on: EZD-354. Complexity: high. About 16 files.

### EZD-355b · Build system: sandboxed units reach Docker only through the policy relay
- Scope: a unit relay (scope `unit`, template copies from a snapshot of the unit's worktree at each create) that the launcher starts before each unit and without which no unit starts; `scripts/unit-sandbox.json` allows only its socket and sets `DOCKER_HOST`; before a unit, leftovers of a dead gate on its lane are removed; a one-time cleanup of stacks made before the relay and a launcher restart (Josh's yes); KNOWN-LIMITS K2. Draft rows 11, 12, O2, O4, 13 (the D9 bullet), 15 (K2); D9; C13 `clearForUnit`, C16; tests T18, T20, T21 (3).
- Done when: A sandboxed unit's Docker socket is the relay (test). The launcher starts no unit when the unit relay does not start (test). Before a unit, a dead gate's stack on its lane is removed and a live gate's is not (test). A build unit's `pnpm db:up` passes through the unit relay (launcher run).
- ACs: AC-EZD-355-3 moves here; three new ACs for the other sentences (`gen_acs.mjs`).
- Depends on: EZD-355a. Complexity: high (sandbox and launcher). About 6 files.

## Draft for the part planners (not a plan; IDs as above)
- **ACs:** AC-EZD-355-1, AC-EZD-355-2, AC-EZD-355-3, AC-EZD-355-4
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** tooling, scripts, security, testing
- **User-visible result:** code that the gate or an agent runs reaches Docker only through a checker that refuses anything able to reach your files or another run's containers.
- Phase: 1 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: split proposal

## 1. What to build
Builder: the orchestrator in fix mode for every non-test row (`scripts/` root is builder-denied, `.claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs:114`; gate.mjs, unit-sandbox.json, gate-docker-relay.mjs are in `REPAIR_NEVER_FILES`, `scripts/launcher-idle.mjs:83`; as EZD-354 section 1). Tests first (test-author). Merge develop before the gate (L-053); at risk: `lint`, `test`, every Docker-using check (O3). Relay tests listen on a unix socket, which a sandboxed shell refuses (`listen EPERM`, planner probe): run verify commands unsandboxed. `V` = `node --test scripts/process/docker-relay.test.mjs`.
Open before the build: EZD-354 merged, its step 3 and O2 done.
Done when: rows 1-12 as written; S1-S4; rows 13-15 text; P1 recorded; J1 checked; O2-O4 passed; `vault/handoff/LAUNCHER_FIX.md` deleted after the merge.

| Where | Text |

| `docs/runbook.md`, Gate user step 4 (J1) | **4. Let Docker see only the relay's copies** (after the orchestrator says EZD-355 row 12 is done). Docker Desktop → Settings (gear) → Resources → File sharing: add `/Users/Shared/ezdraft-gate/binds`; remove `/Users/ezdraft/gate`; keep `/Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/.claude/worktrees`; click Apply & restart. Why: the gate's and the agents' containers now mount only read-only copies of the email templates from that folder, so nothing else needs sharing with them. |
| console, gate.log, launcher log | C12's message and log line, D1's `docker relay` line, the two F9 texts (section 3) |

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas: permissions (who may act on which Docker objects), data access (host files containers reach), API (the Docker Engine API the relay filters).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes (Fable 5.1, high).
Threat class (L-029): a Docker API call that hands a caller host files, host namespaces, the engine, or another caller's containers. Fail-closed: an unknown route, HostConfig key, bind path or label is refused; the relay is the real control for ezdraft and units, Docker Desktop file sharing (J1) behind it. Josh-side steps read only git objects and Docker API JSON, never a path in the run copy or a worktree (D5; L-045, L-047): `materializeTemplates` reads blobs by id through `trustedGit`; the unit relay's `makeSnapshot` is EZD-354's accepted gate step; `stopStacks`/`clearForUnit` read API JSON only.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
high: a new security control (an HTTP-level Docker API filter with hijacked streams) across the gate, the launcher and the lane scripts. 21 files, 12 of them one- to three-line edits; the new logic sits in `gate-docker-relay.mjs`; 26 tests. Not split: a units part would be about five files and repeat the probe, fix mode, J1 and the full gate (Josh 2026-10-22: fewer, fuller tickets). Test-author Sonnet 5.5 / medium (exact table); builder: the orchestrator in fix mode, Opus 5.5 (PROCESS.md section 4, high).

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-354 (row): `gate-user.mjs`, `gate-docker-relay.mjs`, user mode, the run copy, `RELAY_DIR`, `makeSnapshot`, `checkRelayDir`, `GateUserError`, F-lines; its step 3 and O2.
- Not in the row: Josh's step J1; the launcher restart after the merge (Josh's yes; `run.mjs` starts the unit relay); EZD-172 and EZD-287 code (merged). EZD-016a not needed (no screen).
- Risks: a Docker call the suite needs that C3 or H1-H4 refuse fails the gate (O3 finds it, PLAN-GAP); between merge and launcher restart units cannot reach Docker, so O2 and the restart follow the merge at once; a stack started before O2 blocks units until O2 or the lane's next gate; each lane 0 gate now starts and stops its stack (EZD-354 D16 already restarted it); a test running the real CLI on its own workdir with the gate's environment must drop `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID` (S1, S2; O3 finds any other).

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-210b · Drawing tools on the plan

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-207-6, AC-EZD-207-7 (tools and rail clauses), AC-EZD-210-1, -2, -3, -5, -7, -8, -9, -10, -11 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:787-797`, stage-0)
- **Complexity:** high
- **Areas:** ui, testing, canvas, geometry
- **User-visible result:** a rail with Wall and Room rectangle; W or R (or a click) picks a tool, clicks and typed lengths draw saved walls with a cobalt rubber band and snap marker, rooms show as `ROOM 1 · 120 SF`, and a chain that misses its start shows a red gap pill with Pick the wall that absorbs it and Keep the room out of square.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

Short names: **T** = `app/src/editor/tools/`; **G** = `@ezdraft/geometry`; **P210** = `vault/plans/EZD-210.md` Part EZD-210b; **P210a**, **P207a**, **P207b**, **P209**, **P206**, **P205a**, **P120b**, **P120c** = those plans' section 3 and the rows named; **S02B**, **S03B** = `vault/mockups/html/project/S02Import.dc.html`, `S03Plan.dc.html`; **GAP** = walls (0,0)→(144,0)→(144,120)→(0,120)→(0,0.5) (09j Closure row 2: 1/2" gap).

security-review: no. UI only; walls, rooms and the override "who" save through EZD-120a's save route and EZD-205b's check, which enforce Edit model and the viewer server-side. No route, table, policy, permission or money field.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: pointer, touch and keyboard wiring onto the WebGL canvas under the no-render rule, with ten browser tests of the drawing flow (PROCESS.md section 4; Slice 4 Risks). About 13 source files plus 5 generated icon files and 9 test files; kept whole (one screen, already split once). Test-author Sonnet 5.5, builder Opus 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
Row: EZD-210a, EZD-207a, EZD-207b, EZD-209, EZD-120c, EZD-010b (icons), EZD-016a (harness; visual checklist). None.

# EZD-356 · Fix: the iPad long-task count during pan stays at 0 in the gate run

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-356-1, AC-EZD-356-2, AC-EZD-356-3
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, perf, scripts
- **User-visible result:** The build is unblocked (EZD-209, the typed dimension bar, resumes). Every perf run now lists when each long task happened during the pan and how loaded the Mac was. Nothing on screen changes (Q-0618 (c): keep the look).
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

Evidence the steps rest on (cited by ID below):
- **E-a** EZD-209 gate run 3 (`.claude/worktrees/EZD-209/gate.log:10967, 11044`; its `perf-results/latest.json`): `long-tasks-during-pan:ipad` 6 in E1 and 1 in the perf step; iPad frames p50 16.8 ms, p95 50, max 50.1, 94 of 379 over 33.3 ms, pan 10,217 ms; desktop p95 16.8 ms and 0 long tasks. STATUS EZD-209: 53 (load 25-40), 2, 6; perf step red in 2 of 3. STATUS EZD-207c / its D-Isolate: 0-1 in the lone perf step at merge. The count sits at the 50 ms edge.
- **E-b** `vault/spikes/EZD-027.md:31`: the drawing work stays near 1 ms per frame, and the dropped frames come from the GPU. At 4× CPU (Q-0616 (a)) that is about 4 ms of script, so tasks of about 50 ms point to the main thread waiting on software WebGL (no GPU flags: EZD-207c D-GPU) that fills 2,360 × 1,640 pixels with antialiasing. This is a hypothesis; Step 4 proves or disproves it (CLAUDE.md rule 1).
- **E-c** R26 R10 (`vault/spec/decisions/11-non-functional-requirements.md:20`): CI gates on counts that need no GPU. Same in 11 Performance, opening paragraph.
- **E-d** Chromium cannot start in the unit sandbox (`vault/KNOWN-LIMITS.md`, unit sandbox hole (1); this planning session's launch probe failed). The gate is the builder's only browser runner, so every measurement is a gate run.

Data: none.

### Build steps

| 1 | `scripts/perf/pan-script.mjs` | change | `runPan(context, baseUrl, panUrl, profile)` unchanged; its result gains `panTasks: Array<{ at: number; ms: number }>` and `load1: number` (D-Tasks, D-Load); doc comment per D-095 | its own `longTasksPan` filter (`pan-script.mjs:178`) | T1, T2 (gate `test` step; Chromium runs only in the gate, E-d) |
| 2 | `scripts/perf/check.mjs` | change | `panInput` case `long-tasks-during-pan` returns `{ value: pan.longTasksPan, details: { profile: name, tasks: pan.panTasks, load1: pan.load1 } }` (D-Details) | the `react-commits-during-pan` details object (`check.mjs:166-172`) | T1, T2, T3 |
| 3 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | none; D-Docs text in `### Performance check (EZD-017)` | EZD-207c D-Docs | `pnpm run lint` |
| 4 | `scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs` (diagnosis only: restored, never committed) | temporary edit | `PROFILES.ipad.deviceScaleFactor` 2 → 1 for runs V1-1 and V1-2 only | none (one literal) | D-Diagnose; after restoring, `git diff --quiet -- scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs` exits 0 |
| 5 | `scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs` (branch G only; Q-0618 (c)) | change | `PROFILES` gains key `'ipad-1x'` after `ipad` (D-C) | `PROFILES.ipad` | T4c |
| 6 | `scripts/perf/registry.mjs` (branch G only; Q-0618 (c)) | change | rows `react-commits-during-pan:ipad`, `long-tasks-during-pan:ipad`, `long-tasks-during-load:ipad`: profile `'ipad'` → `'ipad-1x'` (D-C) | the rows themselves (`registry.mjs:17-23`) | T4c |

V1-1, V1-2: Step 4's edit, then two gate runs (`profiles.test.mjs` N1, `perf-profile.test.ts`, `pan.test.mjs` P1 and E1's `deviceScaleFactor` line then fail by design and are ignored), then `git checkout -- scripts/perf/perf.config.mjs`. # EZD-357 · Fix: a typed chain that closes at exactly 12 inches shows its gap box

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-357-1, AC-EZD-357-2
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** geometry, testing
- **User-visible result:** a wall chain typed 12', 10', 12', 9' now shows its 12" gap box with Absorb and Keep out of square; a chain that misses by 12 1/16" still shows none.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
