# EZD-358 · Fix: the EZD-207c E3 no-database test waits for the first draw before reading draw calls

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-358-1 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md` line 822)
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** testing
- **User-visible result:** none in the app; the benchmark-page browser test stops failing at random at the merge gate, so merges are not held up by it.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Cause (read from code on develop, section 2 C1–C4): **a wrong wait in the test, not an app fault.** `attachCanvas` sets `ready`, then `redraw()` only schedules a frame (`root.invalidate()`, frameloop `demand`). `PlanCanvas` sets `data-plan-state="ready"` when `attachCanvas` resolves, so Playwright can see "ready" before that frame has rendered. Until it renders, `stats().drawCalls` is three.js `gl.info.render.calls` = 0. E3 read the stats once right after "ready" and so lost the race once (ticket row). Fix: E3 waits until the stats report a draw, and that wait's result is what E3 asserts. No assertion is removed or weakened. A new negative test proves the wait fails when the plan never reports a draw.

No data, no migration, no app code.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts` (test-author) | change | none exported. (a) Add `import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';` as the first import line (above `node:child_process`). (b) After `rowOf` (ends line 75) add `type DrawStats = { drawCalls: number; contexts: number };` and the module-level `async function firstDrawStats(page: Page, timeout: number): Promise<DrawStats>`, with this comment line directly above it: `// EZD-358: the plan reports ready before its first frame is drawn (attachCanvas only schedules it); wait for a draw.` Body: `const handle = await page.waitForFunction(() => { const s = (window as unknown as { __ezdraftPlan?: { stats(): DrawStats } }).__ezdraftPlan?.stats(); return s !== undefined && s.drawCalls >= 1 ? { drawCalls: s.drawCalls, contexts: s.contexts } : null; }, undefined, { timeout }); return (await handle.jsonValue()) as DrawStats;` (c) In E3 (line 146): title becomes `'EZD-207c E3 page with no database (EZD-358)'`; replace the `const stats = await page.evaluate(...)` statement (lines 160–166) with `const stats = await firstDrawStats(page, 30000);`. Lines 167–168 (`drawCalls` ≥ 1, `contexts` 1) and every other E3 line stay. (d) After the closing `});` of `test.describe('EZD-207c benchmark pan')` add the new top-level describe and test N1 (section 4). Nothing else changes | the same file's glyph wait (lines 169–175: `page.waitForFunction(..., undefined, { timeout: 30000 })`); `app/e2e/device-layouts.spec.ts` lines 3–4 (type import of `Page` from `@playwright/test`, then the harness import); EZD-324 Build step 1 (a local helper in front of an unchanged assertion) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec eslint e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app run typecheck` exit 0; `pnpm exec prettier --write app/e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts`; one run of `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-358 e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts` meets the section 4 T3 per-run rule. Done: commit dd6f273c on t/EZD-358; no further test edit |
| 2 | none (builder) | none | none. The builder changes no file. In the worktree it runs `pnpm db:up`, then `pnpm build`, then `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-358 e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts` as its own Bash call (no `cd`, `&&`, pipe or redirect; Bash timeout 600000) until 10 runs in a row count under section 4 T3. The count starts at the first run after this plan patch; the 2026-11-06 run 1 is evidence for section 9, not one of the 10. For each run it reports the summary block (the `failed`, `flaky`, `interrupted`, `skipped`, `did not run` and `passed` lines with the titles under them) and whether it counts. It stops with a `PLAN-GAP` and that run's output when a T3 stop condition is met; it changes nothing to make a run pass | EZD-324 Build step 2 (builder runs the proof only) | the run summaries (section 4 T3) |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App or test fix | Test. `BenchmarkPlan.tsx`, `controller.ts`, `render-root.ts`, `PlanCanvas.tsx` stay as they are | section 2 C1–C4; ticket row ("make the test wait") |
| What is waited for | `__ezdraftPlan.stats().drawCalls >= 1`, the ticket row's second option. Not `frames >= 1` (a frame can render before the camera is fitted, and N1 rejects it), not a plan "first draw" event (none exists; adding one is app code) | ticket row; `controller.ts:370–372` (`stats` shape) |
| How it waits | `page.waitForFunction` with its default polling; no `waitForTimeout`, no fixed sleep, no `expect.poll`, no retry, no longer expect timeout | ticket row ("with no sleep"); same file lines 169–175 |
| One read, not two | The helper returns the stats object from the same evaluation that saw `drawCalls >= 1` (`handle.jsonValue()`); E3 asserts on that value, never on a second `stats()` read | a second read could land on a later frame; three.js `gl.info` holds the last frame's count (`render-root.ts:68–70`) |
| Missing hook | The helper treats an absent `__ezdraftPlan` as "not drawn yet" (`?.`), so it waits instead of throwing | `BenchmarkPlan.tsx:37` sets the hook inside an effect |
| E3 wait timeout | 30000 ms, the value E3 already uses for its ready and glyph waits | EZD-207c section 4 E3 ("within 30 s"); same file lines 154, 175 |

| N1 placement and titles | New top-level `test.describe('EZD-358 first-draw wait', () => { ... })` after the EZD-207c describe, test title `'EZD-358 the first-draw wait fails when the plan never draws'`; untagged, so Playwright project `perf` | architecture `### Test scope (Q-0006)` (a later ticket adds its own top-level describe; C9); EZD-207c section 3 (file runs in `perf`) |
| E3 title | `EZD-207c E3 page with no database (EZD-358)` | architecture `## Tests` (closing test has the ticket id in its title); EZD-324 precedent |

The getter returns `undefined` before the page sets the hook, which the helper's `?.` treats as not drawn. Only `drawCalls` is hidden; `frames`, `contexts`, `glyphs`, `handle` pass through. `configurable: true` so `BenchmarkPlan`'s cleanup `delete` works | `BenchmarkPlan.tsx:37–39` (assignment), `:50` (`delete`) |
| N1 frames wait | Exactly: `await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as unknown as { __ezdraftPlan: { stats(): { frames: number } } }).__ezdraftPlan.stats().frames >= 1, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });` (the same `window as unknown as` cast style as the file's glyph wait, lines 169–175) | same file lines 169–175; C1 (`frames` in `stats`) |
| Formatting | `pnpm exec prettier --write app/e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts` | architecture `## Tests` |
| How the 10 runs are made | Separate `ui-run.mjs` calls on this spec. Each call runs the whole browser suite (284 tests in the builder's run 1): project `perf` lists the four device projects under `dependencies`, and Playwright runs a dependency project's tests in full whatever file is named; the file's 4 tests run last, in `perf`, one worker. The run is read by test title in the summary (section 4 T3), never by the `passed` count | C7; C10; builder PLAN-GAP run 1 (2026-11-06) |
| Runs and the error rate limit | Before each run, `pnpm db:up` in the worktree, never `pnpm db:reset`: `db:up` always runs `supabase db reset --local` and then stores a fresh API gate hash (`scripts/db/local.mjs:2,70,92-100` `storeLocalGateSecret`); `db:reset` (`package.json` `db:reset`) drops that hash, so sign-in fails closed (`sign_in_throttle_take` 401 `api_gate_not_configured`) and project `perf` does not run. EZD-024 T18 (`e2e/error-reporting.spec.ts`) sends browser errors through the tunnel, which allows 60 events per address per rolling hour (`error_tunnel_take`), and all runs share one local database and one address: the first attempt passed 9 runs, then failed T18 3 times with 0 events received. The limit is the likely cause, not yet proven. If T18 still fails right after a reset, stop and block with that output: it is then a real defect, and a defect ticket for EZD-024 T18 goes to the front of the queue. A run that fails T18 does not count toward the 10 | `supabase/migrations/20261025043417_create_error_tunnel_throttle.sql`; overwatch 2026-11-07 |
| No runner change | No `--project=perf` or `--no-deps` (`ui-run.mjs` refuses any argument after the spec, C7, and is build system, frozen: CLAUDE.md rule 18), no `playwright.config.ts` change (outside this ticket; the gate runs the same full suite, so the full run is also the gate's condition) | C7; C10; CLAUDE.md rules 4, 18 |
| Other failures in a run | A failure of any test other than E3 and N1 (the EZD-207c done-when test included) does not stop the runs and is not fixed here: the builder lists its title and first error line in its report, and the orchestrator files it as a defect ticket at the front of the queue (section 9) | CLAUDE.md rules 4, 17; ticket Done when names E3 only |

### Do not touch
- App code: `app/src/app/dev/benchmark-plan/**`, `app/src/editor/plan/**`.
- E1 and E2 in the same file, the module helpers `findRepoRoot`, `runPerf`, `latestOf`, `rowOf`, `PAN_IDS`, `R`, and the file's header comment.
- `app/playwright.config.ts`, `app/test-harness/**` (`devices.ts` `PERF_SPECS`), `scripts/perf/**`, `scripts/ui-run.mjs`, `scripts/gate.mjs`.

Ticket row (`vault/tickets/phases/phase-04.md` line 29):
- Scope: Defect found at the EZD-210a merge gate (2026-11-06): app/e2e/perf-benchmark-pan.spec.ts:146 (E3 page with no database) read stats.drawCalls at line 167 and got 0, expected at least 1 (the test ended 412 ms after start); the same test passed in the gate run before it on identical code, so it is a race between page load and the first draw. Make the test wait until the plan reports its first draw (or the stats show drawCalls of at least 1) before the assertion, with no sleep, and prove it with repeated runs.
- Done when: The E3 test passes in 10 consecutive e2e runs and still fails when the plan never draws.
- Depends on: EZD-207c · Spec ref: EZD-207c plan; rule 17

## 2. Sources

# EZD-359 · Fix: the EZD-207c done-when test long-tasks-during-pan fails at random in the full browser suite

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-359-1
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, perf, scripts
- **User-visible result:** The build stops failing at random on the pan long-task check, and every red perf run says how much of each long task was the app's own work. Nothing on screen changes.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-06, plan gaps 2026-11-07 (I2 red: Q-0623) · Status: questions

## 1. What to build

Evidence (cited by ID below):
- **E-a** The 10 E1 results since EZD-356 (523cd691), read here from Josh's temp folder (`/var/folders/2t/t09425m57_g4jvd1l3z5wnj00000gn/T/ezd-perf-*/latest.json`; ui-run runs as Josh). 2 of 10 runs red: 2026-11-07T04:00Z desktop `[{at 5167, ms 67}]` load1 5.43 and ipad-1x `[{at 5451, ms 59}]` load1 10.15 (EZD-358 builder run 1); 04:10Z desktop `[{at 202, ms 78}]` load1 12.23. The other 8 were 0 at load1 6.6 to 12.6. Before EZD-356, desktop was 0 in 15 runs (load1 up to 17.22). One task per red row, at no fixed point of the gesture; load1 does not separate red from green.
- **E-b** Desktop is unthrottled at 1x (`perf.config.mjs` `PROFILES.desktop`), and the drawing work is about 1 ms a frame (`vault/spikes/EZD-027.md:31`). Nothing on the pan path starts a timer, a lazy import or a shader compile (`controller.ts`: hover only in mode `'wall'`, :151; the only dynamic import is the error reporter, :89; `scene.ts` makes its materials once). The benchmark page's code did not change between the green and red runs (`git diff --stat 4deba37d f2bb394c -- app/src`: only `editor/tools/`, icons, messages). So the 59 to 78 ms is a stall outside the app's work (Mac load, garbage collection) or a script cost the code does not show. Hypothesis H (a stall) is unproven; D-Diagnose decides it (rule 1).

## 5. Visual checklist
None (no screen changes).

## 6. Proposed wording
None (no user-visible text).

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. Test and perf tooling only; no tables, permissions, money, auth or API.
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a cause found by measuring, a trace parser that can only be proved in Chromium in the gate, a branch, and 10 or more full-suite runs. Test-author sonnet-5-5 medium (the fixtures are given exactly); builder opus-5-5 medium (D-Branch reading and run discipline), with opus-5-5 high on a second round.

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-207c (ticket row): `runPan`, the pan rows, project `perf`, E1.
- EZD-356 (missing from the row): `panTasks`, `load1`, the details key order and `ipad-1x` (523cd691); this plan extends its contract.
- EZD-358 (sibling, not a dependency): it edits E3 in the same spec, and this plan leaves that file alone. Its merge gate can be failed by this defect (EZD-358 plan section 2 note), so this ticket should land first or alongside. Both builders' ui-runs write to Josh's temp folder; D-Diagnose's `ambiguous` rule keeps them apart.
- Risks: on ipad-1x the throttle itself burns about 3/4 of every task's length as CPU time (E-f), so no rule on `cpu` alone separates waiting there; D-Split subtracts it (Q-0623). Its cost: in a task the Mac preempts for p ms the iPad estimate drops by 3p, so app work of 13 to 13 + 0.75p ms passes the iPad row in that task (desktop unaffected). P2's loop is wall-clocked (`ms` stays 200, `cpu` falls by p, estimate 200 − 4p), so P2 goes red when one iPad task is preempted 38 ms or more; I1 only when all 8 are. (a) cannot see a main-thread block that burns no CPU (sync request, alert, Atomics.wait); such a block in app code would land in details.waits and pass (none on the pan path today, E-b; top and gc keep it visible). Tracing adds a little main-thread work to every pan. It can add long tasks but never hide one, and the frame-time rows are trends. No `tdur` or no user-timing mark in this Chromium makes I1 fail, and D-Order stops with `PLAN-GAP`. D-ReadRun uses this Mac's path to Josh's temp folder. P2 and T1 keep `value` 8 with the 200 ms loop: the 60 ms loop already outlasts the 16 ms wheel step, so wheel events already queue today and P2 counts 8; a miscount shows as a red gate and a `PLAN-GAP`. Branch H changes what the gate counts, so it waits for Q-0621. Back-to-back full-suite runs fill the shared local database's error and email limits (E-g; EZD-358 hit the same), so every run follows `pnpm db:up` (D-UiRun); a concurrent EZD-358 reset can still fail a run, which then does not count.

## 10. Open questions
- QP-1 (needed only if D-Diagnose round 2 ends with exactly 1 red pan task, under the line): Q-0621 gates branch H on 2 or more red tasks under the line, and 24 counting runs gave 1 (run 5: 55 ms, `cpu` 2); what then? (a) Branch H on that evidence: H still counts every task over the line or with unknown CPU, and D-Runs keeps recording each wait's `cpu`, `gc` and `top`, so app work still turns E1 red and stops the run series. Planner's recommendation. (b) No branch H: re-plan without Steps 5-7, I2 and T1e and run D-Runs on wall time; at about 1 red in 24 runs the 10-run streak holds about 65% of the time, and the flake stays (rule 17). (c) Another 12-run round.
- Q-0623 (was QP-2; answered-agent (a), phase-auditor 2026-11-07): on ipad-1x the throttle's spin shows as CPU time (E-f), so a task counts when `cpu === null` or `cpu × rate − ms × (rate − 1) > 50` (D-Split); it refines Q-0621 (a), which stays the rule at rate 1.- Q-0621 (answered-agent (a), phase-auditor 2026-11-07; the planner's recommendation stands): If the diagnosis shows every red pan task's own main-thread work is under 50 ms (CPU time × throttle rate ≤ 50: the Mac's other lanes stretched it), what does the gate count? (a) A pan task only when its CPU time × the profile's throttle rate is over 50 ms or unknown; the rest are listed in `details.waits`. Budget 0 and the 50 ms line stay (Q-0073 (a)), the 4× iPad throttle keeps its effect, and the pass stops depending on Mac load (Q-0619's reason). Planner's recommendation. (b) Wall time as now: the Done-when cannot be met while other lanes run; only a quiet perf step (build system, frozen, rule 18) would fix it. (c) CPU time without the rate: the iPad row would pass tasks of 13 to 50 ms of work that run 52 to 200 ms on the throttled CPU, which weakens the iPad check.

# EZD-221a · Template objects on the server

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-221-3, AC-EZD-221-5, AC-EZD-221-6 (server write); AC-EZD-221-1, AC-EZD-221-2, AC-EZD-221-7 (values and checks only) (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:798-803`; split proposal `vault/plans/EZD-221.md` Part EZD-221a)
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** data-model, migrations, security, testing, geometry
- **User-visible result:** none on screen yet: `POST /api/projects` with a template (Galley kitchen, L-kitchen, 5x8 bath, Primary bath and its sizes) makes the project with four walls at the Ceiling height and one room named after the template, also for a Foreman without Edit model. EZD-221b adds the wizard step that sends it.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-07 · Status: planned · Base: develop `6d0cc8ce`

## 1. What to build
Data: no table, column, money field or `schema_version` change. One `security definer` function M1: creates the project through the unchanged `public.create_project` (one project write path, 03b rule 1; migration `20261105105039`) and inserts the template's `model_object` rows in the same transaction (Q-0568; AC-5). Create projects only, not Edit model (Q-0566), so not through `save_objects` (needs `edit_model`, `20261105200004:40-50`); Q-0566/Q-0568 override 03b rule 6 for this write made before any edit lock exists. No drop or rename (ARCH Release safety). The floor comes from trigger `project_first_floor` (`20261105200003`); deferred trigger `model_object_level_check` (`20261105210000`) checks each `data.level` at commit.

M1, copy exactly (run on pinned PostgreSQL 17.11 in a rolled-back transaction 2026-11-07: compiles; execute anon f, authenticated t, service_role f; L-009; no `count(`, EZD-321):
```sql
create function public.create_project_with_objects(p_name text, p_address text, p_type text,
  p_customer_id uuid, p_scope_of_work text, p_objects jsonb)
returns table (project_id uuid, tenant_id uuid)
language plpgsql volatile security definer set search_path = ''
as $$
#variable_conflict use_column
declare
  v_project uuid; v_tenant uuid; v_floor uuid; v_item jsonb; v_keys text array; v_id uuid; v_seen uuid array := '{}';
begin
  perform private.require_api_gate();
  select c.project_id, c.tenant_id into v_project, v_tenant
    from public.create_project(p_name, p_address, p_type, p_customer_id, p_scope_of_work) c;
  if p_objects is null or jsonb_typeof(p_objects) <> 'array'
     or jsonb_array_length(p_objects) < 1 or jsonb_array_length(p_objects) > 5 then
    raise exception 'invalid_input' using errcode = '22023';
  end if;
  for v_item in select e from jsonb_array_elements(p_objects) as e loop
    if jsonb_typeof(v_item) <> 'object' then
      raise exception 'invalid_input' using errcode = '22023';
    end if;
    select array_agg(k order by k) into v_keys from jsonb_object_keys(v_item) as k;
    if v_keys is distinct from string_to_array('data,id,schema_version,type', ',')
      or coalesce(jsonb_typeof(v_item -> 'id'), '') <> 'string'
      or coalesce((v_item ->> 'id') !~* '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$', true)
      or coalesce(jsonb_typeof(v_item -> 'type'), '') <> 'string'
      or coalesce((v_item ->> 'type') not in ('wall', 'room'), true)
      or coalesce(jsonb_typeof(v_item -> 'schema_version'), '') <> 'number'
      or coalesce((v_item ->> 'schema_version') !~ '^[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$', true)
      or coalesce(jsonb_typeof(v_item -> 'data'), '') <> 'object'
    then
      raise exception 'invalid_input' using errcode = '22023';
    end if;
    v_id := (v_item ->> 'id')::uuid;
    if v_id = any (v_seen) then
      raise exception 'invalid_input' using errcode = '22023';
    end if;
    v_seen := v_seen || v_id;
  end loop;
  select m.object_id into v_floor from public.model_object m
    where m.project_id = v_project and m.type = 'floor' and not m.deleted;
  insert into public.model_object
    (project_id, object_id, tenant_id, type, data, schema_version, updated_seq, updated_by)
  select v_project, (e ->> 'id')::uuid, v_tenant, e ->> 'type',
    jsonb_set(e -> 'data', '{level}', to_jsonb(v_floor::text)), (e ->> 'schema_version')::integer, 1,
    private.app_user_id()
  from jsonb_array_elements(p_objects) as e;
  return query select v_project, v_tenant;
end
$$;
revoke all on function public.create_project_with_objects(text, text, text, uuid, text, jsonb) from public, anon, service_role;
grant execute on function public.create_project_with_objects(text, text, text, uuid, text, jsonb) to authenticated;
```

Its fields read sizes with `parseLength(text, 'wall_room')` (parent plan Decided `readTemplate`); `isTemplateSize` is this ticket's server check of the result, and `templateAreaSqFt` is the one area both use.
- Risks: a migration merged after this plan must still sort before M1's timestamp (step 1); `createProject`'s two paths must keep one error mapping (U10).

## 10. Open questions
None. Q-0592 (a) is applied as U12.

security-review: no. No route, table, policy, permission or server code: this part only sends the `template` body that EZD-221a's route checks (EZD-221a section 7 carries the review).

High: a second wizard step built through a lazy module, a live-validated size form and an editor overlay, with 12 tests (9 browser) and 3 earlier-test edits (PROCESS.md section 4). Test-author Sonnet 5.5; builder Opus 5.5.

- Row: EZD-221a (`templates.ts`, `NewProjectBody.template`, route, `template_<key>` keys, the `### Blank templates (EZD-221)` architecture section; planned, not merged), EZD-210a, EZD-210b (rail, `DrawingLayer`, `editor.spec.ts` B2 as it stands), EZD-118, EZD-120b (`ModelStore`), EZD-120c (`ProjectEditor`, `__ezdraftEditor`), EZD-201 (`parseLength`, `formatLength`), EZD-207a (plan canvas, `showPlan`); all done except EZD-221a.
- Missing from the row: EZD-016a (browser harness; visual checklist), EZD-010b (icon pipeline), EZD-015 (`InlineError`, `Skeleton`), EZD-020 (`lazyModule`), EZD-108 (`Segmented` pattern), EZD-332 (`signedInJsContents`), EZD-205a (area grouping); all done.
- Risks: another ticket adding icons before this merges changes E3's list and `icons.json` order; the step-2 dialog narrows column 2 below 1440 px wide viewports (tiles stay 5 across); the hint sits over the canvas centre with `pointer-events: none`, so canvas tests that click there are unaffected.

## 10. Open questions
None.

# EZD-299 · Conflict list: banner, list (board S03b), Show and "make a conflict"

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-299-1, AC-EZD-299-5, AC-EZD-299-6, AC-EZD-299-7, AC-EZD-299-8, AC-EZD-299-10, AC-EZD-299-12
- **Complexity:** high
- **Areas:** ui, testing, tokens
- **User-visible result:** when a change can't be saved, the editor shows a banner; "Review changes" (or the bell notification) opens "Changes not saved", where each change is named ("Wall 4 · Height"), shows yours against the saved value, and is settled with Keep mine, Keep theirs, Remove, Reload or Show; the test page has "Make a conflict".
- Phase: 3 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-07 (re-validated 2026-11-09 on develop 5cc18fae) · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Last part of the EZD-299 split (parts a and b: `vault/plans/EZD-299a.md`, `EZD-299b.md`, contracts P299a, P299b). No data, no tables, no routes. Build after EZD-299a, EZD-299b and EZD-294 are merged. Q-0632 (a) (answered-agent 2026-11-07, phase-auditor): C1's `savedBy`, `savedAt`, `clientName` are required fields (P299a list, P299b `ConflictRow`), and the client suffix, `conflict-saved-by` and `saved_by` are built. Q-0631 (b) (answered-agent 2026-11-07, security-reviewer): a deleted project and one no longer open both reach the list as reason `not_open`, shown with P14b; P14 is not used.

### Build steps

| 2 | `app/src/styles/tokens.css`, `app/src/styles/tokens.ts` | change | 6 tokens (D-Tokens) | the EZD-110 block in both files | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/styles/tokens.test.ts` |
| 3 | `app/src/server/messages/catalogs/en.ts` | change | the `office.conflicts.*` keys of section 6 (English only) | the `office.notifications.*` block | U6 |
| 4 | `app/src/lib/conflicts/conflict-view.ts` | new | section 3 C1-C3 | `app/src/lib/notifications/kinds.ts` (pure, no React) | U1-U3 |
| 5 | `app/src/editor/editor-session.ts` | change | `EditorSession.queued(): Promise<OutboxEntry[]>` = `storage.list()` | same file (`dispose`) | U10 |
| 6 | `app/src/editor/conflicts/use-conflicts.ts` | new | C5 (D-Hook, D-Outdated) | `app/src/components/states/ToastProvider.tsx` (`useSyncExternalStore`) | `pnpm run typecheck`; B3 |
| 7 | `app/src/editor/conflicts/ConflictBanner.tsx` + `ConflictBanner.module.css` | new | C6 (D-Banner, D-CSS) | `app/src/editor/SaveStatus.tsx` | U5 |
| 8 | `app/src/editor/conflicts/ConflictPanel.tsx` + `ConflictPanel.module.css` | new | C7, C8 (D-Panel, D-Actions, D-Show, D-CSS) | `app/src/lazy/notification-panel/NotificationPanelView.tsx` (pure view + container) | U4a-U4c |
| 9 | `app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx` | change | `ProjectEditorProps.conflictsOpen?: boolean` (D-Editor) | same file | B1-B9 |
| 10 | `app/src/app/(editor)/projects/[id]/page.tsx` | change | optional `searchParams` (D-Page) | same file | U7 |
| 11 | `app/src/lazy/notification-panel/NotificationPanelView.tsx` + `app/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.module.css` | change | D-Bell | same files | U11 |
| 12 | `app/src/app/(editor)/dev/saves/[id]/save-bench.ts` | change | C10 (D-Fault, D-Wait) | same file (`createSaveFault`, `waitForSync`) | U8, U9 |
| 13 | `app/src/app/(editor)/dev/saves/[id]/SaveBench.tsx` | change | "Make a conflict" (D-Bench) | same file (`run('fail')`) | B1 |
| 14 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | D-Docs | `### Editor route (EZD-120c)` | review |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Icons | Fetch each with `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app icons:fetch <name>` (prefix `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` inside a unit), add to `icons.json` sorted, `icons:build`. All 10 checked at `ICON_COMMIT` 49d4db35 on 2026-11-07: `viewBox="0 -960 960 960"`, so no legacy conversion | ARCH Design tokens; planner lessons (EZD-103a, EZD-110b) |
| D-Tokens | Append after `--ez-shadow-switch-knob` in both files, comment `/* S03b banner, list; EZD-299 */`, group `color`: `--ez-amber-banner: oklch(0.97 0.03 80)`, `--ez-amber-border: oklch(0.86 0.07 75)`, `--ez-amber-icon: oklch(0.5 0.13 60)`, `--ez-amber-strong: oklch(0.43 0.12 60)`, `--ez-cobalt-deep: oklch(0.42 0.17 262)`; plus `--ez-group-band: #fafbfc` (6 tokens). Colors and shadows come only from `var(--ez-*)`; sizes are px (no spacing tokens, L-013) | board S03b HTML; ARCH Design tokens (check C10) |
| D-Inputs | The list is `ConflictViewInput[]`: every `ConflictRow` of `session.conflicts` (P299b; assignable as is) in its store order, then `outdatedInputs(...)` | P299b `conflict-list.ts`; Q-0511 e |
| D-Outdated | Only while `sync.getState().problem === 'app_outdated'` (P299b D-Settle keeps those changes in the outbox): `session.queued()` loaded when the problem becomes `app_outdated` and each time the list opens; any other problem or `sync` null → `[]`. A rejection → `[]` and `captureBrowserError(error, 'editor.device_copy')` (dynamic import, as `editor-session.ts` `report`). `outdatedInputs`: entries sorted by `queuedAt` descending, then `projectId/id` ascending; `key` `outdated:<projectId>/<id>`; `projectName` null; `mine` `{ deleted: true }` when `value` null, else `{ deleted: false, ...value }`; `saved` = the `session.model.objects` entry with the same id (lower-case compare) when the entry's project is the open one, as `{ updatedSeq, deleted: false, type, schemaVersion, data }`, else null; `savedBy`, `savedAt`, `clientName` null; `actions` `['reload']` | Q-0511 e; Q-0540; P299b D-Settle; board P13 |
| D-Present | `present(x)`: `x` not null and `deleted === false` → its `{ type, data }`. Label = `objectLabel(present(mine) ?? present(saved) ?? null)` (P299a D-Labels; walls and openings read `attributes.number`, unnumbered → "Wall"). Noun and icon from the same value: `wall` → `wall` / `view_column_2`; `opening` with `data.attributes.kind` `door` → `door` / `door_front`, `window` → `window` / `window`; `room` → `room` / `rectangle`; `floor` → `floor` / `layers`; anything else or null → `object` / `category` | Q-0511 b; board S03b icons; `tool-defs.ts` (`rectangle` = Room) |
| D-Read | Raw reads, never parsed, never throw: a length is a `number`, finite, `>= 0`, else null. Wall length = `wallLength({ start, end })` (`@ezdraft/geometry`) when both points have finite `x`, `y`, else null; wall `thickness`, `height` = `data.attributes.*`; opening `width`, `height`, `sill_height` = `attributes.width`, `attributes.height`, `attributes.sillHeight`. Two lengths are the same when both null, or both numbers and `coordsEqual` (1/64", inclusive). Two points are the same when both unreadable, or both readable and `pointsEqual` | 03b rule 5; 03g; Q-0507; `packages/geometry/src/tolerance.ts`, `walls/wall.ts` |
| D-Fields | Both `present`, same type: wall fields in order `length`, `thickness`, `height`, then `position` (start or end not the same) only when `length` is the same; opening `width`, `height`, `sill_height`, `position` (center not the same, or `geometry.hostWallId` not `===`); keep each field that differs; none differ, other types, or types differ → `['details']`. Only one side present (a delete, or no saved value): wall → `['length']`, opening → `['width']`, else `[]` | Q-0511 b "what changed"; board rows show one field per row; section 6 |
| D-Chips | Length field = first of `fields` in `length`, `thickness`, `height`, `width`, `sill_height`. Yours: `mine` null → none; deleted → `Deleted`; else that field's read of `mine` formatted with `formatLength(v, PLAN_DISPLAY_DENOMINATOR)`; no length field or null read → none. Saved: only for reason `conflict`; `saved` null → none; deleted → `Deleted`; else as Yours on `saved` | board S03b P7 (rows 4-7 show Yours only); EZD-201 E6, E9; Q-0568 |
| D-Why | Reason `conflict`: `saved` deleted and `mine` present → `they_deleted` + hint `brings_back`; `mine` deleted and `saved` present → `you_deleted` + hint `deletes_theirs`; else none. Other reasons: `why` = the reason (`invalid`, `outdated`, `not_open`, `not_editable`), no hint. `{noun}` in P8, P10 = `t('office.conflicts.noun.<noun>')` | board P8-P13, P14b, P14c; Q-0511 c, e; Q-0540; Q-0631 (b) (no `gone`) |
| D-Groups | Group of an input: reason `not_open` → `not_open`; project id equals the open one (lower-case compare) → `this`; else `other`. Groups in that order, inputs in input order. Page: the first `limit` inputs across groups in that order; a group with no paged row is left out; `count` = the group's full count; `total` = all inputs; `more` = `total > limit`. `CONFLICT_PAGE_SIZE = 50`; "Show more" adds 50 | Q-0628 (b) (separate generic group, no name); 11 rule 9 (a list that can pass 50 rows is paged; P299a `MAX_RECORD_CHANGES` 1000) |
| D-Row text | Title = label. ## 7. Security review
security-review: no (no route, table, permission or money change; the bench fault is on a developer page that production does not serve, P120d).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier yes · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a new screen with many states wired to two unbuilt modules, nine browser flows across permissions, deletes and app versions. Test-author Sonnet 5.5 / medium; builder Opus 5.5 / medium.

## 9. Dependencies
Row: EZD-299b (done d334acca; Q-0631 answered (b)), EZD-120c, EZD-120d, EZD-110b, EZD-207a, EZD-207b, EZD-201, EZD-016a, EZD-294 (done 5cc18fae; Q-0629 answered (b)), all done. Missing from the row: EZD-299c (the security fix ticket for the membership header on GET and DELETE `/api/sync-conflicts` and their two client calls, plus the conditional server delete of Q-0648 (b); STATUS EZD-299b note; not yet in `tickets.json`, the orchestrator adds it): this ticket builds after it, so the Remove and Keep theirs flows its browser tests drive run on the fixed calls, and its direct GETs already carry the header (section 4). Name clash: the phase-01.md row of this ticket calls its own scope "Part EZD-299c" (the split proposal's label for the part that kept the base ID); that label means EZD-299, not the fix ticket. EZD-299a (done 11d4b66d: types, `objectLabel`, `APP_BUILD_HEADER`, routes, `sync_conflict` title and link), EZD-110a (notification open route), EZD-140 (email settings), EZD-024 (Sentry stub, B4), EZD-010b (icon pipeline), EZD-015b (toast, inline error), EZD-014c (touch-target helper), EZD-210b (`DrawingLayer` in the canvas).
Risks: 10 icons grow the sprite every page carries (Projects 200 KB JS budget, 11 Budgets; perf check); the list stays in the editor chunk (500 KB); a re-validation is needed if EZD-299c changes `ConflictList`'s method names or `ResolveResult` (`conflict-list.ts:46-62`). Debt D-099 (medium, phase 4 gate: a crafted wall number 2147483647 makes new walls refused with 22023) names this list as the place for a recovery rule; it is not in this ticket's ACs and stays on `vault/debt.md`.

## 10. Open questions
None. Q-0629 is answered (b) and changes no test value here (section 2). Q-0632 is answered (a) and Q-0631 (b) (section 2); both are applied in section 1 (D-Why, D-Row text, D-Outdated), section 3 (C1, C2, C12), section 4 (U1 j, U2, U4a, U4c, B5b), section 5 and section 6.

# EZD-299a · Conflict list: server copy, save refusals and the notification

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-299-11, AC-EZD-299-13, AC-EZD-299-14, AC-EZD-299-15
- **Complexity:** high
- **Areas:** data-model, migrations, security, api, testing
- **User-visible result:** a change the server refuses is kept on the server for that person (any device), a save from an older app is refused without writing, and one notification names the project and every refused object.
- Phase: 3 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-07 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

RLS on; `sync_conflict_select` to authenticated using the EZD-006 project template `and user_id = (select private.app_user_id())`; `sync_conflict_api_gate` restrictive. `grant select … to authenticated; grant select, insert, update, delete … to service_role`. S2 functions (all `language plpgsql security definer set search_path = ''`; first line `perform private.require_api_gate();`; then `v_tenant := private.tenant_id(); v_user := private.app_user_id();` null → `raise … errcode '42501'`; each `revoke all on function public.<fn>(<types>) from public, anon, service_role; grant execute … to authenticated;` (L-016). SQL is "confirm on pinned version" (L-009): the T2-T5 rows run it):
- `record_sync_conflicts(p_project uuid, p_changes jsonb, p_payload jsonb) returns jsonb`: membership claim null → 42501; `p_project` null or `not private.can_see_project(p_project)` → P0002; `p_changes` not an array of 1..1000 strict objects with keys `id` (uuid), `base_seq` (integer 0..2147483647; ≥1 when `deleted`), `reason` (the three), `deleted` (boolean), and, only when not deleted, `type` (pattern), `schema_version` (integer ≥1), `data` (object of at most 131,072 bytes as `octet_length(data::text)`), or an id twice → 22023; `p_payload` not exactly `{count, names, more}` strings with `count = jsonb_array_length(p_changes)::text`, `more` matching `^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$` and not above count, `names` non-empty → 22023. Then, in change order, `insert … on conflict (project_id, user_id, object_id) do update set reason, base_seq, deleted, type, schema_version, data, updated_at = now()` (id and created_at kept); then `v_note := private.create_notification(v_tenant, v_user, 'sync_conflict', p_project, p_payload, '/projects/' || p_project::text || '?conflicts=open')`. Returns `{ "ids": [row ids in change order], "notification_id": v_note }` (null when `create_notification` returns null).
- `list_my_sync_conflicts() returns jsonb`: the caller's rows (`tenant_id = v_tenant and user_id = v_user`, every project), `order by updated_at desc, id desc`, as a jsonb array (`'[]'` when none; not a set, so PostgREST `max_rows` does not cut it). Per row: `visible = private.can_see_project(project_id)`; `editable` = the `user_permission` `edit_model` granted check of `save_objects` step 3; `reason` = `not_open` when not visible, else `not_editable` when not editable, else the stored reason; keys `id, project_id, object_id, reason, base_seq, created_at, updated_at`, and, only when visible (else all six null): `project_name` (project.name), `client_name` (`customer.name` joined on `project.customer_id`, null when `customer_id` is null), `mine` (`{deleted, type, schema_version, data}`), `saved` (`{updated_seq, deleted, type, schema_version, data}` of the `model_object` row, null when none), and from that same `model_object` row `saved_at` (its `updated_at`) and `saved_by` (`app_user.name` of its `updated_by`, only when a `public.membership` row with `tenant_id = v_tenant` and `user_id = updated_by` exists, else null); no `model_object` row → `saved_by` and `saved_at` null (D-Saved by).
- `delete_my_sync_conflict(p_id uuid) returns boolean`: deletes the row with that id, `tenant_id = v_tenant` and `user_id = v_user` (no scope check, so a not-open row can be removed); true when a row went.
- `save_objects_resolving(p_project uuid, p_lock_epoch bigint, p_changes jsonb, p_resolves uuid[]) returns jsonb`: `v := public.save_objects(p_project, p_lock_epoch, p_changes)` (all its checks and codes); not `saved` → return `v`; `p_resolves` null, empty, holding a null or a repeat, or longer than `jsonb_array_length(p_changes)` → 22023 (rolls the save back); deletes rows `id = any(p_resolves)` of the caller's tenant and user and `p_project` whose `object_id` is among the saved objects; returns `v || jsonb_build_object('resolved', <deleted ids sorted, '[]' when none>)`.

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas: migrations, data access (new per-user table, definer functions that read across project scope), permissions, API (three routes, save route change).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: a new tenant table with definer functions that bypass project scope by design, a change to the only model write route that every save and several test files depend on, and a notification payload bound. Test-author Sonnet 5.5 (medium), builder Opus 5.5 (medium) (EZD-120a, EZD-202 precedent in STATUS.md).

Risks: every save now needs the app-build header, so any save request not listed above fails with 409 (grep of `/objects` callers on 2026-11-07 found only those listed); a dev server restarted under an open tab refuses that tab's saves until reload (intended). Done when: steps 1-19, T1-T20 and the edit rows, D-Docs text.

## 10. Open questions
None.

plans.text:
# EZD-299b · Conflict list: refused changes leave the outbox; Keep mine, Keep theirs, Remove

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-299-2, AC-EZD-299-3, AC-EZD-299-4, AC-EZD-299-9, AC-EZD-299-16, AC-EZD-299-17, AC-EZD-299-18
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** data-model, security, api, testing, offline
- **User-visible result:** when the server refuses a change for good, that change waits in the conflict list on this device and on the server, your other edits keep saving, and Keep mine, Keep theirs and Remove work (the screens come in EZD-299).
- Phase: 3 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-07 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Data: no table, no migration, no SQL function and no `schema_version` change. No money field (03b rule 2). The device database stays `ezdraft-device` **version 1** (D-Key).

Build only after EZD-299a is merged (every `app/src/lib/conflicts/conflicts.ts` type, `MAX_RECORD_*`, the sync-conflicts routes, `resolves`, `app_outdated`). Q-0631 (b) (answered-agent 2026-11-07, security-reviewer): the device stores one reason, `not_open`, for a project that was deleted and for one no longer open to the person; no presence route or function is built.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/src/lib/outbox/device-db.ts` | change | add `CONFLICT_KEY_PART = 'conflict'`; `conflictRange(appUserId: string, tenantId: string): IDBKeyRange` = `IDBKeyRange.bound([CONFLICT_KEY_PART, u, t], [CONFLICT_KEY_PART, u, t, []])`; `DEVICE_DB_VERSION` stays 1; `countQueued` unchanged | same file (`actorRange`) | T3 |
| 2 | `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts` | change | types of section 3 (`DeviceConflictReason`, `DeviceConflict`, `ConflictKey`, `ConflictMove`, `ConflictServerUpdate`, `ConflictOrphan`, `ConflictDelete`); `SaveOutcome` refused gains optional `conflicts`, `invalid` (D-Classify); `OutboxStorage` gains the six methods of section 3 | same file | T2 |
| 3 | `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-idb.ts` | change | the six methods (D-Key, D-Move, D-Requeue with its `{ kept }` result, D-Server, D-Guard for `deleteConflicts`, which returns the keys it kept); `commit` also deletes `requeued` rows at saved keys in its transaction | same file (`commit`, `drop`) | T3 |
| 4 | `app/src/lib/conflicts/conflict-api.ts` | new | `getConflicts`, `postConflicts`, `removeServerConflict` (section 3) | `app/src/lib/outbox/model-api.ts` (`fetchModel`) | T4, T7 |
| 5 | `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync.ts` | change | `SyncState.conflictRev: number` (0 at start); `OutboxSync.keepMine(row: DeviceConflict, baseSeq: number): Promise<void>`; refusal handling D-Settle, D-Record, D-Resolves | same file | T4 |
| 6 | `app/src/editor/model/model-store.ts` | change | `ModelStore.applyRemote(changes: Change[]): string[]` (D-Remote) | same file (`applyEdit`) | T5 |
| 7 | `app/src/lib/conflicts/conflict-list.ts` | new | `mergeConflicts`, `createConflictList`, types (section 3) | `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync.ts` (`zustand/vanilla` store, injected deps) | T6-T8 |
| 8 | `app/src/editor/editor-session.ts` | change | `OpenDeps.createConflicts?: (o: ConflictListOptions) => ConflictList` (default `createConflictList`); `EditorSession.conflicts: ConflictList`; D-Session | same file | T9 |
| 9 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | D-Docs | `### Patch store and outbox (EZD-120b)` | `grep -c '^### Sync conflicts on the device (EZD-299b)$' docs/architecture.md` prints 1 |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Key | Conflict rows go in the existing `outbox` store under key `[CONFLICT_KEY_PART, appUserId, tenantId, projectId, objectId]`, outside `actorRange`, so `list()`, `countQueued` and an older open tab never see them; no version bump (an older tab reopening a newer version fails with VersionError and loses the edits it holds, `outbox-idb.ts:42-45`). The idb schema's `outbox` value type is `OutboxEntry \| DeviceConflict`; values read through `conflictRange` are `DeviceConflict`, through `actorRange` `OutboxEntry` (cast). This replaces the split proposal's "new store, version 1 → 2" | rule 18; EZD-299 split proposal Part b; KNOWN-LIMITS none |
| D-Classify | `classifySave` adds `conflicts` only for status 409 with code `save_conflict` and `body.conflicts` an array of `{ id: string; serverSeq: number }`; adds `invalid` only for 400 with code `invalid_object` and `body.invalid` an array of `{ id: string; issue: string }`; otherwise the key is absent (not `undefined`). Other outcomes unchanged | objects route (`route.ts:72-88`); P202 section 3 |
| D-Settle | On a refused save, in `loop`: `save_conflict` with `conflicts` → move the sent entries whose id is listed, reason `conflict`, `serverSeq` from the list. `invalid_object` with `invalid` → move the listed sent entries, reason `invalid`, then `captureBrowserError(new Error('invalid_object'), 'outbox.invalid_object')` once per answer (dynamic import as `reportStorage`). `permission_denied` → every entry of that project in `storage.list()` (not only the batch), reason `not_editable`. `project_not_found` → every entry of that project in `storage.list()`, reason `not_open` (a deleted project and one no longer open read the same; no other call). A project-wide move first `drop`s that project's deletes with `baseSeq` 0 (pickBatch rule). When the move list is empty, and for every other code (`invalid_input`, `not_signed_in`, `stale_lock_epoch`, `app_outdated`) → block exactly as today (status `error`, problem = the code, entries kept, no drain until `retry()`). After a move: `set({ failures: 0, conflictRev: +1 })` and the loop continues (the rest keep saving, status ends `saved`, P2 "Your other edits are saved.") | Q-0502; Q-0511 e; Q-0540; Q-0631 (b); 03b rule 9; P299a D-Reason; `vault/mockups/S03bConflictList-wording.md` P2 |
| D-Move | `moveToConflicts(moves, now)`, one `outbox` transaction: per move, the entry at its key now; missing or `rev` ≠ the sent `rev` → skipped (the newer edit is refused on its own later); else the entry is deleted and the row put: `{ projectId, objectId: entry.id, reason, baseSeq: entry.baseSeq, serverSeq, lockEpoch: entry.lockEpoch, value: entry.value, refusedAt: now, state: 'listed', server: reason not_open ? 'device' : 'pending', serverId: <existing row's serverId> ?? null }` | Q-0502 "nothing is lost"; `outbox-idb.ts` `drop` |
| D-Record | At the end of every lock run (`tryRun(lockName, async () => { try { await loop(); } finally { await recordPending(); } })`), when not disposed and online: rows `state 'listed'` and `server 'pending'` from `listConflicts()`; a row whose `TextEncoder` byte length of `JSON.stringify(value.data)` > `MAX_RECORD_DATA_BYTES` (65,536) → `device`, not sent; the rest grouped by project (first-seen order), each group cut into chunks of `MAX_RECORD_CHANGES` (1,000), one `postConflicts` per chunk with changes in `listConflicts` order. Answers: `recorded` → `recorded` + `ids[i]`; refused 404 → `device` with reason `not_open` (Q-0631 (b)); refused 400 → `device` and `captureBrowserError(new Error('sync_conflict_record_refused'), 'outbox.record')`; other refused → pending; `failed` → pending and no more calls this pass. Then one `setConflictServer(updates)`; each orphan with a `serverId` gets one `removeServerConflict` (result ignored); `conflictRev + 1` when `updates` is not empty. A throw anywhere in the pass is caught and reported with `captureBrowserError(error, 'outbox.record')`; a storage throw goes through `storageFailed`. Inside the lock, so two tabs never record the same row | Q-0540 (one sync = one drain); Q-0531; P299a D-Cap, route row |
| D-Server | `setConflictServer(updates)`: row missing at the key → returned as an orphan (Keep theirs or Remove ran during the call); `refusedAt` equal → `server`, `serverId` (when not null) and `reason` (when given) applied; `refusedAt` different (a newer refusal) → only `serverId` set, `server` stays `pending` (the upsert keeps the same server id, P299a S2) | rule 18; P299a S2 `record_sync_conflicts` |
| D-Requeue | `requeue(row, baseSeq, now)`, one transaction: a stored row at the key whose `refusedAt` differs from `row.refusedAt` (a newer refusal) → nothing written, returns `{ kept: true }`; else (equal, or no stored row) returns `{ kept: false }` after: the row put with `state 'requeued'` (other fields kept); the outbox entry at the key, when present, gets `baseSeq` and `rev + 1` and keeps its newer value; else a new entry `{ projectId, id: objectId, baseSeq, lockEpoch: row.lockEpoch, value: row.value, rev: 1, queuedAt: now }` | Q-0511 c, d; Q-0648 (b) |
| D-Resolves | `resolves` is worked out at send time: after `pickBatch`, `listConflicts()`; for each sent entry a `requeued` row at its key with a `serverId` gives that id; the save body is `{ lockEpoch, changes, resolves }` with `resolves` only when not empty. `commit` deletes `requeued` rows at the saved keys (rev check not applied), in the same transaction | P299a D-Resolves; AC-EZD-299-11 |

security-review: yes. Areas: data access (device storage keyed per person and company, Q-0503; refused changes stored on the device and sent to the P299a routes), API (client calls only; no new route, Q-0631 (b)).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer yes · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
High: ordered async work across the outbox, the device list, the three P299a routes and the open editor, with races (record during Remove, refresh during actions) that tests must pin. Test-author Opus 5.5 medium; builder Opus 5.5 high.

## 9. Dependencies
Row: EZD-299a (planned, not built: section 3 types, `resolves`, the routes, `app_outdated`, the app-build header on saves), EZD-120b, EZD-120d, EZD-202 (done). Missing from the row: EZD-120c (`editor-session.ts`, done), EZD-024 (`captureBrowserError`, done). Not needed: EZD-016a (no visual checklist); EZD-006 and EZD-133 (no harness edit since Q-0631 (b) dropped the presence route). Open elsewhere: Q-0629 (EZD-294) option (c) would add renumbering of new objects to this ticket's Keep mine; if it is chosen, this plan is re-validated.
Risks: EZD-299 builds on section 3 (`session.conflicts`, `ConflictRow.actions`); changing `OutboxStorage` and `SyncState` breaks fakes in the three test files named in section 4; the editor bundle gains two small modules (`js-size:editor`). The membership header on `GET` and `DELETE /api/sync-conflicts` (EZD-299a routes) is not in this ticket: it is the separate fix ticket EZD-299c (round-1 review, 2026-11-09). D-Guard and the D-Requeue check close the device side (Q-0648 (b)). The two server-side races (a newer refusal's record POST upserting the same server id before Keep theirs' or Remove's DELETE, or before a Keep mine save's `resolves`, lands) and the membership header both go to EZD-299c (conditional DELETE and `resolves` on `updatedAt`, the record answer returns `updatedAt`); EZD-299b does not depend on it and adds no `updatedAt` wiring.
Done when every artifact is in: steps 1-9, the section 4 test files, the harness and fake edits, and the two architecture edits of D-Docs (L-057).

## 10. Open questions
None. Q-0648 (answered-agent, security-reviewer): option (b); the device-side part is in D-Requeue, D-KeepMine (sync), D-KeepMine (list) and D-Guard; the server-side part is EZD-299c (section 9).

Q-0631 is answered (b) (section 2) and applied in D-Settle, D-Move, D-Record, D-Api and section 3; Q-0632 (a) in D-Merge and `ConflictRow`.

# EZD-360 · Build system: phase 56 ranks right after phase 5 in the ledger tools and release order

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-360-1 (T1, T2), AC-EZD-360-2 (T3, T4, T5), AC-EZD-360-3 (T6, T7, T8, T9); from the Done-when below, via `node vault/tools/gen_acs.mjs`
- **Complexity:** medium
- **Areas:** tooling, scripts, process
- **User-visible result:** the AI assistant phase (56) is planned, built and released right after phase 5 and before phase 6, without renumbering any phase.
- **Fix mode:** the interactive orchestrator writes the guarded paths under `vault/handoff/LAUNCHER_FIX.md` (PROCESS.md rule 19; session 9 brief "How to build a guarded ticket interactively"). Status stays `ready`, so `next_ticket.mjs` holds it (`plan-paths.mjs`) and the launcher never builds it.
- Phase: 1 · Planned by: orchestrator (session 11) · Date: 2026-11-07 · Status: ready

## 1. What to build
One order for phases, in one exported function. Every phase has the rank of its own number except phase 56, whose rank is 5.5 (Josh 2026-11-07: "just name the ai phase 56 and build after 5"; Q-0630; phase-05-spec-gaps-for-josh.md, Josh's answers). Every place that orders phases numerically goes through it.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `vault/tools/phase-rank.mjs` (orchestrator) | new | `phaseRank(p: number): number`; `comparePhases(a: number, b: number): number` (`phaseRank(a) - phaseRank(b)`) | `vault/tools/security-paths.mjs` header comment (in vault/tools/ because the ledger test copies carry all of vault/) | `node --test vault/tools/phase-rank.test.mjs` |
| 2 | `vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs` (orchestrator) | change | none new | D-Sites below | `node --test scripts/ledger/phase-rank-order.test.mjs` |
| 3 | `scripts/release/tags.mjs` (orchestrator) | change | `compareReleaseTags` compares `phaseRank(pa.phase)`, then `pa.patch`; other exports unchanged | itself | `node --test scripts/release/__tests__/tags.test.mjs` |
| 4 | `vault/tools/security-paths.mjs` (orchestrator) | change | add `vault/tools/phase-rank.mjs` to the production-sensitive list | itself | `node --test scripts/release/__tests__/tags.test.mjs` |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Rank | `phaseRank(56)` is 5.5. Every other number returns itself, unchanged; no validation, no throw. A single constant map, one entry | Josh 2026-11-07; Q-0630 |
| D-Sites | In `next_ticket.mjs`: each `.sort((a, b) => a - b)` over phases uses `comparePhases`; each `a.phase - b.phase` uses `comparePhases(a.phase, b.phase)`; each `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` between two phases compares ranks; `Math.min` and `Math.max` over phases pick by rank and return the phase number, never the rank. Sites at the time of planning: lines 861, 868-869, 905, 913-915, 930, 952, 956-957, 1017, 1020, 1056, 1083, 1091, 1160, 1278 | session-11-brief.md open item 4 |
| D-Return | Functions that return a phase return its real number (56), never 5.5; the rank is used only to compare | prevents file names such as phase-5.5 |
| D-Tags | A release tag's format is unchanged. `phase-5.3` sorts before `phase-56`, `phase-56.2` before `phase-6`. `release-name.mjs` needs no change: it orders only through `compareReleaseTags` | `scripts/release/tags.mjs:19`; `scripts/release/release-name.mjs:8,29` |
| D-Import | `tags.mjs` imports `../../vault/tools/phase-rank.mjs`; release scripts already import from vault/tools | `scripts/release/release.mjs`, `github-ops.mjs` |

### Do not touch
`vault/tools/gen_acs.mjs` (its heading order is display only, and no unit reads it for order); `gate.mjs` and `ledger-copy.mjs` (exact-phase matches only); `RELEASE_TAG_RE`; `parseReleaseTag`.

Ticket row, copied from the phase file: Scope: one exported `phaseRank` used by every phase-order site in the ledger tools and the release tag order, so phase 56 sits between 5 and 6. Done when: phaseRank returns 5.5 for 56 and the number itself for any other phase. With tickets in phases 5, 56 and 6 the ledger works phase 5, then 56, then 6, and a function that returns a phase returns 56, never 5.5. Release tags order phase-5, phase-5.3, phase-56, phase-56.2, phase-6, and a Phase 6 pull request after phase-56 gets the tag phase-6, not not_newer. Depends on: none. Spec ref: Q-0630.

## 2. Sources
`vault/spec/decisions/05-screens.md` Q-0630; `vault/questions/phase-05-spec-gaps-for-josh.md` Josh's answers; `vault/handoff/session-11-brief.md` item 4; `vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs`; `scripts/release/tags.mjs`; `scripts/release/release-name.mjs`.

Architecture: Machine checks

## 3. Interface contract
| Kind | Name or path | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| export | `vault/tools/phase-rank.mjs` `phaseRank` | `(p: number) => number` per D-Rank |
| export | `vault/tools/phase-rank.mjs` `comparePhases` | `(a: number, b: number) => number`, negative when a comes first |
| export | `scripts/release/tags.mjs` `compareReleaseTags` | same signature; order per D-Tags |

## 4. Tests
Written by test-author before any code. Expected values come from Josh's instruction (phase 56 after 5, before 6) and the Decided table.
| Test | AC | Type | Input | Expected value | Source of the expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | AC-EZD-360-1 | unit, `vault/tools/phase-rank.test.mjs` | `phaseRank` of 0, 1, 5, 6, 55 and 56 | 0, 1, 5, 6, 55 and 5.5 | D-Rank |
| T2 | AC-EZD-360-1 | unit, same file | `[6, 56, 0, 5, 55].sort(comparePhases)` | `[0, 5, 56, 6, 55]` | D-Rank |
| T3 | AC-EZD-360-2 | unit, `scripts/ledger/phase-rank-order.test.mjs`, ledger copy as in `scripts/ledger/phase-overlap.test.mjs` | open product tickets in phases 5, 56 and 6, all signed off | the unit `--next-unit` gives names the phase 5 ticket | Josh 2026-11-07 |
| T4 | AC-EZD-360-2 | same file | phase 5 tickets all done and phase 5 wrapped; open in 56 and 6 | the next unit names the phase 56 ticket, not the phase 6 one; any phase number printed is `56`; the output has no `5.5` | Josh 2026-11-07; D-Return |
| T5 | AC-EZD-360-2 | same file | a ready tooling ticket in phase 6 while phase 56 is the blocking phase | it is not picked: the cap at line 913 treats phase 6 as later than 56 | D-Sites |
| T6 | AC-EZD-360-3 | unit, `scripts/release/__tests__/tags.test.mjs` | sort `phase-6`, `phase-56.2`, `phase-5`, `phase-56`, `phase-5.3` with `compareReleaseTags` | `phase-5`, `phase-5.3`, `phase-56`, `phase-56.2`, `phase-6` | D-Tags |
| T7 | AC-EZD-360-3 | unit, same file | `releaseTagFor({ prTitle: 'Phase 6: x', tags: ['phase-5', 'phase-56'], tagsOnSha: [] })` | `{ tag: 'phase-6', resume: false }` | D-Tags |
| T8 | AC-EZD-360-3 | unit, same file | `releaseTagFor({ prTitle: 'Phase 56: x', tags: ['phase-5'], tagsOnSha: [] })` | `{ tag: 'phase-56', resume: false }` | D-Tags |
| T9 | AC-EZD-360-3 | unit, same file | `releaseTagFor({ prTitle: 'Phase 56: x', tags: ['phase-6'], tagsOnSha: [] })` | `{ code: 'not_newer' }` | `release-name.mjs:13`, D-Tags |

## 5. Visual checklist
None.

## 6. Proposed wording
None.

## 7. Security review
security-review: yes. Areas touched: release order (`scripts/release/`).
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer always · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer yes

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
Medium: small code at many sites of the phase order, and a mistake stalls the launcher or a release. Test-author and builder as `--dispatch` gives; the builder's work is done by the orchestrator in fix mode.

## 9. Dependencies
None. Risk: the launcher keeps old code until restarted; a mid-run change of `next_ticket.mjs` takes effect at the next spawn because it runs as a child process. No phase 56 ticket exists until this merges, so the order does not change for any ticket on the day it lands.

# EZD-204 · Openings core (split proposal)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-204-1, AC-EZD-204-2, AC-EZD-204-3, AC-EZD-204-4, AC-EZD-204-5, AC-EZD-204-6, AC-EZD-204-7, AC-EZD-204-8, AC-EZD-204-9, AC-EZD-204-10, AC-EZD-204-11, AC-EZD-204-12, AC-EZD-204-13, AC-EZD-204-14, AC-EZD-204-15, shared out to the parts below
- **Complexity:** high (each part; section 8)
- **Areas:** data-model, migrations, testing
- **User-visible result:** Doors and windows have their full data (swing, hand, impact, rough opening mode). A door left off every wall stays put and draws red on the plan, and it clears when a wall touches it again. Placing doors comes with EZD-211.
- Phase: 5 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-07 · Status: split proposal

## Split proposal
**Why.** Planned whole, the ticket touches 27 files: 14 source and doc files, 4 new test files and 9 earlier test files that the v4 schema forces to change. That is over the size rule (PROCESS.md section 6 "Ticket size": about 20 files; Josh 2026-10-22). The cut follows EZD-221's: the stored data first, then the geometry and the flag. Sections 1 to 10 below stay the detailed plan, and each part's plan takes its rows from them unchanged. Build order a → b.

### Part EZD-204a · Opening data v4
- **Scope:** Build steps 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (exporting `./opening` only), 10, and 13 (only the Model schema line and the `### Openings (EZD-204)` Files and Flag bullets for `opening.ts`). Decided rows: Opening v4, Swing meaning, Hand meaning, `isVerticalLine` / `leftEndIsLow`, `axis` (stored values only), v3 → v4 step, v4.json, `autoRoughOpening`, `createOpeningData`, Flips, Benchmark, Docs (the parts named). `DEFAULT_DOOR_SWING` and the drawing stay as they are.
- **Tests (7 + 7 edits):** O1–O6, S1; E1, E2, E3, E5, E6, E7; E4 for the `opening()` helper only (T5 and T10 unchanged).
- **Files (17):** `schema/opening.ts`, `schema/migrate.ts`, `samples/v4.json`, `openings/opening.ts`, `openings/index.ts`, `G/index.ts`, `benchmark/benchmark.ts`, `docs/architecture.md`; `openings/opening.test.ts`, `opening-upgrade.db.test.ts`, `migrate.test.ts`, `wall-layers.test.ts`, `room.test.ts`, `walls/test-utils/fixtures.ts`, `benchmark.test.ts`, `model-schema.test.ts`, `drawing/build.test.ts`.
- **Done when:** a stored v3 door loads with Hinge left, swing left, Not rated and a typed rough opening, and its stored row is not rewritten (S1, O3); a new door or window is Existing with the Q-0630 sizes (O4).
- **ACs:** AC-EZD-204-5, -6, -14, -15 (data), -10 (data and flips).
- **Depends on:** EZD-203 (row); missing from the row: EZD-294 (section 9).
- **Complexity:** high: it raises the stored schema version with a migration and a sample (03b rule 5; EZD-205a precedent). Test-author opus-5-5 medium, builder opus-5-5 medium.
- **security-review: no.** **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor yes (sizes, rough opening) · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

### Part EZD-204b · Offsets, hosting and the Not on a wall flag
- **Scope:** Build steps 5, 6, 7 (adding `./offsets`, `./hosting`), 8, 9, 11, 12, and 13 (the Drawing list bullets and the Openings Rule bullet). Decided rows: every row not listed in part a, plus `axis` (drawing and re-host).
- **Tests (14 + 1 edit):** F1–F6, H1–H4, D1, D2, M1, B1; E4 for T5 and T10.
- **Files (13):** `openings/offsets.ts`, `openings/hosting.ts`, `openings/index.ts`, `drawing/types.ts`, `drawing/build.ts`, `A/editor/plan/batches.ts`, `A/editor/tools/model-changes.ts`, `docs/architecture.md`; `offsets.test.ts`, `hosting.test.ts`, `drawing/build.test.ts`, `model-changes.test.ts`, `batches.test.ts`.
- **Done when:** the ticket Done-when (H1): moving a wall away flags the opening, which then draws on the red `flagged` layer (H1, B1).
- **ACs:** AC-EZD-204-1, -2, -3, -4, -7, -8, -9, -11, -12, -13; -10 and -15 for the door symbol (D2).
- **Depends on:** EZD-204a, EZD-203 (row), EZD-294 (`wallEditChanges` signature); done: EZD-238 (`build.ts`), EZD-207a (`batches.ts`), EZD-210a (`model-changes.ts`).
- **Complexity:** high: a hosting algorithm wired into every wall edit, plus the offset and tolerance geometry. Test-author opus-5-5 medium, builder opus-5-5 medium.
- **security-review: no.** **Reviewers:** code-reviewer · calc-auditor yes (offsets, tolerance, rounding, symbol geometry) · ui-verifier no (section 5) · security-reviewer no.

## 1. What to build
Short names: `G` = `packages/geometry/src`, `A` = `app/src`, `tol` = `COMPARISON_TOLERANCE_IN` (1/64", inclusive; `G/tolerance.ts`, 03g). Ids are compared lower-cased and "first id" means the smallest lower-cased id (Q-0595 (a); EZD-203 s3 id rule). This plan builds on EZD-294 merged (section 9). `openingDataSchema` keeps EZD-294's `attributes.number`.

Data: no table, SQL or RLS change. Model schema v3 → v4 (03b rule 5; ARCH Model schema version rule). New opening fields, Decided "Opening v4".

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `G/schema/opening.ts` | change | `DOOR_SWINGS = ['left','right'] as const`, `DOOR_HANDS = ['left','right'] as const`, `IMPACT_RATINGS = ['not_rated','impact_rated','shutter'] as const`, `SHUTTER_TYPES = ['accordion','roll_down','storm_panel','colonial','bahama'] as const`, `ROUGH_OPENING_MODES = ['auto','typed'] as const`, `AXIS_UNIT_TOLERANCE = 1e-9`, types `DoorSwing`, `DoorHand`, `ImpactRating`, `ShutterType`, `RoughOpeningMode`; `openingDataShape` (the strict object, no refine) and `openingDataSchema = openingDataShape.refine(…)` per Decided "Opening v4" (any merged EZD-294 code that reads `.shape` reads `openingDataShape`); `OpeningData` | `G/schema/wall.ts` (strictObject + `.refine`) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/openings/opening.test.ts` |
| 2 | `G/schema/migrate.ts` | change | `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4`; private `migrateV3ToV4: MigrateStep`; `MIGRATIONS[3]` | `migrateV1ToV2` in the same file | same + `src/schema` |
| 3 | `G/schema/samples/v4.json` | new | the document from Decided "v4.json" | `samples/v3.json` | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/schema` |

| 5 | `G/openings/offsets.ts` | new | `type HostCorner = { at: number; wallId: string \| null }`; `hostCorners(host: WallObject, walls: readonly WallObject[]): HostCorner[]`; `openingSpan(o: OpeningObject, host: WallObject): { along: number; lo: number; hi: number; across: number } \| null`; `openingOnWall(o: OpeningObject, wall: WallObject): boolean`; `type OpeningOffsets = { left: number; right: number; leftCorner: HostCorner; rightCorner: HostCorner }`; `openingOffsets(o: OpeningObject, host: WallObject, walls: readonly WallObject[]): OpeningOffsets \| null`; `type PlaceAtOffsetInput = { host: WallObject; walls: readonly WallObject[]; openings: readonly OpeningObject[]; width: number; near: Point; side: 'left' \| 'right'; offset: number; ignoreId: string \| null }`; `placeAtOffset(input: PlaceAtOffsetInput): { ok: true; center: Point } \| { ok: false; reason: 'invalid_input' \| 'past_corner' \| 'overlap' }` | `G/walls/joins.ts` (`onInterior` maths) | same |
| 6 | `G/openings/hosting.ts` | new | `openingHostUpdates(input: { level: string; walls: readonly WallObject[]; previousWalls: readonly WallObject[]; openings: readonly OpeningObject[] }): OpeningObject[]` | `G/rooms/sync.ts` (pure, returns new objects) | same |
| 7 | `G/openings/index.ts`; `G/index.ts` | new; change | barrel `export * from './opening'; './offsets'; './hosting'`; root adds `export * from './openings'` | `G/walls/index.ts` | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry run typecheck` |
| 8 | `G/drawing/types.ts` | change | `DrawingLayer` gains `'flagged'`; `DEFAULT_DOOR_SWING` and its comment removed | none | same |
| 9 | `G/drawing/build.ts` | change | `buildDrawingList` unchanged signature; Decided "Door symbol", "Flagged opening" | the door branch in the same file | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/drawing` |
| 10 | `G/benchmark/benchmark.ts` | change | `DOOR`, `WINDOW` gain the v4 attributes; each opening's geometry gains `axis: null` | itself | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/benchmark` |
| 11 | `A/editor/plan/batches.ts` | change | `LAYER_TOKEN` gains `flagged: '--ez-red'` | itself | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/editor/plan/batches.test.ts` |
| 12 | `A/editor/tools/model-changes.ts` | change | `wallEditChanges` keeps EZD-294's signature `(objects, level, walls, newId, highs)`; Decided "wallEditChanges" | `roomChange` in the same file | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/editor/tools` |
| 13 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | Decided "Docs" | the `### Rooms (EZD-205a)` section | `node vault/tools/outline.mjs docs/architecture.md --section 'Openings (EZD-204)'` |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening v4 | `geometry: { center: Point; hostWallId: uuid \| null; axis: Point \| null }`. `attributes` adds `swing: DoorSwing \| null`, `hand: DoorHand \| null`, `impactRating: ImpactRating`, `shutterType: ShutterType \| null` and `roughOpeningMode: RoughOpeningMode`. `kind`, `width`, `height`, `roughOpening`, `sillHeight` and EZD-294's `number?` are unchanged (width, height and roughOpening are positive; sill is `min(0)`). One `.refine` makes four rules: (a) a door has both `swing` and `hand` non-null, and a window has both null; (b) a non-null `shutterType` needs `impactRating === 'shutter'`, and with `'shutter'` a null `shutterType` is allowed; (c) a non-null `hostWallId` needs `axis === null`; (d) a non-null `axis` has `Math.abs(Math.hypot(x, y) - 1) <= AXIS_UNIT_TOLERANCE`. Any failure is the `invalid_data` issue. | Q-0630 rows 4, 5, 14, 38; Q-0633 shutter list, typed-or-auto; Q-0640 flag; Q-0508 (record shape is a build choice) |
| Swing meaning | `'left'`/`'right'` = the side of the line the door opens to, walking the host wall start→end, or along `axis` while flagged. | Q-0642 row 2 ("wall's left side, walking start to end") |
| Hand meaning | `'left'` = Hinge left = the opening end with the smaller plan x. When `isVerticalLine` of the wall is true, the end with the larger y (Hinge top). | Q-0640; Q-0641 row 1; Q-0642 row 3 |
| `isVerticalLine` / `leftEndIsLow` | `coordsEqual(line.start.x, line.end.x)`. `leftEndIsLow(d, vertical)` = `vertical ? d.y < 0 : d.x > 0`. "Low" is the end at the smaller distance along `d`. | Q-0642 row 3; 03g |
| `axis` | It is null while hosted, so the host gives the direction and the two cannot drift apart. When an opening leaves every wall, it is set to the unit start→end direction of its previous host. It goes back to null on re-hosting. Stored v3 data upgrades to null. A flagged opening with a null axis is drawn along `{ x: 1, y: 0 }`. | 04 Selection, undo and flags ("stay put"); board S03dStates tile "Door no longer on a wall"; rule 18 |
| v3 → v4 step | Copies `data`, `data.geometry` and `data.attributes` only. If `type === 'opening'` and all three are records, then `geometry.axis = null`. If `attributes.kind === 'door'`, set swing and hand to `'left'`; otherwise set both to null. Also set `impactRating: 'not_rated'`, `shutterType: null`, `roughOpeningMode: 'typed'`. Every other object is returned at version 4 with its `data` by reference. Never mutate the input. | AC-EZD-204-6, -15; Q-0641 row 3; Q-0642 row 2; EZD-203 plan-gap (copy only the changed levels) |
| v4.json | Run once from the repo root, then `pnpm exec prettier --write packages/geometry/src/schema/samples/v4.json`: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const p="packages/geometry/src/schema/samples/";const d=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p+"v3.json","utf8"));for(const o of d.objects){o.schema_version=4;if(o.type==="opening"){const door=o.data.attributes.kind==="door";o.data.geometry.axis=null;Object.assign(o.data.attributes,{swing:door?"left":null,hand:door?"left":null,impactRating:"not_rated",shutterType:null,roughOpeningMode:"typed"});}}fs.writeFileSync(p+"v4.json",JSON.stringify(d,null,2)+"\n")'`. Never edit it after merge. | ARCH Model schema (`samples/v<n>.json`) |
| `autoRoughOpening` | Door: width + 2, height + 2.5. Window: width + 0.5, height + 0.5. | Q-0630 (Josh, question 1, row 3) |
| `createOpeningData` | `hostWallId = host.id`, `axis = null`, `level = host.data.level`, `center` copied, `status: 'existing'`, `impactRating: 'not_rated'`, `shutterType: null`, `roughOpeningMode: 'auto'`, `roughOpening = autoRoughOpening(kind, size)`. Door: `DEFAULT_DOOR_SIZE`, `sillHeight: 0`, `hand: 'left'`, `swing: input.swing ?? 'left'`. Window: `DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE`, `sillHeight: DEFAULT_WINDOW_SILL_IN`, swing and hand null (`input.swing` is ignored). No `number` (EZD-211 numbers it, EZD-294 N7). No validation of `center`. | Q-0630 (sizes); Q-0630 row 6, AC-14; Q-0641 row 3; door sill 0 as in `samples/v1.json` and EZD-236 `DOOR` |
| Flips | `flipSwing` and `flipHand` toggle `'left'`↔`'right'` on a copy, and every other value stays deep-equal, `center` included (the offset is kept). On a window they return `null`. | Q-0630 row 4; Q-0633 row 2; AC-10 |
| `openingSpan` | `L = wallLength(host.data.geometry)`. If `L <= tol`, the result is `null`. With `d` the unit start→end vector, `along = (c − start)·d`, `across = |(c − start)×d|`, `lo = along − width/2`, `hi = along + width/2`. | 03g |
| `openingOnWall` | True when the opening's level equals the wall's level (lower-cased), the span is not null, `across <= tol`, `lo >= −tol` and `hi <= L + tol`. A partial overhang is off. | Q-0630 row 5; 09k On a wall, Partial overhang |
| `hostCorners` | Returns `[]` when `L <= tol`. Otherwise it holds `{ at: 0 }` and `{ at: L }`. Their `wallId` is the first `otherId` among `findWallJoins(walls, host.id)` joins of kind `corner` or `tee-into` at that end, else `null`. For each join of kind `tee-on` or `cross`, take both of that wall's `wallFaceLines` and intersect each, as an infinite line, with the host line. Skip a face whose direction cross product with the host is exactly 0, and keep only `tol < at < L − tol`, with `wallId` = that wall. Sort by `at`, then by `wallId` (null first, then lower-cased). | Q-0630 row 1 (corner = wall end or face of a wall teeing in); Q-0570 and Q-0598 (a) (a crossing is a join); 09k Tee |
| `openingOffsets` | Returns `null` unless `openingOnWall(o, host)`. `low` = last corner with `at <= lo + tol`; `high` = first corner with `at >= hi − tol`. `lowDist = max(0, lo − low.at)`, `highDist = max(0, high.at − hi)`. If `leftEndIsLow(d, isVerticalLine(host line))`, then left = low side; otherwise left = high side. | Q-0630 row 1; Q-0636; Q-0640 |
| `placeAtOffset` | Returns `invalid_input` when width, offset or near is not finite, when `width <= 0` or `offset < 0`, or when `hostCorners` is `[]`. Let `s = clamp(along of near, 0, L)` and `i` = last corner index with `at <= s`, clamped to `0 … n−2`. The bay is `corners[i]`, `corners[i+1]`. When `side` maps to the low end, `lo = bay low + offset`, `hi = lo + width`, and `hi − bayHigh.at > tol` gives `past_corner`. Otherwise `hi = bayHigh.at − offset`, `lo = hi − width`, and `bayLow.at − lo > tol` gives `past_corner`. Then for each opening whose `hostWallId` equals `host.id` and whose id is not `ignoreId`: `min(hi, ohi) − max(lo, olo) > tol` gives `overlap`. On success `center = start + d·(lo + hi)/2`. | Q-0630 row 1 (0" accepted, past the end refused, overlap over 1/64" refused, exact fit accepted); Q-0630 row 14; 09k Offset rows |
| Door crossing a tee face | Refused as `past_corner`, because a tee face is a corner and the other side cannot be negative. | Q-0630 row 1 corner definition; 09k Offset maximum |
| `openingHostUpdates` | Uses walls and openings on `level` only. Openings are taken in first-id order. Pass 1: a hosted opening whose host (by id in `walls`) still passes `openingOnWall` stays put, and its span counts as taken on that wall. Every other opening is off, and its `oldDir` is the unit direction of its host in `previousWalls`, else in `walls`, else `{1,0}`; for an opening already flagged, `oldDir` = `axis ?? {1,0}`. Pass 2: each off opening, in id order, takes the first-id wall where `openingOnWall` is true and no taken span overlaps it by more than `tol`. On a re-host: `hostWallId` = that wall, `axis: null`, and `swing` is toggled when `dir(wall)·oldDir < 0` (a door's leaf stays on its side); the new span counts as taken. With no wall found: `hostWallId: null` and `axis = oldDir`. `center`, `hand` and every other value stay. Returns only the openings whose `hostWallId`, `axis` or `swing` changed, as new objects, in id order. Never mutates its input. | Q-0630 row 5 (re-host on contact, ties to the first id); Q-0633 row G12 (a span another opening holds leaves it off); Q-0630 row 38 (a deleted host leaves it off); 04 "stay put" |
| `wallEditChanges` | `before = toModelObjects(objects, level)` is computed before the walls are replaced. The openings come from parsing each `objects` value of type `opening` on `level` with `parseStoredObject` (a private `openingsOn` helper; unparsable values are skipped). `previousWalls` = walls of `before`; `walls` = walls of `next`. The result is `[...walls.map(wallChange), ...roomChanges(rec), ...openingHostUpdates(...).map(openingChange)]`, with a private `openingChange` built like `roomChange`. Every caller passes this one array to one `applyEdit`, so the wall change and the flag form one undo step. `toModelObjects` is unchanged. | AC-12; ARCH Drawing tools ("every wall edit goes through `wallEditChanges`"); `A/editor/model/model-store.ts` (one `applyEdit` = one edit) |
| Door symbol | It takes the host frame `f` (or the flagged frame) with `sc`, `w = width` and `vertical`. `hingeLow = (hand === 'left') === leftEndIsLow(f.d, vertical)`; `sh = sc ∓ w/2` (minus when `hingeLow`). The face is `f.oL` for swing left and `f.oR` for swing right; `k = +1` for left and `−1` for right. `hinge = at(f, sh, face)`. The leaf is a `cut` line from `hinge` to `hinge + f.n·k·w`. `u = hingeLow ? f.d : −f.d` and `v = k·f.n`. The arc (`hidden`) has centre `hinge` and radius `w`; `startAngle = degrees(cross(u,v) > 0 ? u : v)` normalised to `[0, 360)`, and `endAngle = startAngle + 90`. Hosted doors use `vertical = isVerticalLine(host line)`. Item order per door: leaf, then arc. Windows are unchanged. | Q-0574 (the default is replaced in EZD-204); Q-0642 rows 2, 3; 09h roles |
| Flagged opening | `hostWallId === null`: drawn instead of omitted. Its frame is `start = center`, `d = axis ?? {1,0}`, `n = (−d.y, d.x)`, `oL = oR = 0`, `sc = 0`, `vertical = Math.abs(d.x · width) <= tol`. Items on layer `'flagged'`: a `cut` bar from `at(−w/2)` to `at(+w/2)`, then for a door the leaf and arc. The items go after every hosted symbol, in document order. A non-null host that is missing (`host_not_found`) or off its span (`not_on_wall`) is still omitted as before. | AC-4; Q-0630 row 27 (the whole object turns error red); board S03dStates |
| Colour | `flagged` → `--ez-red` (`app/src/styles/tokens.css` `oklch(0.6 0.19 28)`). Batch order 3, as the other segment layers. | 04 Frame and visual system; Q-0026 |

security-review: no. No table, SQL, route, permission or money change. The server's existing parse (`saveObjects`, `loadModel`) takes the stricter schema unchanged.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
high: a schema version raise with a migration and a sample, a new hosting algorithm wired into every wall edit, door drawing rules, and 9 earlier test files to edit. Each part is high (Split proposal). test-author opus-5-5 medium; builder opus-5-5 medium (EZD-203 and EZD-205a precedent).

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-203 (row), done.
- **EZD-294 (missing from the row).** Both edit the strict `openingDataSchema` and `wallEditChanges`; this plan keeps EZD-294's `number?`, the `highs` argument and `NO_NUMBERS` (EZD-294 s3). It is `ready`, build position 101.7 < 102.
- Risks: (1) `wallEditChanges` now parses the level's openings on every wall edit, about 381 per floor on the benchmark, O(1) each plus a wall scan for off openings only (11 Budgets: typed commit 50 ms; 11 rule 2). (2) EZD-217's delete and paste must call `openingHostUpdates` (section 3 dependents). (3) EZD-5602's send list must classify `axis` and `roughOpeningMode`. (4) Any develop test added after this plan that builds opening data needs the five fields (section 4 grep).
