| 11 | `S/floors/FloorSwitcher.tsx`, `S/floors/FloorSwitcher.module.css` | new | `FloorSwitcherProps = { store: ModelStore; floors: FloorView; canEdit: boolean; newId?: () => string }`; `FloorSwitcher(props): ReactElement` | `S/plan/ZoomStack.tsx` (office editor control, `useT`, `touch.module.css`); `useStore` as in `S/EmptyPlanHint.tsx` | `vitest run src/editor/floors/FloorSwitcher.test.tsx` |
| 12 | `S/ProjectEditor.tsx` | change | ready state gains `floors: FloorView` | the `createDrawingController` call in the load effect | `pnpm build && pnpm test:e2e -- e2e/floors.spec.ts` |
| 13 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | new `### Floors (EZD-6001)` after `### Rooms (EZD-205a)`; in "Patch store and outbox" add D-Batch and D-Stamp to the Sync bullet; in "Selection (EZD-208)" "open floor" = the chosen floor (D-Open) | `### Rooms (EZD-205a)` | review |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-List | `listFloors`: every object with `type === 'floor'` that parses with `parseStoredObject` (as `parsedObjects` in `batches.ts`), as `{ id, name, order }`, sorted by `order` ascending then `id` ascending. | `batches.ts` `lowestFloor` tie rule; `floor.ts` comment "unique order left to the floor tools" |
| D-Open | `resolveOpenFloor`: `chosen` when it equals (lower-case compare) a listed floor id, returned in the listed spelling; else the first listed floor; else `null`. The open floor at load is therefore the lowest floor, today's behaviour. A choice does not outlive a reload: every open starts on the lowest floor, so `createFloorView()` starts at `{ chosenId: null }` and saves nothing (no storage, no column, no route). | `batches.ts` `openFloorId`; Q-0690 (a); 03 Q-0664 "eye toggles … device session … reset on reload" (precedent) |
| D-Store | `createFloorView`: `zustand/vanilla`; `setOpenFloor(id)` sets `chosenId` and does nothing when the value is unchanged (no notify). Never saved, never sent. One per editor session, made in the `ProjectEditor` load effect beside the controllers. | Q-0667 "floor switcher … display only" for view-only; ARCH Selection "State. Session only" |
| D-Wire | Each controller of steps 3-5 computes its floor as `openFloorId(objects, floors?.getState().chosenId ?? null)`. It subscribes to `floors` (when given) and, on a change of the resolved open floor, runs the same steps its model-store subscription runs for a changed floor: plan controller `hover.sync(objects, floor, [])`, `rebuild()`, selection and text steps, `updateHover(true)`, `redraw()`; selection controller `index.sync(objects, floor, [])` then selection `[]` (its existing `floorChanged` branch); drawing controller recompute `level`, `models`, a new `createWallSnapIndex`, `drawingIds`, `setUi({ boxes })`. Store subscriptions keep their `objects` early return; `dispose` unsubscribes. No `floors` = lowest floor, so existing tests pass unedited. `ProjectEditor` passes its `FloorView` to every controller it creates, including ones wired by other tickets first (EZD-208b). | Q-0509 "the canvas shows one floor at a time"; `hover.ts` and `pick-index.ts` already rebuild on a new `floorId` |
| D-Draw-switch | When the open floor changes while a drawing tool has a chain or rectangle started, the drawing controller does what Escape does in `keyDown` (`input({ type: 'escape' })`, `emitFrame()`), and a pick in progress ends as its Escape branch does. The tool stays selected. | 03f every object has one `level`; `drawing-controller.ts` `keyDown` Escape |
| D-Hint | `EmptyPlanHint` with `floors`: shown when `hasNoWallsOn(objects, openFloorId(objects, chosenId))` (no wall whose raw `data.level` matches, lower-case); `hasNoWallsOn(objects, null)` = `true`. Without `floors`, `hasNoWalls` as now. | Q-0591 (a) via EZD-221b "over a plan with no walls"; Q-0509 |
| D-Add | Add floor (Edit model only): `id = newId()` (`newObjectId` from `S/tools/model-changes.ts`); `name = t('office.floors.default_name', { n: nextFloorOrder(objects) })`; `addFloorChange` returns `{ id, value: { type: 'floor', schemaVersion: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, data: { name, order: nextFloorOrder(objects) } } }`; `nextFloorOrder` = highest listed `order` + 1, or 1 with no floor. One `store.applyEdit([change])` (one undo step), then `floors.setOpenFloor(id)`. New floors go last; reordering floors is not in Q-0509's list and is not built. | Q-0509 "add"; migration's "Floor 1"/order 1 naming; design brief Board 2 "Add floor names the new floor 'Floor N' and switches to it" (wording for Josh, section 6) |
| D-Rename | Rename acts on the open floor. Text field prefilled with its name; Enter or blur commits, Escape cancels with no edit. `renameFloorChange`: trims; returns `null` (no edit, old name shown) when the trimmed name is empty, equals the current name, or `id` is not a listed floor; else `{ id, value: { type: 'floor', schemaVersion: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, data: { name: trimmed, order: <kept> } } }`, one `applyEdit`. No length cap beyond `floorDataSchema` (`min(1)`, no max), as room names (P218); a long name shows cut with an ellipsis (`text-overflow: ellipsis`). Duplicate names are allowed. | Q-0509 "rename"; `floor.ts`; EZD-218 plan "Room edits" (trim, Enter/blur/Escape) |
| D-Delete | Delete acts on the open floor. `objectsOnFloor(objects, floorId)`: ids of every non-floor object whose raw `data.level` (a string) equals `floorId` lower-case, parsed or not, sorted ascending. `deleteFloorChanges`: `null` when `floorId` is not listed or is the only listed floor; else the deletes of `objectsOnFloor` then the floor's delete (`value: null`). The switcher: last floor → Delete shown disabled with the reason `office.floors.last_floor` (AC-3); 0 objects → delete at once, no question; ≥1 → `useConfirm()` with `title: 'office.floors.delete_title'`, `message: 'office.floors.delete_message'`, `params: { name, count }`, `confirmLabel: 'office.floors.delete_confirm'`, `tone: 'danger'`; `'cancel'` → nothing. Confirmed: one `applyEdit` (one undo step), then `floors.setOpenFloor(resolveOpenFloor(<objects after>, null))` (the lowest remaining floor). Undo restores the floor and its objects in one step and leaves the open floor as it is. | Q-0509 "deleting a floor that still has objects asks first and deletes them with it"; AC-3; ARCH State components (`useConfirm`); `model_object_level_check` (b) reads raw `data ->> 'level'` |
| D-Invalid | Objects the load reports in `invalid` are not in the store, so they are not deleted with a floor; if one names it, the server refuses the save (`level_not_found`, 400 `invalid_object`) and the refused changes go to the conflict list like any refusal (EZD-299b). No new handling. | P202 contract `parseModelDocument`; ARCH "Sync conflicts on the device" |
| D-Batch | `pickBatch` (`outbox.ts`): after choosing the oldest entry's project and lock generation as now, it orders that project's eligible entries with every entry whose `value?.type === 'floor'` first (their own queue order kept), then the rest in queue order, and only then applies `MAX_CHANGES_PER_SAVE` (100) and the baseSeq-0 drop rule. A floor (new, restored or renamed) is then always saved before or with the objects that name it. | `model_object_level_check` (a); ARCH Patch store "at most 100 changes"; CLAUDE.md rule 18 |
| D-Stamp | `put` (`outbox-idb.ts`): a change with `value === null` whose id holds a floor (the existing entry's `value?.type === 'floor'`, or else the `working_copy` mirror row's `value?.type === 'floor'`) is written with `queuedAt: now + 1`, for a new entry and for an existing one (which otherwise keeps its `queuedAt`). So a floor delete sorts after the deletes of its objects queued by the same edit (all `queuedAt: now`), whatever the ids. | `model_object_level_check` (b): "a floor deleted … while a live object names it" refuses; batches split at 100 |
| D-Switcher | Contents (section 3 testids): trigger showing the open floor's name; opened, the floor list in `listFloors` order with the open one marked; with `canEdit` only, below the list Add floor, Rename floor, Delete floor. Choosing a floor calls `floors.setOpenFloor(id)` and closes the list. View-only (`canEdit` false): the list only, no edit item rendered (AC-4; Q-0667; Q-0664 "Views and permissions"). Rendered when `showPlan` (as `ZoomStack`): absent while loading, on load failure, no access, not found, and when the canvas failed. Text through `useT()` with `office.floors.*` keys. Every control is a 44 px target under a coarse pointer (`touch.module.css` `target`; Q-0630 tablet rule; L-060). Placement, list container and position, sizes and colours: Q-0666 / board S03e. | Q-0509; Q-0666 |
| D-Keys | The open list follows ARCH "Menus (EZD-108)" keys and closing: click, Enter, Space or ArrowDown on the trigger open it on the open floor's option; ArrowDown / ArrowUp wrap, Home, End; Escape closes and focuses the trigger; Tab closes; a press outside closes. Roles: trigger `button` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`; list `role="menu"`; floor options `role="menuitemradio"` with `aria-checked`; actions `role="menuitem"`; the disabled Delete keeps focus but does nothing when chosen. | ARCH Menus (EZD-108); WAI-ARIA APG menu button |
| D-Rename-UI | Choosing Rename floor closes the list and shows `floor-name-input` in the trigger's place, prefilled with the name, focused, text selected; after commit or cancel the trigger returns and takes focus. | D-Rename; brief Board 2 "Rename edits the name in place" |
| D-Case | Every id compare in `floors.ts` (`resolveOpenFloor`, `renameFloorChange`, `deleteFloorChanges`, `objectsOnFloor`) is lower-case; changes use the listed spelling of the floor id. | `batches.ts`, `hover.ts` lower-case compares; level check `lower(...)` |
| D-Gone | When an undo, redo, delete or `applyRemote` removes the chosen floor, each controller's model-store subscription (objects changed) recomputes `openFloorId(objects, chosenId)`, gets the lowest floor and takes its floor-change branch; `chosenId` is left as it is, so a redo that brings the floor back opens it again (D-Open). The switcher reads both stores (`useStore`) and shows the resolved floor. | D-Open; D-Wire |
| D-Mount | `ProjectEditor` mounts `<FloorSwitcher store floors canEdit />` in the place Q-0666 picks: (a) first child of `StatusBar`'s `start` (before EZD-214a's View control); (b) top of the Layers tab (EZD-218b's panel file); (c) a part of `EditorHeader`'s `subtitle`. Until Q-0666 is answered this ticket is not built. | Q-0666; `StatusBar.tsx` `start`; EZD-218 plan "Dependents" |

### Do not touch
- `app/src/app/(editor)/dev/saves/[id]/SaveBench.tsx` (its own `lowestFloor`; test page).
- Server save path, `save_objects`, `model_object_level_check` and every migration.
- `OutboxEntry`, `Batch`, `OutboxStorage` shapes; `requeue`, `commit`, `drop`, `moveToConflicts`.

# EZD-366 · Fix: a crafted wall or opening number cannot stop a project from taking new walls

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-366-1, AC-EZD-366-2
- **Complexity:** medium
- **Areas:** data-model, migrations, security, testing
- **User-visible result:** a project where someone saved a wall or door numbered 2147483647 still takes new walls and doors, and no number already stored changes.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-09 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
The rule, decided by the planner as the ticket row asks (Q-0625 (a), Q-0629 (b), Q-0650; CLAUDE.md rule 18): **when a key's highest stored number + 1 is above 2147483647, the number trigger gives the lowest whole number from 1 that no row of that project and key holds (deleted rows counted). It refuses with 22023 only when every number from 1 to 2147483647 is taken.** Every other branch of the trigger stays as it is (keep the stored number on update; keep a sent number that is unused and at most 2147483647; otherwise highest + 1). Each new row takes one number, so a project would need 2147483647 rows of one key before a new object is refused, and no sent number can bring that about. In the same pass, the schema and the device numbering stop at the same bound (D3 (a), CLAUDE.md rule 18).

Data: one forward-only migration that replaces the body of `private.model_object_number()` (same signature, same trigger, same index). No table, column, policy, grant or `schema_version` change. No `update`, no backfill call: stored numbers are untouched (AC-EZD-366-2).

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `packages/geometry/src/numbers.ts` | change | add `export const NUMBER_MAX = 2147483647;`; `numberNewObjects` signature unchanged; one private (not exported) helper `withoutObjectNumber<T extends NumberedLike>(o: T): T` | `withObjectNumber` in the same file | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/numbers.test.ts` (B2) |
| 2 | `packages/geometry/src/schema/wall.ts` | change | `attributes.number: z.int().min(1).max(NUMBER_MAX).optional()`; `import { NUMBER_MAX } from '../numbers';` | line 33 itself | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry exec vitest run src/numbers.test.ts` (B1) |
| 3 | `packages/geometry/src/schema/opening.ts` | change | `attributes.number: z.int().min(1).max(NUMBER_MAX).optional()`; same import | line 44 itself | same (B1) |
| 4 | `supabase/migrations/<ts>_object_number_free_fallback.sql` | new | `create or replace function private.model_object_number()` exactly as SQL F1 below; then `revoke all on function private.model_object_number() from public;` | `supabase/migrations/20261109100000_number_model_objects.sql` (the function and its revoke) | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/server/model/object-numbers.db.test.ts` (D1-D4, R1-R9) |
| 5 | `docs/architecture.md` (`### Model working copy (EZD-120a)`, bullet **Object numbers**) | change | none; text D-Doc below | the bullet itself | `pnpm run lint` |
| 6 | `vault/debt.md` (orchestrator, at merge) | change | row D-099 status `closed: EZD-366 <commit>` | rows D-086, D-097 (closed in be714103) | `node vault/tools/next_ticket.mjs --check` |

**SQL F1** (run on the pinned local PostgreSQL 17.11 inside a rolled-back transaction at plan time, L-009). This is the 20261109100000 body with the lines from `if v_top > 2147483647 then` through its `end if;` replaced by:
```sql
  if v_top > 2147483647 then
    select c.n into v_top
    from (
      select 1::numeric as n
      union all
      select private.object_number(o.type, o.data) + 1
      from public.model_object o
      where o.project_id = new.project_id and private.object_number_key(o.type, o.data) = v_key
        and private.object_number(o.type, o.data) < 2147483647
    ) c
    where not exists (
      select 1 from public.model_object u
      where u.project_id = new.project_id and private.object_number_key(u.type, u.data) = v_key
        and private.object_number(u.type, u.data) = c.n
    )
    order by c.n
    limit 1;
    if v_top is null then
      raise exception 'object_number_out_of_range' using errcode = '22023';
    end if;
  end if;
```
Keep the declare block, the `language plpgsql volatile security definer set search_path = ''` header and every other line of the function as they are. Plan-time run: walls sent as 2147483647, unnumbered, 5 (deleted), then four sent as 2147483647 in one insert, came out 2147483647, 1, 5, 2, 3, 4, 6.

**D-Doc** (append this sentence after the last sentence of the **Object numbers** bullet, same line): `When highest + 1 is above 2147483647 the trigger gives the lowest number from 1 that no row of the key holds, deleted rows counted, and refuses with 22023 only when none is free; the schema caps \`number\` at \`NUMBER_MAX\` (2147483647) and \`numberNewObjects\` leaves a new object unnumbered once its key's high is 2147483647, so the server numbers it (EZD-366; D-099).`

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recovery rule | Lowest unused number from 1 when highest + 1 is above 2147483647; candidates are 1 and each stored number + 1 below 2147483647; smallest candidate no row holds | ticket row ("planner picks the rule"); Q-0625 (a) never reused (a number no row ever held was never given); Q-0650 (nothing above 2147483647 written) |
| Refusal | 22023 `object_number_out_of_range` only when the lookup finds no candidate; `saveObjects` keeps mapping 22023 to `{ ok: false, code: 'invalid_input' }` (`app/src/server/model/model.ts:241`, unchanged) | Q-0650; 20261109100000 migration |
| Sent number rule | Unchanged: a sent number from 1 to 2147483647 that no row of the key holds is kept, even above highest + 1 | Q-0629 (b) "keeps the sent number if unused" |
| Update rule | Unchanged: an update with the same key keeps the stored number | Q-0629 (b); EZD-294 R4 |
| Deleted rows | Counted in the free-number lookup (no `deleted` filter), as in the existing lookups | Q-0629 (b) "deleted rows counted" |
| Several new rows in one save | Each row's trigger sees the rows inserted before it in the same statement (row-level BEFORE trigger, volatile function); tests compare such numbers as a sorted list | PostgreSQL trigger visibility rules; EZD-294 R6 relies on the same |

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
Medium: three small code edits, but a security-definer trigger change with ordering inside one statement and database tests that must fail on the old trigger. Test-author: Sonnet. Builder: Sonnet.

## 9. Dependencies
- EZD-294 (done; its trigger, schema field and helpers are what this ticket changes). None missing from the ticket row; no visual checklist, so no EZD-016a.
- Risks: a device that queued a wall numbered above 2147483647 before this deploy gets `invalid_object` on its next save. This happens only in a project poisoned before the deploy, and only on develop or the dev project: production has no EZD-294 yet (phase 4 PR not merged, `vault/handoff/CURRENT.md`). In a poisoned project, new walls show no number until the save answer arrives (`applySavedNumbers`), and their numbers fill from the lowest free one. Normal saves are unchanged, so the 300 ms Save budget is unaffected; a crafted save of many new objects past the bound costs one indexed scan of the key's rows per object.

None.

# EZD-368 · Fix: Fit to screen for a view-only member gives the same zoom as the editor view (EZD-207b B3)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-368-1 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:848`); re-proves AC-EZD-207-8 (`:787`, as read by `05-screens.md` Q-0630 row 9)
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** testing, ui
- **User-visible result:** nothing changes on screen: a view-only member's Fit to screen already gives the editor's zoom, because both now have the 56 px rail; the phase 4 full gate's B3 check is corrected to that value.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

**Cause (found from merged code, no app defect):**
- B3 (`app/e2e/plan-zoom-hover-text.spec.ts:357-382`) expects Fit ppi `1472 / 120` (line 381). That value is the Fit zoom with no rail on screen: canvas region width `1600 − 2 × 16 = 1568` (`04-app-shell-and-global-ui.md:7`, body padding 16), minus `2 × FIT_MARGIN_PX` (`48`, `app/src/editor/plan/view.ts:22`; `fitView` `:78-96`) = `1472`, over W1's 120 in (`addW1`, spec `:107-127`).
- EZD-210b (a34868ee) gave editors the rail and moved B1's Fit value to `1400 / 120` (spec `:313`): `1568 − 56` (rail, `04:7`; `--ez-rail-width: 56px`, `app/src/styles/tokens.css:34`) `− 16` (body gap, `04:7`; `--ez-body-gap`, `tokens.css:33`; `EditorFrame.module.css` `.body` `gap`) `= 1496`; `1496 − 96 = 1400`. B3 kept 1472 because a view-only member then had no rail.
- EZD-208b (d660c58c) put Select on the view-only rail, as decided: `05-screens.md` Q-0630 row 9 ("Select shows on their rail"; "no tools" reads "no drawing tools"); code `editorRail` returns `SELECT_ONLY` for ready without `canEdit` (`app/src/editor/selection/selection-controller.ts:358-368`); docs `### Drawing tools (EZD-210)` bullet "Select only without Edit model"; already pinned for a viewer by EZD-207a B4 (`app/e2e/plan-canvas.spec.ts:321-326`, rail 1, tool `select`). The viewer's region is now 1496 px wide like the editor's, so Fit gives `1400 / 120`. EZD-208b's plan E4 (`vault/plans/EZD-208b.md:111`) said "B3 values unchanged" and missed that B3's Fit value depends on the rail.
- So the app is right and line 381's number is stale (ticket Scope: "if the app is right and the number is stale, raise it to the reviewer"). The fix is a planned test edit (E1), written by the test-author and checked by the code-reviewer at the test review (PROCESS.md section 8: a structural repair may not change an expected value, so this is an E row, as EZD-210b's E2 and EZD-208b's E3/E4 were). Same assertion, same tolerance (3 places): not a weakening (CLAUDE.md rule 16).

# EZD-370 · Fix: the secret-key client list matches its users after EZD-5601 (EZD-323 T8)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-370-1
- **Complexity:** low
- **Areas:** security, testing
- **User-visible result:** nothing on screen changes; the phase 4 gate's secret-key check passes again, and the one new use of the secret key (the once-a-minute sweep that re-encrypts stored AI keys) is recorded as an accepted use.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
Finding (gate-failures.log line 7-8, develop 63e5c705): EZD-323 T8 expects 6 non-test `app/src` files naming `createJobsDbClient` and finds 7. The seventh is `app/src/server/jobs/ai-key-rewrap.ts` (added by EZD-5601, cc1832c1; it calls `createJobsDbClient()` at line 26). Planner grep at plan time (`grep -rln createJobsDbClient app/src`, test files excluded) lists exactly the 6 pinned files plus that one.

Decision: the use is needed, so the T8 list adds it with its reason (ticket row option 1). Grounds:
- `public.user_ai_key` grants select/insert/update/delete to `service_role` only and revokes all from `anon` and `authenticated` (`supabase/migrations/20261110120001_create_user_ai_key.sql` lines 33-34; EZD-5601 M1). A publishable-key client reaches no row of it.
- The rewrap runs inside `GET /api/jobs/sweep` (`app/src/app/api/jobs/sweep/route.ts` line 35), a Vercel Cron call with no user session, and must reach every tenant's stale rows: Q-0638 (decisions `05-screens.md` row Q-0638: "Key rotation rewraps every row before the old value is removed"). The per-user definer `rewrap_my_ai_key` is executable by `authenticated` only and takes user and tenant from the claims (`20261110120003_create_user_ai_key_functions.sql` lines 217-218), so it covers rewrap on use (Q-0637, decisions `10-permissions-and-settings.md` row 56) but never a key nobody uses.
- The sweep route is the job runner, not a user request path (`route.ts` header lines 2-3; docs/architecture.md `## Server-only data access and can()`: secret key "used only in job handlers ..."). docs/architecture.md already records "The sweep runs `rewrapStaleAiKeys()` ... with the runner's client" (line 992), so no doc edit.
- EZD-5601's plan section 7 (line 158) asked its security-reviewer to confirm "rewrap runs in the sweep with the secret key"; its STATUS row records review r2 PASS. This ticket's security-reviewer confirms it again (section 7), which AC-EZD-370-1 requires.

No app code changes. The only edit is the test file, which the builder never edits (CLAUDE.md rule 5), so the test-author makes it and the builder only runs the verification.

# EZD-372 · Fix: the long-tasks-during-pan perf check still fails at random on a lane gate (desktop, 1 long task)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-372-1
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** tooling, scripts, testing
- **User-visible result:** none in the app; the gate's pan long-task check stops failing at random when the Mac is busy, and any task it still cannot explain carries its trace evidence in the results file.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## Evidence (planning session, 2026-11-10)
- **E-1** The red run: `.claude/worktrees/EZD-367/perf-results/latest.json`, `runAt` 2026-11-10T18:22:45.902Z (EZD-367 lane 1 gate, gate.log:11477). Row `long-tasks-during-pan` (desktop, rate 1): value 1, `details.tasks` = `[{at:16763, ms:50, cpu:null, gc:null, top:null}]`, 149 waits (every one `cpu` 1-2, `ms` 50-249, mostly `FireAnimationFrame`), `load1` 9.84; the last wait is at 17,711 ms, against the 3,008 ms gesture (docs/architecture.md, Performance check, Benchmark pan). `:ipad` passed (1 wait).
- **E-2** Every pan row with `details.waits` in `perf-results/history.jsonl` of the main checkout and 12 worktrees (46 desktop records) was read this session. The task in E-1 is the only `cpu: null` task. Every other task matched a trace slice, including two other `ms` 50 tasks in the same run (at 1032 and 16297).
- **E-3** Code: `attributeTasks` (scripts/perf/trace-tasks.mjs; EZD-359 D-Attr (4)) takes only top-level slices with `dur > 50000` µs that start within 3 ms of `at`. The Long Task API lists tasks over 50 ms by Chrome's own task clock, and `ms` is `Math.round(duration)` (scripts/perf/pan-script.mjs), so an `ms` 50 task lasted 50.0-50.5 ms by that clock. A `cpu` null task counts (fail closed, Q-0621, Q-0622).
- **E-4** The trace of E-1 is gone. The gate copies back only `latest.json`, `history.jsonl` and `bundle-report.md` (scripts/gate-user.mjs `copyBack`, `PERF_FILES`; EZD-354 D12), and none of them holds trace events.
- **Cause (inferred from E-1 to E-3; the trace cannot confirm it, E-4):** the task sat on the 50 ms line. The API measured it just over 50 ms; the trace measured its slice at 50,000 µs or less, so the `dur > 50000` filter dropped the only slice that was the task. This is the one cause that fits all of E-1 to E-3: the miss is at the smallest `ms` the API can list, the start window worked for 148 tasks in the same run, and the trace still holds events after the miss. The record cannot rule out two other causes: the slice starting more than 3 ms after `at`, or no slice at all (a hole in the trace). D-Match closes the 50 ms line and stays fail closed for both of the others. D-Miss makes any later miss show which one it was, from the trace, in `latest.json` (ticket Scope: "find the cause from the trace").

## 1. What to build

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `scripts/perf/__tests__/trace-tasks.test.mjs` (test-author) | change | two new `describe` blocks, section 4 V1-V5, M1-M4; header comment gains the line `// EZD-372 V1-V5, M1-M4 (vault/plans/EZD-372.md section 4): the 50 ms line and miss evidence.` | the existing `EZD-359 trace attribution` block in the same file | `node --test scripts/perf/__tests__/trace-tasks.test.mjs` (V1, V2, M1-M4 red before Step 3) |
| 2 | `scripts/perf/__tests__/pan.test.mjs` (test-author) | change | edits E1-E3 (section 4) | the same file | runs in the gate `test` step (Chromium cannot start in the unit sandbox) |
| 3 | `scripts/perf/trace-tasks.mjs` | change | new `export function describeMisses(events, tasks)` (section 3); `attributeTasks` gets D-Match; private `topLevel(thread)` (D-Shared); JSDoc per D-Text | `attributeTasks` in the same file | `node --test scripts/perf/__tests__/trace-tasks.test.mjs` all green |
| 4 | `scripts/perf/pan-script.mjs` | change | `runPan` result gains `panMisses` (D-Wire); import list gains `describeMisses`; header comment gains one line (D-Text) | the `panWaits` line in the same return | `pnpm run typecheck`; gate `test` step (E1-E3) |
| 5 | `scripts/perf/check.mjs` | change | `panInput` case `'long-tasks-during-pan'`: `details` = `{ profile: name, tasks: pan.panTasks, waits: pan.panWaits, load1: pan.load1, misses: pan.panMisses }` in that key order | the same object | gate `test` step (E1) |
| 6 | `docs/architecture.md` | change | section `Performance check (EZD-017)`, bullet `Long tasks (G5)`: append the D-Text doc sentence after its last sentence | none | `node vault/tools/outline.mjs docs/architecture.md --section 'Performance check (EZD-017)'` shows it |
| 7 | none (runs) | none | D-Runs | EZD-359 D-Runs | T-AC |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Order | Tests (Steps 1-2) first, then Steps 3-6, then a ticket gate. In that ticket gate only, a red other than V/M/E rows: `PLAN-GAP` with `gate-failures.log`. After that, D-Runs (its own rule for other failed steps). Steps 3-5 are written before any D-Runs gate; no code changes during D-Runs | rule 5; EZD-359 D-Order |
| D-Match | In `attributeTasks` step (4), a slice is a candidate when `Math.abs((e.ts - anchor.ts) / 1000 - t.at) <= 3` **and** (`durOf(e) > 50000` **or** `durOf(e) >= (t.ms - 3) * 1000`). Everything else in D-Attr stays: the nearest start wins (ties: earlier `ts`), then `cpu`, `gc`, `top` from that slice. Why this is never weaker: a slice that starts within 3 ms of the task and lasts at least `ms - 3` overlaps the task for at least `ms - 6` ms (44 ms or more, since `ms` ≥ 50). Top-level slices on one thread run one at a time, so that slice is the task's own, and its `tdur` is the task's CPU time, as D-Attr (5) already defines. The 3 ms is D-Attr's window (the rounding of `at` and the gap to the mark), and `ms` is rounded the same way. For `ms` ≥ 54 the second clause adds nothing the first does not, so longer tasks match as today | E-3; EZD-359 D-Attr (4), (5); Q-0073 (a); ticket Scope ("do not change the budget or weaken the check") |
| D-Shared | Move the expression `outermost(thread.filter((e) => e.ph === 'X' && catOf(e).split(',').includes('toplevel')))` into a module-private `function topLevel(thread)`. `attributeTasks` calls `topLevel(thread)` and then filters per task with D-Match (the old `.filter((e) => durOf(e) > 50000)` on the list goes). `describeMisses` calls the same `topLevel` | lesson EZD-147 (one extraction, not two copies) |
| D-Miss | `describeMisses(events, tasks)`, pure; never throws on arrays. (1) It returns one entry per input task with `cpu === null`, in input order; a task with any other `cpu` gives nothing. (2) The anchor A is the first event with `name === PAN_START_MARK`. With no anchor, the entry is `{ at, ms, anchor: false, events: events.length, near: [] }`. (3) With an anchor, the thread is the events with A's `pid` and `tid`. Slices = `topLevel(thread)`. `lo = A.ts + (t.at - 20) * 1000`, `hi = A.ts + (t.at + t.ms + 20) * 1000`. A slice is near when `e.ts < hi && e.ts + durOf(e) > lo`. (4) Keep the 10 near slices with the smallest `Math.abs(e.ts - A.ts - t.at * 1000)` (ties: earlier `ts`), then sort them by `ts` ascending. (5) Each slice becomes `{ dt: Math.round((e.ts - A.ts - t.at * 1000) / 100) / 10, dur: Math.round(durOf(e) / 100) / 10, tdur: typeof e.tdur === 'number' ? Math.round(e.tdur / 100) / 10 : null }` (ms to one decimal). (6) The entry is `{ at: t.at, ms: t.ms, anchor: true, events: events.length, near }`. Key orders are exactly as written | E-4; ticket Scope; the 20 ms reach is planner's choice: wide enough to show a start slip several times the 3 ms window, small enough to stay a short list |
| Miss window and cap | 20 ms either side, 10 slices; constants are module-private `MISS_REACH_MS = 20` and `MISS_MAX = 10` (not exported) | D-Miss |
| Which tasks | `describeMisses(events, split.counted)`: only counted tasks can have `cpu` null (D-Split puts null in `counted`) | trace-tasks.mjs `splitTasks` |
| D-Wire | pan-script.mjs: `const attributed = attributeTasks(events, raw); const split = splitTasks(attributed, profile.cpuThrottleRate);` (replacing the one-line `split`), then in the result, after `panWaits: split.waits,` add `panMisses: describeMisses(events, split.counted),`. No other field changes. On a failed trace `events` is `[]`, so every counted task becomes `{ anchor: false, events: 0, near: [] }` | pan-script.mjs `runPan`; EZD-359 D-Trace |
| Error rows | `panInput`'s error and `unexpected` branches are unchanged (no `misses`) | check.mjs `panInput` |
| Rounding and -0 | No `-0` handling: `latest.json` is written with `JSON.stringify`, which writes `-0` as `0`; no section 4 fixture gives `-0` | check.mjs results writer |
| D-Text | trace-tasks.mjs: the file's first comment line gains `EZD-372: the 50 ms line (D-Match) and miss evidence (D-Miss).` The `attributeTasks` JSDoc text `from the trace's top-level task within 3 ms of \`at\`` becomes `from the trace's top-level task that starts within 3 ms of \`at\` and lasts over 50 ms or at least \`ms\` − 3 ms (EZD-372)`. `describeMisses` JSDoc: `EZD-372 D-Miss: for each task with cpu null, whether the trace has the pan-start mark, its event count, and up to 10 top-level tasks within 20 ms of it (dt, dur, tdur in ms to one decimal).` pan-script.mjs header gains `// EZD-372: each counted pan task with no CPU time carries its trace evidence (panMisses).` Doc sentence (Step 6): `A pan long task matches the trace's top-level task on the main thread that starts within 3 ms of it and lasts over 50 ms or at least its own length less 3 ms; \`details.misses\` lists each counted pan task with \`cpu\` null, with \`anchor\` (the trace holds the \`ezd-pan-start\` mark), \`events\` (the trace's event count) and \`near\` (up to 10 top-level tasks within 20 ms of it, each \`dt\`, \`dur\` and \`tdur\` in ms to one decimal) (EZD-372).` Nothing else | lessons EZD-152, L-030, L-039 |
| D-Runs | After the ticket gate is green, run the gate until 10 counting gates in a row, at most 14 gates in all (the green ticket gate is run 1). Each gate is its own Bash call: `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/gate.mjs <this worktree>`, timeout 1800000 ms, on the lane the launcher gave the unit (`EZD_LANE` 1-3; unset or `0`: stop before run 1 with `PLAN-GAP`, because the AC names lane gates). Before each gate, record `date -u +%s000` as `since` and D-Busy as `start`; after it, record D-Busy as `end`. A gate **counts** when `end` shows another lane busy, `gate.log` has the line `=== perf: pnpm run perf ===`, the gate summary has `results    pass`, and `perf-results/latest.json` has `runAt` after `since`. # EZD-373 · Fix: the plan draws no text on CI, so 9 browser tests fail only on CI

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-373-1
- **Complexity:** medium
- **Areas:** ci, testing, ui
- **User-visible result:** room labels and dimension numbers appear on the floor plan on any computer or tablet that lacks the Arial font (Linux, the CI machine), not only on Macs and iPads.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

**Cause (found at plan time, sources in section 2).**
1. `app/src/styles/fonts.ts` loads both fonts with `next/font/local` and no `adjustFontFallback`, so Next adds a metric-matched fallback face per font whose only source is `local(Arial)` (R-060 point 8). The built CSS in `app/.next` holds `@font-face{font-family:dmMono Fallback;src:local(Arial);…}` and `@font-face{font-family:instrumentSans Fallback;src:local(Arial);…}`, and the variables read `--ez-font-mono: "dmMono", "dmMono Fallback", monospace` (read 2026-11-10 from the local build output).
2. `createGlyphAtlas` (`app/src/editor/plan/glyph-atlas-canvas.ts:64-83`) passes the whole variable to `document.fonts.load('400 40px "dmMono", "dmMono Fallback", monospace')`. Chromium's `FontFaceSet::load` rejects as soon as one matched face fails (R-060 point 1). On Linux, `local()` matches only an installed full or PostScript name, with no alias such as Liberation Sans (R-060 point 4). The Ubuntu runner and Playwright's Ubuntu deps install no Arial (R-060 points 5, 6). So on CI the load rejects, the controller reports `plan.glyph_atlas` (`controller.ts:405-416`), `atlasSet` stays false, and `glyphs` stays 0.
3. The 9 tests started failing together. Develop CI was last green on EZD-205b (run 42270896570). The next product push was EZD-207b, which added the atlas (94299813; its run 42277742601 was cancelled), and every run since has failed (A3-regressions.md A3.1). EZD-120c B1's one extra request matches `/api/` traffic from the atlas error report: the Sentry tunnel is `app/src/app/api/monitoring/route.ts`, and the test counts every `/api/` request (`e2e/editor.spec.ts:109-115`).
4. This is an app bug a user's device can hit. Any browser without a font named Arial gets no plan text. The fix goes in the app (ticket row: "Fix the app when the app is wrong"), not in `.github` or the gate.

**Fix:** the atlas loads and draws only the first family of each font variable, which is the woff2 file the app ships (11 Performance rule 8). A fallback face that cannot load can then never stop the atlas. This closes the whole class (CLAUDE.md rule 18): any non-first face, on any device.

### Build steps

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/src/editor/plan/glyph-atlas-canvas.test.ts` (test-author) | change: add a second top-level `describe('EZD-373 glyph atlas font loading')` with U1-U5 (section 4); the EZD-207b describe stays unchanged | none | the same file's `fake()` helper for the canvas; `vi.stubGlobal` as in `app/src/editor/selection/SelectionLayer.edit.test.tsx:74`, with `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals())` | `pnpm --dir app exec vitest run src/editor/plan/glyph-atlas-canvas.test.ts` (U1-U5 red, EZD-207b U6, U7 green) |
| 2 | `app/e2e/plan-text-fallback-font.spec.ts` (test-author) | new: `test.describe('EZD-373 plan text without the fallback fonts')` with F1 (section 4) | none | `app/e2e/plan-zoom-hover-text.spec.ts`: copy lines 22-23 (`EDITOR`), 25-31 (`fixtureS`), the `Window2`/`PlanHook`/`EditorHook` types (35-61, the fields used), `editorState`, `planCanvas` (63-64), `openReady` (68-72), `stat` (74-75), `floorId` (98-107), `addR1` (130-159), and the `afterAll` (251-257). Imports, nothing else: `import { CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION } from '@ezdraft/geometry';` `import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';` `import { cleanup, closeHarness, createMember, createTenant, expect, setPermissions, test } from '../test-harness/e2e/test';` `import { seedFixtureS } from '../test-harness/projects-fixture';` (`signInAs` is the harness fixture argument). Head comment "Copies of plan-zoom-hover-text.spec.ts helpers (EZD-207b)" | `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-373 e2e/plan-text-fallback-font.spec.ts` (F1 red before step 3) |

After "(no font file URL)" insert: "; only the first family of each variable is loaded and drawn, never the `local(Arial)` fallback faces `next/font` adds (EZD-373)" | none (one inserted clause) | `node vault/tools/outline.mjs docs/architecture.md --section 'Plan canvas (EZD-207a)'` shows the clause |

AC-EZD-373-1 is met when gate.log's test:e2e part passes and none of the 9 tests in section 4 row "CI" is listed failed |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where to fix | `createGlyphAtlas` only. `fonts.ts` stays as is (keeping its fallback metrics for page text), and `.github/` and `scripts/gate.mjs` are not touched | ticket row Scope; CLAUDE.md rule 18 (build system frozen); section 1 Cause 4 |
| What the atlas loads and draws | the first family of each variable, for both `document.fonts.load` and `ctx.font`. `drawGlyphAtlas` gets the first families in `families`, so the drawn font string equals the loaded one | Cause 2; 11 Performance rules 4, 8; P207b C5 |
| `firstFontFamily` rules | Trim leading whitespace. If the next character is `"` or `'`, return the text through the matching closing quote, quotes included. With no closing quote, return `''`. Otherwise return the text before the first comma, trimmed. Empty or all-space input, or a list that starts with a comma, returns `''`. No other parsing (no unescaping) | CSS `font-family` list syntax; both quote styles appear in `app/.next` output (Cause 1) |
| Missing first family | rejects `Error('font variable missing: <variable name>')`, the existing text, before any `document.fonts.load` call | `glyph-atlas-canvas.ts:70`; P207b C5 |
| A first family that fails to load | still rejects with that load error, unchanged; the controller still reports `plan.glyph_atlas` once (P207b C13). No retry, no catch-and-continue | P207b C5, C13 |
| Order of loads | `ATLAS_FONTS` order (mono 400, then sans 600), one `await` each, as today | `glyph-atlas-canvas.ts:41`; EZD-207b U6 |
| A message to the user when the atlas fails | not built here. Q-0692 (open, Josh's design question) decides it; the ticket row's Scope and Done-when name no message (CLAUDE.md rule 4) | QUESTIONS.md Q-0692; phase-04.md EZD-373 row |
| The 9 CI tests and their expected values | unchanged; no skip, no retry, no timeout change | ticket row; CLAUDE.md rule 16 |
| Logging | no new log, report or `console.*` | ARCH Errors and logging (check C8) |
| F1's missing-font condition | an init script that adds `new FontFace(family, "local('ezd373-no-such-font')")` to `document.fonts` for `'dmMono Fallback'` and `'instrumentSans Fallback'`, with no descriptors. These are the same family names and default descriptors as Next's faces (Cause 1), so the faces join the families the old code loads. The script only constructs and `document.fonts.add`s the two faces. It never calls `face.load()`, so nothing in it can reject. The faces load, and fail, only when a `document.fonts.load` names their family: the atlas in the old code, or F1's self-check | Cause 1, 2; R-060 point 1 (load starts the matched faces' loads) |

# EZD-374 · Fix: the pan and load perf checks fail on CI (plan_not_ready, EZD-207c P2 pan counts)

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-374-1
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** ci, testing, scripts, tooling, docs
- **User-visible result:** the CI check on develop measures the plan's pan and load speed again instead of reporting "plan not ready", and the perf tool's own pan test stops failing on the CI machine.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

**Cause (found at plan time; sources in section 2).**
1. *plan_not_ready is the EZD-373 cause.* `runPan` waits up to 30 s (`PLAN_READY_MS`) for `[data-testid="plan-canvas"][data-plan-state="ready"]` and `window.__ezdraftPlan.stats().glyphs > 0`, else returns `plan_not_ready` (`scripts/perf/pan-script.mjs:19-21, 125-139`; EZD-207c D-Wait). The pan page `/dev/benchmark-plan` takes that branch (`page.tsx:18` `data-perf-wait-plan`) and builds its text with the same `createGlyphAtlas` (`BenchmarkPlan.tsx:17`). On CI that call rejects and glyphs stay 0 (P373 Cause 2), so every pan and load row is `plan_not_ready` (A1-tickets.md phase 4 row 1). EZD-373's fix makes glyphs > 0 on any machine. No perf-tool code changes for this; B1 (section 4) proves it on the Mac.
2. *The P2 count depends on the machine's CPU load.* The iPad long-task rows use `ipad-1x` at rate 4 (`registry.mjs:26-33`, `perf.config.mjs:25-32`). A task counts when `cpu × 4 − ms × 3 > 50` (`trace-tasks.mjs:93-100`; Q-0623 (a)). The throttle's spin counts as CPU, so a 200 ms busy wheel task (`pan.test.mjs:15-18`) scores `200 − 4p`, where p is the time the OS takes the thread off the CPU. It turns into a "wait" at p ≥ 38 ms: Q-0623's own cost line, "P2 goes red when one iPad task is preempted >= 38 ms". The root `test` script runs 4 files at once (`package.json` `--test-concurrency=4`; Q-0114) on CI's 4-vCPU public-repo runner (`ci.yml:20` `ubuntu-latest`; ARCH line 1430 "public repo"). Several perf test files beside it launch Chromium. CI counts 4 or 5 on the iPad row while desktop holds 8 (A1 row 2), and that fits preemption: the desktop row needs p > 150 ms. This is inferred, not measured. The CI logs show only `4 !== 8`, and P2 prints no task detail, so P2 gains diagnostics (step 2).
3. *Why the fix is isolation.* With a share f of off-CPU time, the iPad score of any busy task is about `W(1 − 4f)`. No fixture length keeps it over 50 once f nears 25%. The rule (Q-0623) and the budgets are fixed by the ticket row. So the only robust fix is that nothing else runs beside the pan fixture test. It runs alone after the other repo tests (CLAUDE.md rule 18: close the class).

# EZD-375 · Fix: an angled wall shows its length 1/2 inch short after rounding

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-375-1, AC-EZD-375-2
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** geometry, testing
- **User-visible result:** a wall typed 12' 6 1/4" at 45° now shows 12' 6 1/2" in the typed dimension bar, and an angled 11' 11 3/4" wall shows 12' 0", instead of half an inch short.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build
One changed line plus one private constant in `packages/geometry/src/length.ts` (`formatLength`), and new tests in three existing test files. No data, no migration, no schema change, no new export.

Cause (checked by the planner on develop 5a679b59): the bar shows `formatLength(lastLength, PLAN_DISPLAY_DENOMINATOR)` (`TypedEntryLayer.tsx` `TypedBar`, line 51), where `lastLength` is `wallLength` (a `Math.hypot`) of the drawn end points (`drawing-controller.ts` `finishStep`, line 443; ends from `wall-chain.ts` `typedAt` via `resolveTurnDirection`). From (150, 0) at 45°, a typed 150.25 gives 150.24999999999997, and `Math.floor(inches * d + 0.5)` (`formatLength`, line 73) drops the exact half. The same loss hits 09j row 11 (143.75 → 143.74999999999997 shows `11' 11 1/2"`).

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `packages/geometry/src/length.test.ts` (test-author) | change: append one top-level `describe('EZD-375 display rounding margin', …)` after the last one | none (tests L1-L5, section 4) | the file's own `test('T13 plan display (1/2")', …)` case-table loop | `cd packages/geometry && pnpm exec vitest run src/length.test.ts` (L1, L2, L3, L4b, L5 fail before step 4) |
| 2 | `app/src/editor/tools/drawing-controller.test.ts` (test-author) | change: append one top-level `describe('EZD-375 typed angled wall length', …)` after the last one; add `formatLength`, `parseLength`, `PLAN_DISPLAY_DENOMINATOR` to the existing `@ezdraft/geometry` import | none (tests D1, D2) | the file's own D5 (`setup`, `click`, `send`, `ev`, `walls`, `near`, `pt` already in the file) | `cd app && pnpm exec vitest run src/editor/tools/drawing-controller.test.ts` (D1, D2 fail before step 4) |
| 3 | `app/src/editor/typed-entry/TypedEntryLayer.test.tsx` (test-author) | change: append one top-level `describe('EZD-375 typed bar rounding', …)` after the last one | none (test M1) | the file's own M2 (`layer`, `textOf`, `STUB` already in the file) | `cd app && pnpm exec vitest run src/editor/typed-entry/TypedEntryLayer.test.tsx` (M1 fails before step 4) |
| 4 | `packages/geometry/src/length.ts` (builder) | change: add the private constant and its comment above `function gcd`; change line 73 only | none new; `formatLength(inches: number, denominator: DisplayDenominator): string` unchanged; module-private `const DISPLAY_ROUNDING_MARGIN_IN = 1e-6;` (not exported) | `packages/geometry/src/rooms/area.ts` `AREA_ROUNDING_MARGIN_SQ_IN` and `roomAreaSqFt` (margin added before the half-up floor) | the three commands above pass; `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/geometry test`; `cd app && pnpm exec vitest run src/editor src/lib/conflicts src/lazy/template-picker`; `pnpm run typecheck`; `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/gate.mjs <worktree>` |

### Decided for the builder

| --- | --- | --- |
| Where the fix goes | `formatLength` only. `lastLength` stays the raw `wallLength` (never rounded); `TypedBar`, `DrawingTools.tsx`, `drawing-controller.ts`, `wall-chain.ts`, `turn.ts` unchanged | ticket row Scope (names `length.ts:73`); 03g (computed coordinates are not rounded; display never changes the stored value); C6 `DrawingUi.lastLength` (P210b) |
| The new line 73 | `  const n = Math.floor((inches + DISPLAY_ROUNDING_MARGIN_IN) * d + 0.5);` | `area.ts` `roomAreaSqFt` (`+ AREA_ROUNDING_MARGIN_SQ_IN` before the floor) |
| The constant and its comment, exact text, placed directly above `function gcd` | `// EZD-375 (vault/plans/EZD-375.md): added before the half-up floor so float noise in a computed length (an angled wall's hypot) cannot drop an exact half (09j row 12; 03g); far below 1/64" (03g), so no real length moves.` then `const DISPLAY_ROUNDING_MARGIN_IN = 1e-6;` | CLAUDE.md rule 2; comment style of `area.ts` lines 24-26 |
| Margin size: 1e-6 inch, not `COMPARISON_TOLERANCE_IN` (1/64") | 1/64" moves real values: `formatLength(150.03, 16)` would give `12' 6 1/16"`, failing EZD-201 T14 (`12' 6"`), and `formatLength(150.2499, 2)` would give `12' 6 1/2"`, against Q-0207 "nearest 1/2"" (150.2499 is nearer 12' 6"). 1e-6 is above float noise for any model coordinate (ulp of 1e5" is 1.5e-11) and changes only values within 1e-6" below a half step. ### Do not touch
- Every other line of `length.ts` (`parseLength`, the shapes, `gcd`, the text building), its exports and `packages/geometry/src/index.ts`.

Ticket row, copied from `vault/tickets/phases/phase-04.md`:
- **Scope:** Defect found by the build audit calc-auditor (2026-11-10, A1-tickets.md phase 4, 209-1 row): the typed dimension bar shows the length worked out from the drawn end points (wallLength, a hypot, app/src/editor/tools/drawing-controller.ts:443) through formatLength, and packages/geometry/src/length.ts:73 rounds with Math.floor of inches times the denominator plus 0.5 with no allowance for floating-point error. A wall typed 12 ft 6 1/4 in from (150, 0) at 45 degrees has length 150.24999999999997 and shows 12 ft 6 in, against 09j row 12 and 03g (a halfway value rounds up: 12 ft 6 1/2 in). 724 of 9,620 start and angle pairs on the 1/2 inch grid show the wrong length. TypedEntryLayer.test.tsx:71 passes the exact 150.25, so the hypot path is never tested. Allow the same comparison tolerance the geometry package uses elsewhere (EZD-357 precedent) and add a test that drives the drawn end-point path.
- **Done when:** A wall typed 12 ft 6 1/4 in at 45 degrees from (150, 0) shows 12 ft 6 1/2 in in the typed dimension bar. Every other typed-length row of 09j and 03g keeps its shown text.

# EZD-379 · Fix: the EZD-207b B2 hover test sees a React commit when another lane runs a gate

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-379-1
- **Complexity:** low (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, ui
- **User-visible result:** none on screen; the hover test stops failing at random when the build machine is busy, so Josh's builds stop stalling on it.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

**Finding (from merged code at develop 86303108, and the failing run):** this is a test structural repair, not an app defect.
- Failing run: EZD-372 g1 (2026-11-10T21:31Z). The failing assert is `app/e2e/plan-zoom-hover-text.spec.ts:353` (`commits - commits0`), Expected 0, Received 1. Source: the EZD-372 build session log `~/.claude/projects/-Users-josh-Projects-ezdraft/d248ebf7-78ab-417c-8a5b-abc7ea1cd8d3.jsonl`. The gate.log files of g1, g7 and g10 were overwritten; the EZD-372 STATUS note lists the 3 failing gates.
- Hover has no React path. `onHover` → `updateHover` → `scene.setHighlight` → `redraw` (`app/src/editor/plan/controller.ts:209-220, 475-478`). The cursor readout writes `textContent` directly (`app/src/editor/status/PlanStatus.tsx:254-262`). Spec 11 rule 4 (no React render per pointer move) holds.
- The commit B2 counts comes from the autosave of B2's own wall:
  - `addW1` → `sync.enqueue` → `schedule(debounceMs)`, with `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 2000` (`app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync.ts:62, 489-505`; spec 11 rule 1, "a few seconds after the last edit").
  - The save then sets `saving`, calls `onSaved` (`applySavedNumbers`), sets `failures: 0` and finally `saved` (`outbox-sync.ts:378-385, 418-428`).
  - Each of those sets re-renders the editor: `useConflictInputs` reads the whole sync state through `useSyncExternalStore` (`app/src/editor/conflicts/use-conflicts.ts:37-42`), and `SaveStateText` reads `status` (`app/src/editor/SaveStatus.tsx:14-15`).
  - B2 opens its window (`commits0`, line 348) about 1-2 s after `addW1` without waiting for the save. With no load, the window closes before the debounce fires (B2 takes 1.8 s in EZD-372's gate.log). Under load, the screenshots and in-page PNG decodes push the window past 2 s, so the save's commit lands inside it.
- B1 has the same exposure: `addW1` at line 268, window lines 295-317. It is fixed here in place (Decided D-B1).
- Step 1 (probe) re-checks this finding on fresh throttled runs before the fix is written (D-Find).

### Build steps
Order: test-author Steps 1-3; test review (code-reviewer mode 2); builder Step 4 (proof runs only; no file changes).

| 2 | `app/e2e/plan-zoom-hover-text.spec.ts` (test-author) | change | none; insert the D-Fix lines after line 329 (B2 `const w1 = await addW1(page);`) first, then after line 268 (B1 `await addW1(page);`), so both line numbers hold at develop 86303108; nothing else changes | `app/e2e/plan-canvas.spec.ts:276-278` | `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-379 e2e/plan-zoom-hover-text.spec.ts` as its own Bash call: 0 failed |

# EZD-380 · Fix: the EZD-133 W1 money-pages smoke test fails with ECONNRESET when another lane runs a gate

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-380-1 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:868`)
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, tooling, docs
- **User-visible result:** the money-hiding smoke check stops failing at random when two builds are checked at once, so builds stall less often; the app itself does not change.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

Cause (E1-E6 in section 2): the browser-test web server (`next start`, test only; production is Vercel, ARCH Hosting) closes an idle kept-alive connection 6,000 ms after its last response (Node 22: `keepAliveTimeout` 5,000 + `keepAliveTimeoutBuffer` 1,000). `captureTraffic`'s `route.fetch` (`app/test-harness/e2e/traffic.ts:160`) runs on Playwright's `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` (playwright-core 1.64.1 `lib/coreBundle.js:27702`). That agent keeps idle sockets until the server closes them (E4). A request sent on a socket idle for 5,996-6,000 ms gets `read ECONNRESET` (E4 reproduces it with no load). Load makes the 6 s boundary likely: slower responses make a page burst open more sockets, and that reaches sockets last used about 5.9 s before (E2). Not the database (the reset files are static chunks) and not the server start (E3). Fix: the test web server never closes an idle connection during a run, which closes the race for every client of that server (route.fetch, `page.request`, browsers). No retry (ticket row).

Order (D-Order): test-author steps 1-3, code-reviewer test review, builder steps 4-5.

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/e2e/web-server-keep-alive.spec.ts` (test-author) | new | none. Imports: `http` from `node:http`; `{ expect, test }` from `../test-harness/e2e/test`. One local function `getOnce(agent: http.Agent, url: URL): Promise<{ status: number; keepAlive: string \| undefined; reused: boolean }>` (D-Get). Tests K1, K2 (section 4) | `app/e2e/net-guard.spec.ts` (header comment, `node:` imports, harness `test`) | before step 3: `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/ui-run.mjs EZD-380 e2e/web-server-keep-alive.spec.ts`, K1 and K2 fail (D-Red) |
| 2 | `app/test-harness/e2e/harness-config.test.ts` (test-author) | change: the `webServer.command` line (now line 110) and one comment line above it | none | itself | before step 3: `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run test-harness/e2e/harness-config.test.ts` fails on that line |
| 3 | `app/playwright.config.ts` (test-author) | change: `webServer.command` only, plus one comment line above it (D-Comment) | none | itself | the step 1 and step 2 commands pass |
| 4 | `docs/architecture.md` (builder) | change: two bullets (D-Docs) | none | itself | `node vault/tools/outline.mjs docs/architecture.md --section 'Browser tests (EZD-016a)'` prints the new sentence |
| 5 | none (builder: merge develop, ticket gate, D-Runs) | runs | none | EZD-372 D-Runs | D-Runs result (T-AC) |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Who | Steps 1-3 are the test-author's: `.claude/hooks/guard-paths.mjs:28-30` counts `playwright.config.ts` as a test config, and the builder is refused test files (`:105`). Step 4 and the runs are the builder's. The builder changes no file but `docs/architecture.md` | guard-paths.mjs; EZD-021 plan (config edits by the test-author) |
| D-Order | Step 1 and step 2, then D-Red, then step 3 and both verify commands green, then the code-reviewer's test review (Stage 3 step 5). Then the builder: step 4, `git merge develop` into the worktree (L-053), one ticket gate, then D-Runs. No code or test change after the ticket gate | rule 5; L-053 |
| D-Red | Before step 3 the test-author runs both verify commands. It puts in its report the K1 line (received `timeout=5`), the K2 line (`reused` false) and the H1 line (old command string). If K1 or K2 passes before step 3, stop with `PLAN-GAP` and the output | rule 16; L-036 |
| D-Keep | Value `3600000` (ms). Above the longest run that can hold an idle socket: the CI job cap of 45 min = 2,700,000 ms (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:21-23`, runs take 17-19 min), the D-Runs per-gate cap of 1,800,000 ms, and the longest test timeout of 300,000 ms (`app/e2e/money-pages.spec.ts:66`). Below the overflow: Node arms `keepAliveTimeout + 1000` as a socket timer, and a timer over 2,147,483,647 ms is set to 1 ms. Passed as the `next start` flag `--keepAliveTimeout`, which takes an integer of ms (next 16.4.2 `dist/bin/next` start options, `parseValidPositiveInteger`). `pnpm start` passes it through (E5) | E5, E6; ci.yml; Node 22 `_http_server` (E6) |
| D-Cmd | Step 3 sets exactly `` command: `pnpm start -p ${web} -H 127.0.0.1 --keepAliveTimeout 3600000`, `` and changes nothing else in `webServer` (`url`, `cwd`, `reuseExistingServer`, `env` stay) | D-Keep |
| D-Comment | Step 1 header comment, exactly: `// EZD-380 K1, K2 (vault/plans/EZD-380.md section 4; AC-EZD-380-1). The test web server keeps idle kept-alive connections open for an hour (playwright.config.ts --keepAliveTimeout), so a client that reuses one after 8 s gets an answer on the same socket. Untagged, so desktop only.` Comment above the step 3 line, exactly: `// EZD-380: idle connections stay open for an hour, longer than any run (CI job cap 45 min), so the server never closes one that route.fetch or the browser is about to reuse (Node's 6 s close reset W1 with ECONNRESET).` Step 2's comment, exactly: `// EZD-380: the web server keeps idle connections for 3600000 ms (vault/plans/EZD-380.md D-Keep).` | L-030, L-039 (states only what step 3 enforces) |
| D-Get | `getOnce` calls `http.get(url, { agent }, cb)`. `cb` calls `res.resume()`. On `res` `end` it resolves `{ status: res.statusCode ?? 0, keepAlive: res.headers['keep-alive'], reused: req.reusedSocket }`. It rejects on `req` `error` and on `res` `error`. No timeout of its own: the 60,000 ms test timeout bounds it (`app/playwright.config.ts` `timeout: 60000`) | Node `http` API; E4 probe used the same calls |
| D-Agent | Each test makes one `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` (the same options as Playwright's fetch agent, coreBundle.js:27702) and calls `agent.destroy()` in `finally` | L-051 |
| D-URL | `new URL('/api/health', baseURL)` from the `baseURL` fixture, after `expect(baseURL).toBeTruthy()`. `/api/health` is the web server's own ready URL (`app/playwright.config.ts` `webServer.url`) and answers 200 on the gate's stack | `app/src/app/api/health/route.ts`; ARCH Browser tests (EZD-016a) |
| D-Idle | K2 waits 8,000 ms (`await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 8000))`) between its two rounds. The old server closes at 6,000 ms (E4: the free sockets were gone at 6,006 ms), and 2,000 ms of margin covers a late server timer under load | E4 |
| D-Project | Untagged, so it runs in `desktop` only; not named `perf-*` | ARCH Browser tests (EZD-016a) routing |
| D-Docs | (a) `## Tests`, Browser tests bullet: `web server \`pnpm start -p 3000 -H 127.0.0.1\`` becomes `web server \`pnpm start -p 3000 -H 127.0.0.1 --keepAliveTimeout 3600000\``. (b) `### Browser tests (EZD-016a)`, end of the **Config** bullet, add exactly: `The web server runs with \`--keepAliveTimeout 3600000\` (EZD-380): Node's default closes an idle kept-alive connection after 6 s, and a request on such a socket at that moment (route.fetch's keep-alive agent, under load) failed with ECONNRESET; an hour is longer than any run.` Nothing else in the file | L-055; EZD-152 lesson (docs restate the new rule) |
| D-Runs | After the green ticket gate (run 1), run the gate until 10 counting gates in a row, at most 14 gates in all. Each gate is its own Bash call: `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/gate.mjs <this worktree>`, timeout 1800000 ms, on the unit's lane (`EZD_LANE` 1-3; unset or `0`: stop before run 1 with `PLAN-GAP`, because the AC names lane gates). Before each gate, record D-Busy as `start`; after it, record D-Busy as `end`. A gate **counts** when `end` shows another lane `live` and `gate.log` has a line holding `✓` and `EZD-133 money pages › W1 no page shows a company cost name to a member without See company costs`. A gate that does not count is recorded and neither breaks nor extends the streak. **Stop at once with `PLAN-GAP`** and that run's D-Record, in any gate, counting or not, when `gate.log` has a line holding `✘` and `EZD-133 money pages › W1`, or any line holding `ECONNRESET`. Another failed test or step: record its name, go on (defect evidence for the report). 14 gates with fewer than 10 counting in a row: stop, `PLAN-GAP` with all D-Records. Never re-run a red to get green | AC-EZD-380-1; ticket row ("Do not add a retry"); EZD-372 D-Runs (14 cap, streak rule); rules 16, 17 |
| D-Busy | One Bash call, as in EZD-372 D-Busy: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),T="/var/folders/2t/t09425m57_g4jvd1l3z5wnj00000gn/T",own=Number(process.env.EZD_LANE\|\|0);for(const m of [1,2,3]){if(m===own)continue;let pid=0;try{pid=Number(fs.readFileSync(T+"/ezdraft-gate-lane"+m+".lock","utf8").trim())}catch(e){};let live=false;if(pid>0){try{process.kill(pid,0);live=true}catch(e){live=e.code==="EPERM"}}console.log("lane"+m,pid,live?"live":"idle")}'`. "Another lane `live`" = at least one `live` line | EZD-372 D-Busy; ARCH Build lanes (EZD-172) Gate lock; lock file seen at that path in this planning session |
| D-Final | The ticket is done only when the last gate of the series is green (rule 12). If the 10th counting gate is red on another test, run more gates (still within the 14) until one is green. None green by gate 14: `PLAN-GAP` | CLAUDE.md rule 12 |
| D-Record | One line per gate in the builder's report: run n, UTC start-end, D-Busy `start` and `end`, the W1 line (`✓`/`✘`/none, with its time), the summary `results` line, failing test names, counts yes/no | EZD-372 D-Record |

### Do not touch
- `app/e2e/money-pages.spec.ts` (W1 and W2 checks, title, timeouts; ticket row "the money-hiding check itself must stay as it is"); `app/test-harness/e2e/traffic.ts` (no `maxRetries`, no `connection: close`, no fetch options); `retries: 0` and `timeout` in `app/playwright.config.ts` (also EZD-379's Do not touch).
- `app/package.json` `start` script; `scripts/perf/check.mjs` (its own `next start` on 3200 + 10 n serves only the perf page loads; no reset was seen there, so it is out of this ticket's evidence); `scripts/gate-port.mjs` (`isLeftoverGateServer` still matches `/\b(next|pnpm) start -p \d+/` with the flag appended, so no change there).
- `vault/architecture.md`: the orchestrator re-copies it from `docs/architecture.md` after the merge (Q-0012 (b); docs/architecture.md:3).

Ticket row (phase-04.md): **Scope:** Defect found in EZD-372's D-Runs series (2026-11-10, gate 11, lane 2 with lanes 1 and 3 running gates): app/e2e/money-pages.spec.ts:63 (EZD-133 W1 …, @smoke) failed with ECONNRESET. On CI the same test times out (EZD-373 scope). Find whether the app server or the local database drops the connection under load (an app or server defect) or the test's setup races the server start; the money-hiding check itself must stay as it is. Do not add a retry. **Done when:** EZD-133 W1 passes in 10 consecutive lane gates while another lane runs a gate, with its checks unchanged. **Depends on:** EZD-133. **Spec ref:** rule 17 (gate defect, EZD-372 D-Runs 2026-11-10).

## 2. Sources
- Ticket row and AC: `vault/tickets/phases/phase-04.md` (EZD-380 row); `vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:868`. Spec: `vault/spec/sections/11-non-functional-requirements.md` Performance (the gate's checks bind every ticket; no budget is touched here). No decisions name this area (`tickets.json` `decisions: []`).
- Rules: CLAUDE.md rules 5, 12, 16, 17; guard-paths.mjs:28-30, 102-105.
- Evidence (planning session, 2026-11-10):
  - E1 `.claude/worktrees/EZD-372/gate.log` (gate 23:07:53Z, lane 2): line 11596 `✘ 11 [desktop] … W1 … (32.3s)`; 11604 `traffic read failed: GET /_next/static/chunks/turbopack-0hk-bigsin20q.js: route.fetch: read ECONNRESET` at `traffic.ts:241`; W2, the same function, passed in that run (`✓ 66`, 28.3 s); the only `[WebServer]` lines (11642-11644) are the start line and NO_COLOR warnings, so no server error was logged.
  - E2 the failing run's trace (`/Users/ezdraft/gate/lane2/tree/app/test-results/money-pages-…-desktop/trace.zip`, `0-trace.trace`): three `APIRequestContext.fetch` calls of the `/dev/perf-probe` burst (26,682 ms; `turbopack-0hk-bigsin20q.js`, `1tndo90x61r1g.js`, `0xjjainnwmgum.js`) failed together with `read ECONNRESET` at `TCP.onStreamRead`. That burst ran 18 fetches at once, with responses taking 39-85 ms. The last burst that needed that many sockets was `/dev/benchmark-plan` (20,663-20,791 ms), about 5.9 s earlier. Pages before it loaded every 0.5-0.7 s with responses of 2-30 ms.
  - E3 not a start race: Playwright's `webServer` waits for `/api/health` before any test (`app/playwright.config.ts` `webServer.url`), and gate.log lists 62 passing results on the same server before W1's `✘` line (11532-11595) and 3 after it, W2 among them (E1). Not the database: the reset files are static chunks.
  - E4 probe (`next start` from the main checkout's Nov 6 build on 127.0.0.1:3991, Node v22.23.3, `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true })`): responses carry `Connection: keep-alive`, `Keep-Alive: timeout=5`; the agent's free sockets stayed until 6,006 ms, then went to 0; a second round sent after 5,996-6,000 ms of idle got `ECONNRESET` on 1-4 of 4 requests, and from 6,001 ms on it got new connections and no errors (17 trials).
  - E5 probe with `--keepAliveTimeout 3600000` (`next start` and `pnpm start -p 3994 -H 127.0.0.1 --keepAliveTimeout 3600000`, which printed `$ next start -p 3994 -H 127.0.0.1 --keepAliveTimeout 3600000`): `Keep-Alive: timeout=3600`; rounds after 5,997, 5,999, 6,000 and 6,500 ms idle: 4 of 4 `reused`, no error. With 4 idle connections open, the server exited at once on SIGTERM.
  - E6 Node v22.23.3 internals (`process.binding('natives')`): `_http_server` arms `socket.setTimeout(keepAliveTimeout + keepAliveTimeoutBuffer)` (buffer 1,000 ms by default); `_http_agent` has a keep-alive-hint branch, but E4 shows idle sockets kept to the server's close. next 16.4.2 `dist/server/lib/start-server.js:233-234` sets `server.keepAliveTimeout` only when the flag is given.
- Code read on develop 86303108: `app/playwright.config.ts:135-163` (`webServer`), `app/test-harness/e2e/harness-config.test.ts:108-110`, `app/test-harness/e2e/traffic.ts`, `app/e2e/money-pages.spec.ts`, `scripts/gate.mjs:380-400` (lane ports are freed before e2e, so the gate always starts its own server with the flag), `scripts/gate-port.mjs:27-31`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:19-23`.
- L-055 grep (`git grep -e "pnpm start -p" -e "next start" -e keepAliveTimeout -e webServer` on 86303108, outside vault plans, research, handoff, lessons, snapshots and spikes): the command itself is at `app/playwright.config.ts:136`, `harness-config.test.ts:110` (H1) and `docs/architecture.md:1164` (D-Docs (a)); `scripts/gate-port.mjs:31` matches it by regex (Do not touch); `vault/architecture.md:830` is the orchestrator's copy; `scripts/perf/check.mjs:33, 300`, `app/e2e/production-build.spec.ts:109` and `sentry-stub-transport.ts:3` name `next start` in prose only.
- EZD-133 contract (`vault/plans/EZD-133.md` section 3): W runs `captureTraffic`, per-path `goto` and `networkidle`, 300,000 ms; this plan changes none of it.
- EZD-372 plan D-Runs, D-Busy, D-Record (method copied, cited by ID).
- Research: no report covers this ticket; no retriever was used.

Architecture: Browser tests (EZD-016a); Build lanes (EZD-172); Hosting

## 3. Interface contract
| Kind | Name or path | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| file | `app/e2e/web-server-keep-alive.spec.ts` | `test.describe('EZD-380 test web server keeps idle connections open', …)`; 2 tests: `EZD-380 K1 the test web server announces a one-hour keep-alive` and `EZD-380 K2 a connection left idle for 8 seconds is reused`; nothing else |

| command | D-Busy, D-Runs | AC proof; D-Record lines in the builder's report |

## 4. Tests
3 rows written by the test-author (2 new tests, 1 changed assertion) plus the AC run series.
| Test | AC | Type | Input | Expected value | Source of the expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| K1 | AC-EZD-380-1 | browser (desktop) | `getOnce(agent, /api/health)` once | `status` 200; `keepAlive` === `'timeout=3600'`. Old config: `'timeout=5'` (red) | D-Keep (3,600,000 ms / 1000); E4 (old), E5 (new) |
| K2 | AC-EZD-380-1 | browser (desktop) | same agent: round 1 = 4 `getOnce` calls in one `Promise.all`; wait 8,000 ms (D-Idle); round 2 = 4 more in one `Promise.all` | all 8 `status` 200; every round-2 `reused` === `true`. Old config: all 4 round-2 `reused` false (the server closed them at 6,000 ms) (red) | E4 (closed at 6,006 ms), E5 (reused after 6,500 ms) |
| H1 (edit, EZD-016d test) | AC-EZD-380-1 | unit (Vitest) | `harness-config.test.ts` existing config load | `expect(webServer.command).toBe(\`pnpm start -p ${web} -H 127.0.0.1 --keepAliveTimeout 3600000\`)`; the rest of the file unchanged | D-Cmd; L-021 (earlier test pins the edited value) |
| T-AC | AC-EZD-380-1 | gate runs | D-Runs | 10 counting lane gates in a row with the W1 `✓` line; no W1 `✘` and no `ECONNRESET` line in any gate; last gate green; D-Records | AC-EZD-380-1; D-Runs, D-Final |

H1 runs only in full scope (its describe is `EZD-016d harness config`, phase 0; ARCH Test scope (Q-0006)); K1, K2 run in every phase-4 ticket gate. Smoke: no.

None (no screen changes).

## 6. Proposed wording
None (no user-visible text).

## 7. Security review
security-review: no. The change is the loopback-only test web server's idle-connection timer (`-H 127.0.0.1`), a docs sentence and tests; no auth, permission, data access, money or API code.
Reviewers needed: code-reviewer yes · calc-auditor no · ui-verifier no · security-reviewer no.

## 8. Complexity and model recommendation
medium: three small edits, but the AC needs a series of 10-14 lane gates, and the builder must apply the D-Runs stop and count rules exactly. Test-author Sonnet 5.5; builder Sonnet 5.5.

## 9. Dependencies
- Row: EZD-133 (done). Missing from the row, all done: EZD-007f and EZD-016d (`playwright.config.ts`, `harness-config.test.ts`), EZD-163 (`traffic.ts`), EZD-172 (lanes, gate lock), EZD-364 (`gate-port.mjs`). EZD-016a is not needed (no visual checklist).

EZD-379's B2 flake can turn gates red; under D-Runs that does not stop the count, but D-Final needs one green gate. EZD-373 (CI timeout of W1, W2) is separate; this change does not touch its files. A run on a machine with a server already on the lane port (`reuseExistingServer` off only on CI) would use that server without the flag; the gate frees lane ports first (`scripts/gate.mjs:380-400`), so gate runs always start their own server.

# EZD-381 · Fix: the EZD-208b B9 hover test counts 14 React commits where 17 are expected after develop merges in

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-381-1
- **Complexity:** low (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, ui
- **User-visible result:** none on screen. The selection hover test stops failing at random, so EZD-212a (move and resize geometry) can merge and Josh's build moves on.
- Phase: 5 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-10 · Status: planned

## 1. What to build

**Finding (from merged code at develop 50330d9a and the failing run).** This is a test structural repair, not an app defect.
- Failing run: EZD-212a gate, 2026-11-10 17:35 (`.claude/worktrees/EZD-212a/gate.log:11471-11507`). B9 failed at `app/e2e/selection.spec.ts:602:39` with `Expected: 14`, `Received: 17`. So `before` was 14 and the count after the hover moves was 17: 3 commits landed in the window. The ticket title gives the two numbers the wrong way round; nothing below depends on that. The failure's trace stayed in `/Users/ezdraft/gate/lane1/tree/app/test-results/` (the ezdraft user's folder; no access, KNOWN-LIMITS "gate's checks run as the ezdraft user").
- Hover has no React path:
  - `onHover` → `updateHover` → `scene.setHighlight` → `redraw` (`app/src/editor/plan/controller.ts`, `updateHover` and `attachSurface` `onHover`).
  - In Select mode, the picker is a pure lookup (`app/src/editor/selection/selection-controller.ts`, `const picker`).
  - The only cursor listener, `PlanStatus`, writes `textContent` (`app/src/editor/status/PlanStatus.tsx`, `handle.onCursorChange`; same finding as EZD-379 section 1).
  - Spec 11 rule 4 (no React render per pointer move) holds.
- The 3 commits come from the autosave of B9's own `addSel` edit (3 objects):
  - `__ezdraftEditor.edit` → `store.applyEdit` → `onCommit` → `sync.enqueue` → status `pending` → `schedule(debounceMs)`, with `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 2000` (`app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx` test hook; `app/src/editor/editor-session.ts` `onCommit`; `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync.ts` `enqueue`; spec 11 rule 1).
  - The save then sets `saving`, calls `onSaved` (`store.applySavedNumbers`), sets `failures: 0` and finally `saved` (`outbox-sync.ts` drain loop).
  - Each set re-renders React: `SaveStateText` reads `status` (`app/src/editor/SaveStatus.tsx`), and `useConflictInputs` reads the whole sync state through `useSyncExternalStore` (`app/src/editor/conflicts/use-conflicts.ts`).
  - B9 reads `before` (line 600) without waiting for that save. When the steps between `addSel` (line 580) and line 600 take less time than the debounce plus the save's round trip, the save's commits fall inside the window.
