- **Diagnosis** (design step, from R-061, the merged code and Q-0623's own figures):
  1. *How the throttle works (R-061).* A throttler thread signals the page's main thread every 200 µs; the signal handler busy-waits on the wall clock for (rate − 1) × the wall time since the thread last resumed (run capped at 1,000 µs), so at rate 4 the thread spends 3/4 of its time spinning. The handler also runs on a thread blocked in a wait (`SA_RESTART`), the spin is main-thread CPU, and nothing makes up time the OS takes away. This matches the Q-0623 probe (a pure 100 ms wait shows cpu 76-78) and lesson EZD-359 (the POSIX throttle spins and does not suspend).
  2. *What D-Split then computes.* For a task with own work `o` ms that the OS takes off the CPU for a share `f` of its wall time, spin and run both lose that share, so `ms = 4o / (1 − f)` and `cpu = 4o`. D-Split's score `cpu × 4 − ms × 3` is then `4o × (1 − 4f) / (1 − f)`: it reaches 0 at `f = 0.25` for every task, however much work it does. For P2's wall-bounded 200 ms loop the score is `200 − 4p` with `p = 200f` ms preempted, under the line from `p = 38` (Q-0623 cost line), that is `f = 0.19`.
  3. *The count is not load sensitive.* The long-task observer still delivers the 8 wheel tasks: the desktop row (rate 1, `cpu > 50`, needs `p > 150` to miss) holds 8 on the same fixture run while the iPad row counts 4 to 6, on CI (`vault/plans/EZD-374.md` section 1 item 2, A1 row 2) and on the Mac (EZD-372 STATUS note, gate 4).
  4. *The fixture's margin cannot fix it.* A longer loop only moves P2's line from `f = 0.19` (200 ms) toward `f = 0.25`, and a loop that counts only its own running time scores the same `4o × (1 − 4f) / (1 − f)`. No fixture holds 8 once the Mac takes a quarter of the main thread.
  5. *The same flaw hides real app work.* Under that load an iPad pan task of any size becomes a wait and passes (fail open). Rule 18 asks to close the class, so the fix is in the rule, on the row the benchmark pan gates, not only in the fixture. That overrides Q-0623 (a): Q-0737.
- **Why option (a) is never weaker at idle** (code-bound step): on an idle Mac a throttled task with own work `o` has `ms = cpu = 4o`, so today's score is `4o` and it counts when `o > 12.5` ms; `countByCpu` at rate 1 counts when `tdur × 4 > 50`, that is `o > 12.5` ms. The line is the same; only the load sensitivity goes. With no trace, the row errors instead of counting less (D-NoTrace).

# EZD-389 · Every email a user's action sends also goes to that user

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-389-1, AC-EZD-389-2, AC-EZD-389-3 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:1040-1042`)
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** email, security, testing
- **User-visible result:** when Josh sends an email from EZ Draft (a client send, an invite, a resend, an owner-set password notice), he also gets a marked copy in his own inbox that he can forward if the recipient's copy lands in spam; emails the system sends on its own go only to their recipients.
- Phase: 5 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-11 · Status: questions
- Template: v2
- Plan step: code-bound

## Brief
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Plain words | Change the shared send helper `sendEmail` (`app/src/server/email/send.ts`, EZD-008a) so that each call names the user whose action sent the email, or names none for a system email (Q-0701). When a user is named, the switch is on and that user's address is not the recipient's, the helper sends that user a second message: the same email, marked as a copy of the one sent to the recipient, so they can forward it (Q-0701). With no user named (alert emails `app/src/server/errors/alert-email.ts`, Q-0067 (b); system notifications), only the recipient gets it (Q-0701). One switch turns every copy off when Josh lifts the rule (phase-02.md row EZD-389). The existing callers in `app/src/server/profile/profile.ts`, `app/src/server/assistant/user-key.ts`, `app/src/server/errors/alert-email.ts` and `app/src/server/jobs/handlers/notification-email.ts` each pass the acting user or none. The copy's marking (subject prefix and opening line) is new wording for Josh's approval (CLAUDE.md rule 3). The architecture note `### Email (EZD-008)` gains the rule. |
| ACs | AC-EZD-389-1, AC-EZD-389-2, AC-EZD-389-3 |
| Screens | none (server helper only; the copy has no screen, so no visual checklist and no EZD-016a dependency) |
| Tables | none |
| Routes | none (the routes that call the changed helpers keep their paths and responses) |
| Files (estimate) | 9 |
| Tests (estimate) | 15 |
| Split | no |

## 1. What to build
Ticket row (`vault/tickets/phases/phase-02.md:74`): Scope: in the shared send helper (EZD-008a, `app/src/server/email/`), every email sent because of a user's action (client sends, invites, resend, owner-set password notice and the rest) also sends that user a copy they can forward when the recipient's copy lands in spam. System emails with no acting user (for example cleanup_due) go only to their recipients. One switch turns the copy off when Josh lifts the rule. The planner settles how the copy is addressed and marked; any wording not on a mockup goes to Proposed wording for Josh. Done when: every email that a user's action sends also reaches that user as a copy they can forward; an email with no acting user goes only to its recipients; turning the switch off stops the copies. Depends on: EZD-008a. Spec ref: Q-0701; R26.

### Design decisions
Settled at the design step; the code-bound step turns each into Build steps and Decided rows against develop's code. Rows D3 and D11 rest on the recommended options of Q-0738 and Q-0739 (section 10); a different answer changes those two rows only.
| # | Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | How the copy is addressed | A second, separate `transport.send` call to the acting user's address alone; never Cc or Bcc on the recipient's message, so the recipient never sees the user's address and each message keeps one recipient. | ARCH Email "one recipient per call"; Q-0701 ("also goes to that user") |
| D2 | Order and condition | The recipient's message goes first. The copy is sent only when that send returned `ok: true`, because the copy says the email was sent; when the recipient's send fails there is no copy and the sender still has the link (Copy link rule). | Q-0701; Q-0035 (Copy link on every send, sent or failed) |
| D3 | How a call names the acting user | `SendEmailInput` gains a required field `sentBy: { email: string } \| null`: the acting user's sign-in email, or `null` for a system email. Required, so the type check refuses any caller that forgets it. | Q-0701; Q-0738 (a), answered-agent |
| D4 | No copy to oneself | No copy when `sentBy.email.toLowerCase()` equals `to.toLowerCase()` (no trim: `z.email()` already refuses an address with spaces, checked on zod 4.6.7): the password-changed and AI-key emails go to the user who acted (`profile.ts:80`, `user-key.ts:241`), so they keep sending one message. | Q-0701 (the copy exists so the user can forward the recipient's email) |
| D5 | Bad `sentBy` | A `sentBy.email` that fails `z.email()` refuses the whole call with `EmailInputError` before any send, as every other bad input does. | EZD-008a input checks; ARCH Email "Input checks (EZD-151)" |
| D6 | The switch | One exported constant `SENDER_COPY_ON = true` in its own file `app/src/server/email/sender-copy.ts`, read by `sendEmail` on every call; `false` stops every copy. Not an environment variable: a code constant cannot differ between Preview and Production, needs no Vercel step from Josh (agents never change Vercel settings), and lifting the rule is a one-line reviewed change. Tests turn it off by mocking that module. | phase-02.md row EZD-389 ("one switch"); ARCH Email (agents never change Vercel settings); CLAUDE.md rule 18 (cannot drift) |
| D7 | What the copy keeps | The same From (with `company`, "<Company> via EZ Draft"), the same Reply-To (the company email), the same paragraphs, link, link label and `lang` as the recipient's message. | Q-0036; Q-0035 |
| D8 | How the copy is marked | Subject `office.email.copy_subject` (`Copy: {subject}`), and a first paragraph `office.email.copy_note` naming the recipient's address, before the original paragraphs; both through `getT('office', 'en')`, because the people who send emails use the office surface, which is English in v1. ### Behaviour per role
The helper has no role check of its own: the route or job that calls it has already decided the action is allowed (ARCH Server-only data access and can()). A role matters only as "whose action sent the email".
| AC | Role | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-EZD-389-1 | owner | (1) The owner does an action that emails someone else (owner-set password notice, invite). (2) The recipient's email is sent. (3) The owner gets the marked copy (D1, D2, D8). |
| AC-EZD-389-1 | office | (1) An office user sends to a client or resends an invite. (2) The recipient's email is sent. (3) The office user gets the marked copy. |
| AC-EZD-389-1 | field | Same as office for any field action whose route sends an email to someone else; a field user acting on their own account (password change) gets one email only (D4). |
| AC-EZD-389-1 | view-only | View-only users have no action that sends an email to someone else; their own password-changed or AI-key email reaches them once (D4). |
| AC-EZD-389-1 | no permission | The calling route refuses with 403 before `sendEmail` runs (EZD-102), so no email and no copy. |
| AC-EZD-389-2 | owner | An alert email to the owner (Q-0067 (b)) or a notification email carries `sentBy: null`: the owner gets that one email and nobody gets a copy. |
| AC-EZD-389-2 | office | Same: a notification email to an office user goes only to them. |
| AC-EZD-389-2 | field | Same: a notification email to a field user goes only to them. |
| AC-EZD-389-2 | view-only | Same: a notification email goes only to its recipient. |
| AC-EZD-389-2 | no permission | A person without an active membership gets no notification email at all (ARCH Notifications); nothing changes. |
| AC-EZD-389-3 | owner | With `SENDER_COPY_ON` false, the owner's sends reach only their recipients; no copy. |
| AC-EZD-389-3 | office | Same as owner. |
| AC-EZD-389-3 | field | Same as owner. |
| AC-EZD-389-3 | view-only | Same as owner. |
| AC-EZD-389-3 | no permission | Same as AC-1: no send, so no copy either way. |

# EZD-225 · Editor states

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-225-1, AC-EZD-225-2, AC-EZD-225-3, AC-EZD-225-4 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:1193-1196`, stage-0; AC-EZD-225-5 moved to EZD-122 as AC-EZD-122-10, Q-0697, Q-0700)
- **Complexity:** high (section 8)
- **Areas:** ui, testing, realtime
- **User-visible result:** When someone else holds the edit lock, the plan editor's drawing tools dim and pause with the note "Editing tools paused while view only" while Select still works; browser tests prove the loading skeleton, the Select-only rail without Edit model, the locked banner and the red door that reads "Not on a wall".
- Phase: 8 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-11 · Status: questions
- Template: v2
- Plan step: design

## Brief
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Plain words | Give a person who has Edit model but does not hold the edit lock the paused rail in the plan editor: drawing tools at 55% opacity and disabled, the note "Editing tools paused while view only", Select still working, drawing keys off, and no edits through the canvas or the inspector. Then prove four editor states with one browser spec: the skeleton while loading with tools disabled; no drawing tools and no Request edit without Edit model; the amber banner and the paused rail on a locked project; a click on a red door shows "Not on a wall" in the inspector. |
| ACs | AC-EZD-225-1, AC-EZD-225-2, AC-EZD-225-3, AC-EZD-225-4 |
| Screens | S03 Plan editor: the rail, the canvas state column, the inspector (read only). The amber banner, Request edit and the View only status item are EZD-126's and are reused unchanged. |

## 1. What to build

### Behaviour per role
Roles are the permission presets of `vault/spec/sections/10-permissions-and-settings.md:9-13`: Owner and Designer have Edit model; Foreman and Crew have View projects (own jobs) without Edit model. "view-only" below is any member with View projects and no Edit model; "no permission" is a member without View projects on the project, who gets EZD-120c's no-access state and never sees the editor (`app/src/editor/ProjectEditor.tsx` `editor-state` `no-access`). Lock holder: `LockState.holderId` equals the viewer (EZD-126 section 3, from EZD-125b).
| AC | Role | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-EZD-225-1 | Owner, Designer (Edit model) | 1. Open `/projects/[id]`. 2. While the model loads, the canvas skeleton shows and every rail tool, Select included, is disabled (S03:139; `editorRail` loading branch, `selection-controller.ts:366`). 3. When the model and the lock state have loaded, the rail turns to the holder state (all tools on) or the paused state (AC-EZD-225-3). |
| AC-EZD-225-1 | Foreman, Crew, view-only (no Edit model) | 1-2 as above. 3. When the model loads, the rail shows Select only, enabled (AC-EZD-225-2). |
| AC-EZD-225-1 | no permission | Never reaches the skeleton's ready state: the editor shows EZD-120c's no-access state and no rail (`editorRail` returns `null` for `no-access`, `selection-controller.ts:367`). |
| AC-EZD-225-2 | Owner, Designer | Not this AC: with Edit model the drawing tools show (holder: enabled; not holder: paused, AC-EZD-225-3). |
| AC-EZD-225-2 | Foreman, Crew, view-only | 1. The rail shows Select only; no drawing tool button is in the DOM (hidden, not greyed: Q-0214; Q-0697 05-screens). 2. The amber banner shows without Request edit (S06:75; Q-0697 10-permissions; EZD-126 `lock-request-edit` absent). 3. Click selects; box select, pan and zoom work (Q-0630 row 9; Q-0664 row "Views and permissions"). 4. The inspector shows the selection as read-only text (EZD-213b `view_only`; S06:100). 5. Drawing keys, Delete, Undo and Redo do nothing (S03:17; S06:82). |
| AC-EZD-225-2 | no permission | No-access state; nothing of the editor shows (EZD-120c). |
| AC-EZD-225-3 | Owner, Designer, not holding the lock | 1. Another user holds the lock. 2. The amber banner shows with Request edit (EZD-126). 3. The drawing tools show paused: 55% opacity, disabled, and the note "Editing tools paused while view only" shows (S06:48; S06 board line 93, 100; Q-0697 05-screens); where the note sits and whether Select dims too wait for Q-0740. 4. Select stays enabled and selects; pan, zoom work (S06:100). 5. Drawing keys, Delete, Undo, Redo, Duplicate, Copy, Paste do nothing; nothing is written to the model through the canvas, the empty-plan hint or the inspector (S03:143 "all edit tools disabled"; S03:17). 6. The inspector is read only (S06:100). 7. When the lock comes to this user (Start editing, EZD-126), the tools enable with Select active and the note goes (S06:78). |

A click on it selects it (Select works for everyone, Q-0630 row 9). 3. The inspector shows the Not on a wall block (EZD-213b, board S03dStates "Door no longer on a wall · clicked"); read-only for anyone without Edit model or the lock. |
| AC-EZD-225-4 | no permission | No-access state. |

### Failure and edge cases
| Function or action | Case | Behaviour | What the user sees |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rail state | model loaded, lock state not loaded yet (`LockState.loaded` false, EZD-126 section 3) | treated as loading for a viewer with Edit model: every tool disabled, no note (S03:139 "tools disabled until model loads"; no edit may start before the lock is known, S03:16) | skeleton gone, rail disabled, no note |
| Rail state | lock state loaded, viewer without Edit model | the lock state is not read for the rail (Select only, AC-EZD-225-2) | Select-only rail |
| Rail state | the canvas failed to start (`canvasFailed`) | unchanged from develop: the rail is disabled (`selection-controller.ts:368-369`) | EZD-120c's canvas error state |
| Lock lost while drawing | the holder changes while a drawing gesture or typed entry is open | the gesture is cancelled as Escape cancels it, nothing is committed, the active tool becomes Select, the rail turns paused (S03:143; Q-0630 row 36 Esc) | the preview disappears; paused rail and note; EZD-126's lock-lost banner |
| Lock lost while dragging a selection | the holder changes mid-drag | the drag is cancelled and the objects return to where they were; nothing is committed (S03:143); a save already queued is EZD-125's (refused with `stale_lock_epoch`, Q-0697 03-data-model) | objects snap back; paused rail |
| Lock gained | Start editing succeeds (EZD-126) | tools enable; active tool Select; note removed (S06:78) | full rail |
| Paused tool | click, tap or Enter on a paused button | nothing (the button is `disabled`) | no change |
| Drawing key | E, V, M, W, D, C, K, L, T while paused or without Edit model | ignored, no message (S06:82) | no change |
| Edit keys | Delete, Backspace, Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+D, Ctrl/Cmd+C, Ctrl/Cmd+V while paused | ignored (S03:17 Edit model "also requires holding the edit lock"; Q-0633 Copy hidden for view-only) | no change |
| Select keys | Esc, Ctrl/Cmd+A, Shift+click while paused | work as for a view-only user (Q-0630 row 9; Q-0633 Select more and Select all) | selection changes |
| Offline | the holder goes offline | keeps the lock (S03:142); tools stay enabled | full rail |
| Offline | a non-holder goes offline | stays paused; Request edit disabled is EZD-126's (S06:104) | paused rail |
| Two tabs | the holder opens a second tab | both tabs hold the lock, both have full rails (Q-0697 03-data-model "the lock is per user") | full rail in both |
| Inspector | a read-only user clicks a field | no input is rendered (EZD-213b view_only text) | plain text |

# EZD-390 · Fix: the EZD-299b conflict-list database test writes an error alert on CI without the alert lock

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-390-1 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:899`)
- **Complexity:** medium (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, ci, api
- **User-visible result:** none on screen; develop's CI gate stops failing on the conflict-list database test, and the server error that test set off on CI is found and fixed instead of being reported as a new error to Josh.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-11 · Status: planned
- Template: v2
- Plan step: code-bound

## Brief
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Plain words | On CI, the three EZD-299b conflict tests pass, but while they run one of the server routes they call writes an error alert (`POST /rest/v1/rpc/record_error_alert`) without the test holding the alert lock, so the EZD-252 guard fails the file. Find which call reported and why, fix that cause in the app so no error is reported, and keep the test's expected values unchanged. Holding the alert lock in the test is allowed only if the report is expected behaviour there, shown with a cited source. No retry is added (ticket row; CLAUDE.md rule 16). |
| ACs | AC-EZD-390-1 |
| Screens | none |
| Tables | none expected; `error_alert` is only the table the guard watches (`app/test-harness/errors/alert-write-guard.ts`). A migration is planned only if the cause is in a database function. |
| Routes | the five the test reaches through `routeFor` (`app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts`): `POST /api/projects/[id]/objects`, `POST /api/projects/[id]/sync-conflicts`, `GET /api/projects/[id]/model`, `GET /api/sync-conflicts`, `DELETE /api/sync-conflicts/[conflictId]`; only the one that holds the cause changes |
| Files (estimate) | 1 |
| Tests (estimate) | 4 |
| Split | no |

## 1. What to build

### Design (step design; Build steps, Decided and Do not touch below are the code-bound step)
The cause, found at this step (section 2 "Cause"), is in the test file's own harness, not in app code. The report is not expected behaviour: in production a request keeps its own cookies from start to end, so no production request goes through this path (section 2). Holding the alert lock would therefore hide a false alert, which the ticket row and rule 16 forbid. The fix changes only `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts`, which the test-author writes (CLAUDE.md rule 5). The builder writes no app code unless the P3 check in D-Prod finds an app defect.
| Design item | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Cookies | Each route call that `routeFor` makes runs with its own copy of that person's cookie map, held in a `node:async_hooks` `AsyncLocalStorage` for the length of the handler call. The `next/headers` mock reads and writes only that store. Outside a call it reads an empty map, never a shared mutable one. This ends both the cookie switch between A's and B's concurrent calls and the afterEach clear reaching a call still running. Built into Node, so no new dependency (rule 7). | cause steps 2-4 (section 2); `app/src/proxy.test.ts:5` (AsyncLocalStorage already used in a test) |
| D-Settle | `routeFor` records every handler call it starts in one pending set for the file. The file's `afterEach` waits until the set is empty (looping, because a settling call can start another: a list refresh re-runs, and `recordPending` deletes orphans) before anything else in the hook. So no route call is still running when the next test starts or when `afterAll` runs `cleanup()`. | L-051 (wait for every pending request before server state changes); cause step 4 |
| D-Expected | The three tests' expected values, inputs and assertions stay as they are. Only the harness lines (`routeFor`, the `next/headers` mock, `afterEach`) and the describe title (D-Scope) change. | AC-EZD-390-1; rule 16 |
| D-Lock | The test does not hold `holdErrorAlertLock`, and the guard (`app/test-harness/errors/*`) is not changed. | ticket row; rule 16; section 2 Cause |
| D-Scope | The describe title gains the ticket ID: `EZD-299b EZD-390 two people save one wall`. Phase scope runs only tests whose names hold a phase-4 ticket ID (`scripts/gate.mjs:84-86`), and EZD-299b is phase 3, so without the ID an EZD-390 lane gate skips the file and no gate counts toward the AC. The local lane gates on record show the file `3 skipped` (for example `.claude/worktrees/EZD-224b/gate.log:11672`). The `it` titles stay. | `scripts/gate.mjs:66-87`; AC-EZD-390-1 |
| D-Control | One new test in the same file proves the old harness fails and the new one passes (L-062): it holds a `GET /api/sync-conflicts` call open across the point where the old `afterEach` emptied the store, then expects that call's status and that no guard violation was recorded. The held await, the injected event and the expected values are in Decided D-Control and section 4 C1. | L-062; L-051 |
| D-Runs | The AC's run series (CI gate job on develop, plus 10 consecutive lane gates while another lane runs a gate) follows the EZD-380 D-Runs pattern (`vault/plans/EZD-380.md` D-Runs), with the counting line set to this file's passing line. The exact rules, including a series that ends short, are in Decided D-Runs and D-CI (EZD-359 lesson). | AC-EZD-390-1; `vault/plans/EZD-380.md:39` |
| D-Prod | Done at the code-bound step (section 2 "D-Prod result"). The planner read the pinned `@supabase/supabase-js` session path the session client uses for an RPC (the access-token read after `getClaims`). If an access token that expires between `getSession`'s `getClaims` (`app/src/server/auth/session.ts:19`) and its `current_app_user_id` RPC (`session.ts:22-23`) can send that RPC as anon in production, that is an app finding for the orchestrator under rule 17, not a change in this ticket. If it cannot, the plan says so with the source. | rule 17; rule 14 |

### Build steps
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts` (test-author) | change | none (a test file). Changes: the harness (D-Harness, D-Route, D-Settle), the describe title (D-Scope), two comments (D-Comment) and two new tests C1 (D-Control) and C2 (D-Control2), in the order of D-Red. File-local names: `cookieScope`, `pending`, `routeFor(cookies: Map<string, string>, calls: { method: string; path: string }[]): typeof fetch` (signature unchanged), `handle(input: unknown, init: RequestInit \| undefined, calls: { method: string; path: string }[]): Promise<Response>`, `settleRouteCalls(): Promise<void>`, nothing else (no other helper; C1's and C2's promises are written inline in the tests). New imports: `AsyncLocalStorage` from `node:async_hooks`; `alertWriteGuardState` from `../../../test-harness/errors/alert-write-guard` | `app/src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts` itself (the five-route `routeFor` body, lines 94-124); the held fetch spy from `app/src/server/auth/captcha.db.test.ts:163-166` | `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts` prints `Tests  5 passed (5)`; `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app run typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec eslint src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts` pass |

### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Who | Step 1 is the test-author's alone: the file is a test file, which the builder may not edit. The builder changes no file; its work, after the test review, is D-Merge, one ticket gate, then D-Runs (no Build steps row, because it writes no file). | CLAUDE.md rule 5; `vault/plans/EZD-380.md` D-Who (same split) |
| D-Red | Order inside step 1. (a) Add C1 (D-Control) and the `alertWriteGuardState` import, with the old harness lines still in place (`state.store`, the old `afterEach`). Run `pnpm --filter @ezdraft/app exec vitest run src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts -t 'EZD-390 C1'`. C1 must fail on `expect(b.status).toBe(200)` with a received value of 403 or 500 (403 when the held request is the `current_app_user_id` call and the second `getSession` then reads no cookies; 500 when the held request is a `getClaims` auth request, and then the guard message `error_alert written without holdErrorAlertLock` also prints). Copy the failing assertion line into the report. If C1 passes here, or fails in any other way (another assertion, another received value, or the 120000 ms timeout), stop with `PLAN-GAP` and that output (the control has not proved the old harness wrong; L-062). C2 is not run at (a): it calls `settleRouteCalls`, which the old harness lacks. (b) Make the D-Harness, D-Route, D-Settle, D-Scope and D-Comment changes and add C2 (D-Control2). Run the step 1 verify commands; all pass. | L-062; section 2 Cause steps 2-4; `app/src/server/permissions/context.ts:44-53` (second `getSession` per request; React `cache` is a pass-through outside a server-components request, `react` 19.3.1 `cjs/react.development.js:994-998`) |
| D-Harness | Replace `const state = vi.hoisted(() => ({ store: new Map<string, string>() }))` with `const state = vi.hoisted(() => ({ scope: null as null \| { getStore(): Map<string, string> \| undefined } }))`. After the imports and before `jarOver`, add `const cookieScope = new AsyncLocalStorage<Map<string, string>>();` and `state.scope = cookieScope;`. In the `next/headers` mock, `cookies` becomes an async function that first sets `const store = state.scope?.getStore() ?? new Map<string, string>();` and returns the same `getAll` and `set` bodies over `store` instead of `state.store`. `headers` stays `async () => new Headers()`. No other code reads `state`. | Design D-Cookies; `vi.hoisted` runs before the imports, so the store is set after them (`outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts:32-47`) |
| D-Route | `routeFor` keeps its signature. It returns a function `(input: unknown, init?: RequestInit)` that runs `const call = cookieScope.run(new Map(cookies), () => handle(input, init, calls));`, then `pending.add(call)`, then attaches one `settle` function that deletes `call` from `pending` with `call.then(settle, settle)`, and returns `call`; the whole function is cast `as unknown as typeof fetch` as now. `handle` is a new file-local `async function` holding the old body from `const url = …` to the `unrouted` throw, unchanged; the line `state.store = new Map(cookies);` is deleted. Each call copies the person's map (`new Map(cookies)`), as before, so a cookie a handler writes never reaches the person's saved map. | Design D-Cookies; old `routeFor` lines 94-124; `app/test-harness/errors/alert-write-guard.ts:114-119` (the same pending-set pattern) |
| D-Settle | `const pending = new Set<Promise<Response>>();` at file scope, next to `cookieScope`. `settleRouteCalls` loops: while `pending` is not empty, `await Promise.allSettled([...pending])`; when it is empty, wait `setTimeout` 50 ms and return only if `pending` is still empty, else loop again (no constant `while (true)`: use a `quiet` flag). The 50 ms check covers a refresh that is between its device-storage reads and its next request (`app/src/lib/conflicts/conflict-list.ts:186-198`); 50 ms is the file's own sync wait (`debounceMs: 50`, line 175). The describe's `afterEach` becomes `afterEach(settleRouteCalls, 30000)`. The describe's `afterAll` first awaits `settleRouteCalls()`, then the existing `cleanup()`, `closeHarness()`, `release()`, with hook timeout 60000. 30000 ms is two of the config's database-call timeouts (`app/vitest.config.mts:17`, `testTimeout: 15000`); 60000 is that plus the same again for the cleanup. | Design D-Settle; L-051; `app/test-harness/errors/vitest.setup.ts:31-35` (the guard's root-level hooks run after the describe's hooks, so settled calls are still checked) |
| D-Scope | The describe title becomes exactly `EZD-299b EZD-390 two people save one wall`. The three existing `it` titles stay. | Design D-Scope; `scripts/gate.mjs:84-86` |
| D-Control | New `it` as the fourth test (C2 is the fifth), title exactly `EZD-390 C1 a route call keeps its own sign-in while a signed-out call starts during it`, timeout 120000 (as T10-T12, lines 295, 338, 382). Body, in order: `const before = alertWriteGuardState().violations.length;` then `const origin = new URL(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL as string).origin;` then `const realFetch = globalThis.fetch;` then, written inline with no helper, `let markReached: () => void = () => {};` and `const reached = new Promise<void>((resolve) => { markReached = resolve; });`, then `let open: () => void = () => {};` and `const gate = new Promise<void>((resolve) => { open = resolve; });`, then `let held = false;`. Then `const spy = vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch').mockImplementation(...)`: the implementation takes `(input, init)`, reads the URL as `input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)`, and when `held` is false and the URL starts with `origin` it sets `held = true`, calls `markReached()` and awaits `gate`; in every case it returns `realFetch(input as RequestInfo \| URL, init)`. Then in `try`: `const bCall = routeFor(cookiesB, [])('/api/sync-conflicts');` then `await reached;` then `const out = await routeFor(new Map(), [])('/api/sync-conflicts');` then `open();` then `const b = await bCall;` then the four expects of section 4 C1, in that order. `finally`: `open();` and `spy.mockRestore();`. The held await is B's first request to the local Supabase origin; the injected event is the whole signed-out call, run to its answer while B's request is held. | L-062; section 2 Cause; `app/src/server/auth/captcha.db.test.ts:163-166` (spy with the real fetch kept); `app/src/server/auth/session.ts:12-28`, `:39-46`; supabase-js 2.118.0 `dist/index.mjs:261-264` (the client calls the global `fetch` at request time, so the spy sees it) |
| D-Control2 | New `it` as the fifth test, title exactly `EZD-390 C2 the hook wait ends only after a route call started by another one has answered`, timeout 120000. Body, in order: `let secondStatus = 0;` then `const first = routeFor(cookiesB, [])('/api/sync-conflicts');` then `const chained = first.then(async () => { await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10)); const res = await routeFor(cookiesB, [])('/api/sync-conflicts'); secondStatus = res.status; });` then `await settleRouteCalls();` then the two expects of section 4 C2, then `await chained;`. The 10 ms pause stands for a refresh's device-storage read between one request and the next (`conflict-list.ts:186-198`); it is shorter than the 50 ms quiet check, and Node runs the earlier-due timer first, so the second call is always in `pending` before the quiet check ends. | L-050 (a test the plausible wrong `settleRouteCalls`, one `allSettled` with no loop or no quiet check, fails); D-Settle |
| D-Comment | Add one header line after line 8: `// EZD-390 (vault/plans/EZD-390.md D-Harness, D-Route, D-Settle, D-Control; AC-EZD-390-1): each route call reads its own copy of the person's cookies, and every hook first waits for every route call to end.` Replace the comment above `routeFor` (line 93) with `// The route a person's fetch reaches: the handler for the method and path, under a copy of that person's cookies held for that call only (EZD-390 D-Route).` Nothing else: no other comment is added or changed. | L-057; L-034; rule 4 |
| D-Expected | No other line of T10, T11 or T12 changes: inputs, waits, expected values and the `list.dispose()` and `storage.close()` endings stay. | AC-EZD-390-1; rule 16 |
| D-Merge | Before the ticket gate the builder runs `git merge develop` in the worktree. The change reaches the gate's unit-test part only (vitest app project, database tests), plus typecheck and lint. | L-053 |
| D-Runs | After the green ticket gate (run 1), run the gate until 10 counting gates in a row, at most 14 gates in all (19 for the series that ran gates 1-12 on 2026-11-11: D-Resume). Each gate is its own Bash call `node /Users/josh/Projects/ezdraft/scripts/gate.mjs <this worktree>`, timeout 1800000 ms, on the unit's lane (`EZD_LANE` 1-3; unset or `0`: stop before run 1 with `PLAN-GAP`, because the AC names lane gates). Before every gate after run 1, run D-Wait; start the gate only when it exits 0. Before each gate record D-Busy as `start`, after it as `end`. A gate **counts** when `end` shows another lane `live` and `gate.log` has a line holding `✓ src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts (5 tests)` with no `skipped` on it. A gate that does not count is recorded and neither breaks nor extends the streak. **Stop at once with `PLAN-GAP`** and that run's D-Record when `gate.log`, in any gate, has a line holding both `FAIL` and `outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts`, or a line holding `outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts (5 tests` and `skipped` (the scope missed the file: D-Scope wrong). Another failed test or step: record its name, go on (defect evidence for the report). 14 gates with fewer than 10 counting in a row: stop, `PLAN-GAP` with all D-Records. Never re-run a red to get green. | AC-EZD-390-1; `vault/plans/EZD-380.md:39` (D-Runs, 14 cap, streak rule); EZD-359 lesson; rules 16, 17; the passing line format in `.git/ezdraft-tmp/ci42959076382/gate.log` |
| D-Busy | One Bash call, the EZD-380 D-Busy command exactly: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),T="/var/folders/2t/t09425m57_g4jvd1l3z5wnj00000gn/T",own=Number(process.env.EZD_LANE\|\|0);for(const m of [1,2,3]){if(m===own)continue;let pid=0;try{pid=Number(fs.readFileSync(T+"/ezdraft-gate-lane"+m+".lock","utf8").trim())}catch(e){};let live=false;if(pid>0){try{process.kill(pid,0);live=true}catch(e){live=e.code==="EPERM"}}console.log("lane"+m,pid,live?"live":"idle")}'`. "Another lane `live`" means at least one `live` line. | `vault/plans/EZD-380.md:40`; `scripts/gate.mjs:134` (lock path); lane 2 and 3 lock files seen at that path in this planning session |
| D-Wait | One Bash call, timeout 1900000 ms, the D-Busy lock check in a loop: `node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),T="/var/folders/2t/t09425m57_g4jvd1l3z5wnj00000gn/T",own=Number(process.env.EZD_LANE\|\|0),end=Date.now()+1800000;function live(){for(const m of [1,2,3]){if(m===own)continue;let pid=0;try{pid=Number(fs.readFileSync(T+"/ezdraft-gate-lane"+m+".lock","utf8").trim())}catch(e){};if(pid>0){try{process.kill(pid,0);return m}catch(e){if(e.code==="EPERM")return m}}}return 0}(function tick(){const m=live();if(m){console.log("lane"+m,"live");process.exit(0)}if(Date.now()>=end){console.log("no live lane after 1800000 ms");process.exit(1)}setTimeout(tick,60000)})()'`. It checks every 60 s for 30 min. Exit 0 (`laneN live`): start the gate. Exit 1 (`no live lane after 1800000 ms`): run no gate; stop with `STATUS: waiting for a busy lane`, all D-Records, the counting streak, the gates run so far and `git rev-parse HEAD`. That is not done and not a plan gap: the orchestrator dispatches the builder again for D-Runs only (D-Resume) when another lane is running a gate. Why: a gate with no other lane live cannot count (D-Runs) and spends a slot of the cap; gates 8-12 on 2026-11-11 ran that way (PLAN-GAP, builder report). | AC-EZD-390-1 ("while another lane runs a gate"); D-Busy; the wait command was run once in this plan-gap session (exit 1, lanes idle) |
| D-Resume | A resumed D-Runs keeps the streak and the gate count of the series before it when `git rev-parse HEAD` in the worktree prints the series' HEAD (for the 2026-11-11 series `5a0d7125a1a3c8ab43f30da70db3cc6d97846918`) and `git status --porcelain -- app supabase` prints nothing; it runs no D-Merge and no new ticket gate, and starts with D-Wait. Otherwise the series starts again from a new ticket gate (run 1) with a 14-gate cap and a streak of 0. The 2026-11-11 series: 12 gates, 7 counting in a row, every gate with the `(5 tests)` line and no `FAIL` line for the file; its cap is 19 gates in all, because gates 8-12 ran with no other lane live, which D-Wait now prevents, so they are left out of the 14-gate cap (14 + 5): 7 more gates for the 3 counting gates still needed, the same 4 gates of slack the 14 cap gives. The counting rule, the stop rules and the AC are unchanged; a gate on another commit never joins the streak. | AC-EZD-390-1; D-Runs; `vault/plans/EZD-380.md:39` (14 cap = 10 + 4 slack); rule 16 (no term redefined: idle gates still do not count) |
| D-Record | One line per gate in the builder's report: run n, UTC start-end, D-Busy `start` and `end`, the file line (`✓`, `FAIL` or none), the summary results line, failing test names, counts yes/no. | `vault/plans/EZD-380.md:42` |
| D-CI | The CI half of the AC is checked on the first CI `gate` run on develop that holds this ticket's commit (the phase 4 pull request, CLAUDE.md rule 11): its gate-logs artifact has the line `✓ src/lib/outbox/outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts (5 tests)` and no line holding both `FAIL` and `outbox-sync-conflicts.db.test.ts`. The builder cannot run CI, so this is the orchestrator's check at the phase 4 release (`vault/handoff/phase-4-release.md`, where the failure was found); a red there is a defect ticket (rule 17). | AC-EZD-390-1; CLAUDE.md rules 11, 17 |

### Do not touch
- `app/test-harness/errors/*` (the EZD-252 guard): no change, and no `holdErrorAlertLock` in this file (Design D-Lock).
- Every route and every `app/src/server/**` and `app/src/lib/**` source file: no app code changes (section 2 Cause; section 2 D-Prod result).
- In the test file: `jarOver`, `cookiesFor`, `wall`, `person`, `reload`, `save`, `objectRow`, `conflictRows`, `notificationCount`, `listFor`, `floorOf`, the `kickJobRunner` mock, the `beforeAll` and `beforeEach` hooks, and every line of T10, T11 and T12 (D-Expected).
- `scripts/gate.mjs` and `app/vitest.config.mts` (no scope or timeout change outside the file).

### Behaviour per role

# EZD-391 · Fix: the EZD-033 T13 sign-in throttle test counts 4 emails where 5 are expected on CI

- **ACs:** AC-EZD-391-1 (`vault/spec/acceptance-criteria.md:900`)
- **Complexity:** low (section 8)
- **Areas:** testing, auth, ci
- **User-visible result:** none on screen; develop's CI gate stops failing on the sign-in email throttle test (EZD-033 T13). The design step found no fault in the app: one email was never sent because the test spaced its requests too closely for Supabase Auth, so only the test changes.
- Phase: 4 · Planned by: planner · Date: 2026-11-11 · Status: planned
- Template: v2
- Plan step: code-bound

## Brief
| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Plain words | On CI, EZD-033 T13 asks for a sign-in email to one member's address 6 times. The app answers "code sent" to calls 1 to 5 and "too many emails" to call 6, as it should. But 3 seconds after the last call, the mail store holds 4 emails for that member, not 5. Find why one of the five "code sent" answers produced no email, and fix that cause. Two places can hold it. (1) Supabase Auth refused one send and the app hid the refusal on purpose (Q-0174 (a)). Then the fault is the test's spacing or wait, and the fix is a test structural repair through the reviewer (PROCESS.md section 8). (2) The email was lost or sent late in the app's own path. Then it is an app defect, fixed in the app. Keep the expected values unchanged. Add no retry. Do not make the fixed 3-second sleep longer as the fix (ticket row; CLAUDE.md rule 16). |
| ACs | AC-EZD-391-1 |
| Screens | none |
| Tables | none expected. `public.sign_in_throttle` (EZD-033) is only read by the test's helpers. `auth.users` send timestamps may be read by the test (design step). |
| Routes | none (server action `requestSignIn` in `app/src/server/auth/actions.ts`, called directly by the test) |
| Files (estimate) | 1 |
| Tests (estimate) | 3 |
| Split | no |

## 1. What to build
The design step decided the cause: case (1) of the Brief. It is lead (A) in section 2: the test's spacing, not the app. The change is a test-only repair of `app/src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts` (EZD-033 T13). No app file changes. The test-author makes the edit, and the code-reviewer confirms that no assertion or expected value changed (PROCESS.md section 8, "Structural test repair"; CLAUDE.md rule 5).

Design rule for the code-bound step: each send to one address waits `max_frequency` + 100 ms (`gap()`, `throttle.db.test.ts:166`), counted from the moment the previous `requestSignIn` call to that address **returned**, not from the moment it started. Auth records its send time while it handles call n (R-062: `time.Now()` is taken after the frequency check and before the SMTP send). That time is therefore no later than the moment call n returns. So call n+1's check at Auth comes at least 1,100 ms after Auth's stamp of call n, more than `max_frequency` = 1 s (`supabase/config.toml:236`), however slow the runner is. Keep unchanged: the expected values, `sleep(3000)` at `throttle.db.test.ts:280`, the loop order and the call count (ticket row; CLAUDE.md rule 16).

### Build steps
Code at develop 9fdf05f4. No `t/EZD-391` branch or worktree exists (checked 2026-11-11), so there is nothing stale to discard. There is one file row. The builder changes no file and runs D-Order, D-Runs and D-Green (Decided below, with the patterns of `vault/plans/EZD-379.md` D-Runs, D-Busy, D-Read and D-Records). The orchestrator runs D-CI after the merge.
| # | Path | New / change | Exports and signatures | Copy the pattern from | Verify with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `app/src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts` (test-author) | change | none exported (the file exports nothing). The module-local `async function spaced<T>(email: string, gapMs: number, send: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` replaces `spaced(email: string, gapMs: number)` (D-Helper). The 3 call sites change (D-Calls), T13's title gains `EZD-391` (D-Title), the line 8 comment is restated (D-Comment), and a new `describe` holds S1 (D-S1) | `app/src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts` (its own `spaced`, lines 151-159, and T13, lines 267-282) | `cd app && pnpm exec vitest run src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts` prints `Tests  10 passed (10)`; then `cd app && pnpm exec vitest run src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts -t "EZD-391"` prints `Tests  2 passed \| 8 skipped (10)` (the planner ran the second form with `-t "EZD-033 T13"` on the lane-0 stack at develop 9fdf05f4: `1 passed \| 8 skipped (9)`, 16.8 s); then `grep -c "gap())" app/src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts` prints `0` (no 2-parameter call is left; at HEAD it prints `3`, lines 211, 242, 273), and `grep -c "plus 100 ms\.$" app/src/server/auth/throttle.db.test.ts` prints `0` (the old line 8 is gone; at HEAD `1`). `spaced` has no copy in another file that this change must follow (planner lesson L-033) |
### Decided for the builder
| Choice | Decision | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-Who | The test-author makes the whole of Step 1. The builder edits no file: Step 1 is a test file, and the fix is a test structural repair. The code-reviewer confirms that no assertion or expected value of T11, T12 or T13 changed. | CLAUDE.md rule 5; PROCESS.md section 8, "Structural test repair" (`vault/PROCESS.md:276`); section 1 above |
| D-Helper | Replace lines 151-159 with exactly this text, laid out as Prettier formats it, and nothing else: `const lastSend = new Map<string, number>();` / `async function spaced<T>(email: string, gapMs: number, send: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {` / `  const last = lastSend.get(email);` / `  if (last !== undefined) {` / `    let wait = last + gapMs - performance.now();` / `    while (wait > 0) {` / `      await sleep(wait);` / `      wait = last + gapMs - performance.now();` / `    }` / `  }` / `  const out = await send();` / `  lastSend.set(email, performance.now());` / `  return out;` / `}`. There is no `try`/`finally`: a `send` that throws fails its test anyway, so the stamp after it is never read | section 1 design rule (stamp after the call returns); R-062 (Auth's stamp is taken before the call returns) |
| D-Clock | `performance.now()`, the global in Node 22, not `Date.now()`. It is a monotonic clock, so a wall-clock step during the run cannot shorten the gap. The `while` loop re-checks on that same clock after each `sleep`, so the gap holds even when a timer fires early | design rule (a bound that holds on any runner, section 2); CLAUDE.md rule 18 |
| D-Calls | T11 (lines 211-215) becomes `const before = new Date();` then `expect(await spaced(w.email, gap(), () => run(store, () => requestSignIn(form({ email: w.email }))))).toEqual({ resolved: { step: 'code' } });`. T12 (lines 242-246) is the same with `k.email`. T13 (lines 273-274) becomes `const out = await spaced(email, gap(), () => run(store, () => requestSignIn(form({ email }))));`, and the `expect(out, \`${i}\`)` line after it stays. Each is laid out as Prettier formats it. T11 and T12 send their first email to an address no earlier call used, so `spaced` waits 0 ms there, as it does today, and moving `before` ahead of the call changes nothing | `throttle.db.test.ts:211-215, 242-246, 273-277` |
| D-Title | T13's title becomes exactly `'EZD-033 T13 EZD-391 sign-in emails are throttled per email, the same for an unknown address'`. Without it, an EZD-391 ticket gate (phase 4 scope) skips T13: the gate's Vitest name filter is `EZD-(<phase 4 ids>)(?![0-9a-z])\|@smoke`, and EZD-033 is phase 0. Then no lane gate counts toward the AC. The local gate logs show the file `(9 tests \| 9 skipped)` (`.claude/worktrees/EZD-376/gate.log:11548`). No other title changes | `scripts/gate.mjs:85-87`; `app/vitest.config.mts:13`; `vault/plans/EZD-390.md` D-Scope (same fix for a phase-3 test) |

  - **How Auth decides (R-062; GoTrue v2.197.0, the image on the local stacks: `docker ps`, 2026-11-11):**
    - A new or unconfirmed user's email reads `confirmation_sent_at` (`sendConfirmation`). An existing user's magic link reads `recovery_sent_at` (`sendMagicLink`).
    - The check runs before the send. It refuses when the stamp + `max_frequency` is after the current time; this is a strict `After`.
    - The new stamp is `time.Now()`, taken after the check and before the SMTP send, and saved after the send.
    - A refusal is HTTP 429 `over_email_send_rate_limit`.
  - **How the app answers:** `requestSignIn` answers `{ step: 'code' }` and sends nothing for every 429 except `over_request_rate_limit` (`app/src/server/auth/actions.ts:173-185`; Q-0174 (a), `vault/questions/QUESTIONS-answered.md:463`).
  - **Why start-based spacing fails under load:** the gap at Auth between stamp(n) and check(n+1) equals 1,100 ms + (time from start(n+1) to Auth's check) − (time from start(n) to Auth's stamp).
    - It drops below 1,000 ms when call n's part before the stamp runs more than 100 ms longer than call n+1's part before the check.
    - That part is the app's `takeSlot` database round trip and the HTTP hop to Auth. For call 1 it also includes creating the auth user and running the before-user-created hook, because `createTestMember` makes no auth user (`app/test-harness/auth-users.ts:29-51`).
